# SIA-v6 — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-09 (Pass 2 refresh — code reads and suite
runs at the head below; this refresh supersedes draft PR #63, which
was verified at `a471608f` and predates PRs #66 and #67);
benchmark sections re-verified 2026-11-10 (D1 remediation pass —
full-suite run and a full real benchmark run at the head below)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 226ef50315c3a13c241952013c3e328ea024b1e7
(pre-remediation head; the D1 remediation lands on top of it)
**Evidence labels:** verified = proven in this pass by code read or
suite run · audit-measured = measured by the 2026-11-08 estate audit
(`sia-family.md`) · reported = claimed by a repo document, not
re-proven in this pass · contradicted = the evidence says otherwise.

## What this repo is

The SIA-v6 platform/shell: (a) a Python agent layer
(`sia-v6-platform/agent/` — paths A/B/C plus sovereign modules:
decision engine, oracle, proof-chain) with a divergent second copy
of the same tree inside `sia-v6-platform/dat1/`; (b) a FastAPI
utility service (`sia-v6-platform/tollbooth/`); (c) a benchmark
harness (`sia-v6-platform/benchmark/`); (d) one-shot generators
(`engines/`), generated artifacts (`artifacts/`), and a large body
of launch/sales documents. Per `ORGANISM_STATUS.json` (the repo's
own architecture statement), the runtime core is SIA-V6-CEROS, the
constitution is SIA-Foundry, and evaluation is Breakthrough-System.

This repo is one of two platform copies: it shares **134 identical
file contents** with `Savage-AI-style` (audit-measured 2026-11-08).
Neither copy is marked canonical in code; the canonical-copy
question is an open decision for Savage (fix-plan §9 decision 16).

## Component state

- **Agent layer (`agent/`)** — *verified.* Suite green (below).
  Paths A (ratchet), B (topology), C (RG flow), sovereign decision
  engine, oracle, and proof-chain all execute under test.
- **`dat1/` second copy** — *verified (as a divergence).* A
  divergent duplicate of the agent tree (fix-plan defect D4, open).
  The top-level `agent` package spans both trees via `__path__`
  extension (`agent/__init__.py`), with the canonical tree winning
  the three `shared/` collisions. Modules unique to dat1 (e.g.
  `agent.path_b.topology_agent_e10`) resolve from the dat1 tree.
- **DAT-8 harness (`dat1/test_dat8_harness.py`)** — *verified.*
  Since PR #67 the 20 certification checks are real parametrized
  pytest tests (BA/PB/SL/DB/CS/DC/LM) driven from a single registry
  shared with the standalone runner: **20 passed** under pytest and
  **20/20** in script mode. Before PR #67 it collected and ran zero
  tests (defect D5, closed by #67).
- **Persistence memory / E10 topology (`agent/path_b/`)** —
  *verified.* `PersistenceMemory.summary()` exists (PR #67) —
  `TopologyAgentE10.betti_1_onset()` and `composite_vector()`
  consume its `sign_change_rate` and `entropy` keys; the PB checks
  exercise `tick()` end-to-end. Before #67 the method was absent
  and every `tick()` raised `AttributeError`.
- **Tollbooth service (`tollbooth/main.py`)** — *verified surface.*
  Route surface read from code: POST
  `/api/v6/isomorphism`, `/conservation`, `/topology`,
  `/boltzmann`, `/oracle`, `/consensus`, `/finance`, `/physics`,
  `/swarm`, `/sca/converse`, `/admin/provision`; GET `/`, `/health`,
  `/api/v6/sentinel/status`. Suite state at the current head,
  measured 2026-11-10 in the pinned-dependency environment: the
  utility-products contract tests pass (**24 passed**), including
  the conservation payload3 non-finite case an earlier version of
  this file recorded as failing — that failure does not reproduce
  at this head, and the full platform suite is green (below).
  PR #66 (the D2 fix) is landed. Draft PR #55, which also
  addresses non-finite inputs, remains open.
- **Benchmark (`benchmark/`, `benchmark_output/`)** —
  *verified (remediated 2026-11-10).* The orchestrator was
  rewritten: every suite executes the system's own operations —
  the sovereign symplectic core, the shared proof chain, the RG
  flow engine, the topological memory and agent, the consensus,
  and the tollbooth's five metered utility endpoints — on inputs
  from the repo's own fixtures (`benchmark/corpus.py`: the agent
  test corpus extracted at runtime from its single source; the
  tollbooth contract-test payloads and exact transforms of them).
  No `_simulate_*` path remains, and no measured quantity is drawn
  from a random generator. Record verification is a real
  HMAC-SHA256 over each record's measured fields
  (`benchmark/integrity.py`; key derived from the run seed by a
  published derivation): it fails on a tampered field, a wrong
  key, or a malformed MAC, and the proof suite's declared tamper
  scenarios (5% of its scenarios) plus the healing suite's
  MAC-tamper family exercise the failure direction on every run.
  The committed artifacts are the output of a full real run
  (2026-11-10, run `035c76ec-696e-44a9-9174-0a1f953ea2ce`,
  seed 42): **1,000,000 observations executed in 666 s; mean
  score 97.47; certified 91.06%; gate status CERTIFIED WITH
  DEGRADATION.** Full CERTIFIED (≥95% certified) was not earned:
  the shortfall is the healing suite's 57.6% (only post-repair
  checkpoints can certify, by construction), the topology
  suite's 71.4% (the agent's acceptance gate does not reliably
  track the measured regime shift), and the Jacobian suite's
  90.0% (its 10% fault-injected scenarios score 0 — the fault
  signal, ~4e-3 against a ~1e-14 clean floor, is detected).
  Scope limits are stated in `benchmark/README.md`: the
  DB-backed products are exercised by the API suites, not this
  benchmark; the ten verticals are workload profiles over the
  one engine; healing certification certifies Hamiltonian
  restoration (the engine's repair contract), not byte-identity
  with the shadow core; `scoring.py`'s pre-existing Jacobian
  curve returns >100 for the cleanest measurements (max 103.5
  this run) and was left untouched. The pre-remediation artifact
  was fabricated (see "What is NOT true") and is retracted by
  replacement. Defect D1 (CRITICAL) is **closed** by the PR
  carrying this refresh. (PR #57 was a plan-only draft with zero
  changed files and is not benchmark remediation.)
- **CI** — *verified (files), reported (runs).* Workflow files
  exist (`.github/workflows/python-tests.yml`, added by PR #66,
  plus organism-status, organism-sync, shell-health, and a
  utility-products acceptance workflow). Whether Actions runs
  are green was not established in this pass.
- **TypeScript workspace** — *reported.* Audit ran `tsc` rc=0
  (2026-11-08); a frozen-lockfile install fails on a stale pnpm
  lockfile (audit-observed). Not re-run in this pass.
- **`engines/`, `artifacts/`** — *not graded in this pass.*
  One-shot generators and ~347 generated files; the audit read
  them for structure, not line-by-line (its stated coverage
  limit), and this pass did not extend that.
- **`ORGANISM_STATUS.json`** — *reported only.* Its automation
  has recorded subordinate `latest_sha` values as unknown; it is
  this repo's architecture statement, not cross-repo ground
  truth.

## How to verify (last run: 2026-11-09, this pass; benchmark
items re-run 2026-11-10)

Environment: venv with the repo's pinned dependencies
(`tollbooth/requirements.txt`: fastapi 0.115.0, pydantic 2.9.0,
numpy 1.26.4) plus pytest; TMPDIR on a workspace disk; commands
run from `sia-v6-platform/`:

- `python -m pytest -q` (full platform suite) → **259 passed**
  at the pre-remediation head; **271 passed** with the D1
  remediation (+12 new tests in
  `tests/test_benchmark_real_benchmark.py`; zero existing tests
  modified or weakened)
- `python -m pytest tests/test_benchmark_real_benchmark.py
  tests/test_benchmark_certification_gate.py
  tests/test_benchmark_empty_artifacts.py -q` → **18 passed**
- `python -m benchmark.run_benchmark --seed 42
  --output-dir ./benchmark_output` → 1,000,000 records in
  666.45 s; the generated report's gate reads **CERTIFIED WITH
  DEGRADATION** (mean 97.47, certified 91.06%)
- `pytest agent dat1` → **146 passed** (126 at the pre-#67 head;
  the +20 are the DAT-8 checks)
- `pytest dat1/test_dat8_harness.py` → **20 passed**; script mode
  (`python dat1/test_dat8_harness.py`) → **20/20**, exit 0
- `pytest agent/tests/test_cross_path.py` → **8 passed**
  (includes the determinism test — see "What is NOT true")

## What is NOT true

- **The old test counts in this file** ("49/49"; "122 pass /
  1 FAIL / 1 collection error") — stale; the counts above are
  the current measured state.
- **C1, the determinism warning this file carried:** "two
  identically-constructed RGAgent instances produce different
  proof_hash values" — **does not reproduce.** The cause was
  fixed in the tree (`agent/path_c/rg_agent.py` defaults
  `rng_seed: int = 0`); the audit's six standalone runs passed
  and this pass ran the cross-path suite 8/8. The historical
  lesson stands; the warning does not.
- **"This repo has NO CI checks at all"** (prior text) — CI
  workflow files exist since PR #66.
- **Any benchmark report predating the 2026-11-10
  remediation** — including the previously committed report
  (run `9ffd6ce1-052c-414f-b750-8ea142f285c3`, "CERTIFIED",
  mean 91.79 over 120,000 points): its inputs were simulated
  and its certification fabricated; no score from it should be
  quoted as measured engine performance. The current committed
  report (run `035c76ec-696e-44a9-9174-0a1f953ea2ce`) is a real
  measurement, and its status is **CERTIFIED WITH
  DEGRADATION**, not CERTIFIED — no stronger claim should be
  quoted from it either.
- **The launch posture of the ~85 launch/sales documents** —
  they assert a commercial state the code does not support
  (audit-verified). They are claims, not state.
- **Products ON now: 0 customer-usable** (audit-verified;
  unchanged — this pass found no deployment or customer-use
  evidence). The tollbooth service is the only self-contained
  deployable the audit found, endpoint-tested by it.
- **The prior location claim for a "benchmarks/million"
  harness** — no such path exists in the tree (verified again
  this pass); the withdrawal recorded in the prior version of
  this file stands.
- **`ORGANISM_STATUS.json` as cross-repo ground truth** — it
  is not (see above).

## Open defects and drafts (2026-11-09; D1/D2 lines updated 2026-11-10)

- **D1 CRITICAL** — benchmark evidence: **closed 2026-11-10**
  by the real-benchmark remediation (see Benchmark, above);
  the fabricated artifact was replaced by a measured run whose
  gate verdict is CERTIFIED WITH DEGRADATION.
- **D2 residue** — PR #66 landed the validation fix; the
  conservation payload3 case passes at the current head
  (measured 2026-11-10; full suite green). Draft PR #55 open
  on the same surface.
- **D3 MEDIUM** — canonical copy (this repo vs Savage-AI-style)
  unmarked in code; Savage's ruling required.
- **D4 MEDIUM** — `dat1/` duplication (above). Open.
- **D5 LOW** — DAT-8 harness: **closed by PR #67** (this pass).
- **D6 LOW** — this refresh: **closed by the PR carrying it.**
- Draft PR #63 (an earlier GT refresh at `a471608f`) is
  superseded by this file. Drafts #61/#62 (SDK hardening) remain
  open, unlanded.

## Recomputable Benchmark (SIA-E1, added 2026-11-11)

- **`sia-v6-platform/recompute/`** — verified (this pass): a
  receipt-bundle format (`savage/benchmark-recompute-bundle/1`)
  and a standalone recompute CLI. A harness run is sealed with its
  corpus commitment, run seed, per-item evidence, a hash chain and
  per-item run MACs; a third party holding only the bundle
  recomputes the headline exactly, or gets a MISMATCH verdict with
  the failing leg named. Reference run (seed 42, reduced budgets,
  2,600 items across all 10 suites): recompute MATCH, maximum
  score delta 0.0; derivation coverage reported per item — 1,840
  fully re-derived from measurements, 80 score-only, 680 bound
  (determinism_replay and adversarial_healing outcomes are not
  functions of the stored record; they stand as issued, sealed by
  chain + MAC, and are labeled bound, never re-derived).
- **Sabotage controls** — verified (this pass): five tamper
  variants of the reference bundle (measurement edit with the
  chain re-sealed, outcome flip, claimed-headline edit, dropped
  item, seed swap) all recompute to MISMATCH, each caught by the
  leg that owns it; the untouched control recomputes to MATCH.
  Pinned as regression tests in
  `tests/test_benchmark_recompute.py`.
- **Service proof outside the SIA family** — verified (this
  pass): savage-standard's own test suite (74 tests, main
  `c865a145`) was bundled through the generic pytest-junit adapter
  and recomputed to MATCH from its bundle alone; a flipped item
  outcome recomputes to MISMATCH.
- **Promotion gate** — the claim record for a recomputed score is
  gated by SIA-V6-CEROS's TriadicPromotionEngine (main); a score
  is a published claim exactly when the gate's signed receipt
  beside the claim record reads PROMOTE. Gate receipts from the
  reference runs are recorded in the SIA-E1 evidence filed with
  this change.
- **What is NOT true here**: the estate's previously published
  benchmark claim (1,000,000 observations, 91.06% certified) is
  NOT recomputable from its published artifacts — the certified
  manifest carries no per-item evidence and no run seed, so no
  MAC can be re-verified and no headline recomputed; only the
  publisher's aggregates can be re-averaged. Re-issuing that claim
  as a bundle requires a fresh sealed run at full budgets; it has
  not been done in this change. The savage-standard envelope was
  evaluated as the bundle's outer format and not used (its
  verifier executes zero legs for an unregistered dialect);
  registering a `benchmark-recompute` dialect there is the named
  SIA-E2 follow-up.

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims
without verification.

# savage-command-center-os — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-11 (fix #119 — queue row D2; census + diffs read in full, suite run on the exact PR head tree + pristine-master baseline control; no deployed-runtime validation). Prior: 2026-11-10 (fixes #92/#93 — queue rows D3 + D4). Prior full verification: 2026-11-03 (Tonight Sprint merge train).
**Canonical branch:** master (this PR is based on master @ 6421e0fb8d8d840c1612857e4af59eb9ccdfe95e)

## What this repo is

The implemented operator/UI donor for Savage Command Center — a
personal command-center PWA (self-use). Distinct from
**Savage-Command-Center**, the specification/document donor. This
repo also carries a `main` branch; the default/canonical branch is
`master`.

## Verified current state

- **Head (master):** `be88f72eeb0648e96f7132b14dcd8f3fd2cfb7ad` — squash merge of PR #31, completing the four-PR Tonight Sprint security train (#28–#31). Tree = 84 blobs.
- **Tests (Tights local run, 2026-11-03, dependencies installed):** **merged master: 81/81 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip** (baseline control on `f4a12a1b`: 59/59; PR heads: #28 66/66, #29 67/67, #30 63/63, #31 62/62). No compile step; `node --check` gates.
- **Security posture changed on master by PR #26** (Phase 2 Prompt
  6, diff read in full by the train): simulated connections ended,
  cached plaintext credentials removed from localStorage, CORS
  allowlist replacing `*`, fail-closed credential testers, no
  upstream error leakage. Those were exactly the audit's three
  findings against the pre-fix code (simulated connect, plaintext
  localStorage credentials, unauthenticated wildcard-CORS write
  proxies).

## Correction to the prior version of this file

The 2026-09-17 version's detailed state section described the
**working branch** `feature/savage-social-control-plane` — the
social control plane, its OAuth flows, its auto-seeded first-wave
briefs — as this repo's current state. Those claims describe that
branch, were not verified on `master` by the audit or this pass,
and are **not carried as current state**. Its cited slate
verification also pointed at a `savagnic/` path; the savagnic org
shows 0 repositories to the estate's token, so that citation is
unverifiable from here.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

- **#26** — into `master` (Prompt 6, above). Tree 75 → 77.
- **#24** — into the `main` branch (Android opt-in Shizuku shell
  bridge for Termux + remote-guard watchdog + handoff doc; opt-in
  only, CI green, diff read in full). Main branch tree 42 → 48.

## Merged in the 2026-11-03 Tonight Sprint train

- **#28** — squash-merged into `master` at `5f9050e0b5955afd985a32d76b2600b3e4b00fd2` (tree proof: PR paths blob-identical post-merge, 77 → 80 blobs, no other path changed). Independent server-only bearer authorization now required for `POST /api/decisions` and `PUT /api/organism-status` on canonical `master`, closing the source-confirmed unauthenticated mutation risk. Local loopback tests are not external Supabase acceptance: protected server-side `COMMAND_CENTER_WRITE_TOKEN` provisioning, Supabase RLS, and deployed-runtime verification remain mandatory before deployment. See `docs/WRITE_AUTH_BOUNDARY.md`.

- **#29** — squash-merged at `14b1dd807994f85d468598b3994bafb98c00bf01` (tree proof PASS, 80 → 82 blobs). Public GitHub intel no longer discloses private repository commits: privileged token removed from public intel, repository visibility verified without the token, private repositories filtered.
- **#30** — squash-merged at `91dd2d936e93dabaa2b334b1bad1daf036642e28` (tree proof PASS, 82 → 84 blobs). Social control plane now requires a dedicated operator bearer credential as the mounted default (fail closed); OAuth callbacks are admitted only when bound to an unconsumed operator initiation nonce. Known limitation carried from the PR: the browser obtains the raw authorization URL after operator authorization; self-use only.
- **#31** — squash-merged at `be88f72eeb0648e96f7132b14dcd8f3fd2cfb7ad` (tree proof PASS, 84 → 84 blobs). WebSocket workspace paths reject symlink components and root-targeting mutations. Carried limitation: path validation is not a race-free filesystem sandbox (TOCTOU under a same-user local process).

## Known defects / honest gaps

- Self-use only today: 1 product ON (personal command-center PWA).
  The audit's named route to a sellable console (wire the UI to the
  real connection testers — done in part by #26 — move credentials
  server-side, auth the API handlers) is days–weeks of work and is
  not finished.
- Deployed-runtime behaviour of either branch is not verified in
  this pass.
- Token provisioning for the new boundaries (`COMMAND_CENTER_WRITE_TOKEN`, `SOCIAL_CONTROL_TOKEN`) and deployed-runtime verification remain outstanding; the merged code fails closed until they are provisioned.

## Where it is going

No direction ruled by Savage for this repo.

## Fixes landed 2026-11-10 (queue rows D3 + D4)

- **D3 (fix #92) — GitHub intel default owner corrected.** The
  `GITHUB_OWNER` fallback in `api/github.js` (and its byte-identical
  `artifacts/agent-shell/` copy) defaulted to `savagnic` — an account
  that, as the correction section above already records, shows 0
  repositories to the estate's token. The default is now `sa6ag9`, the
  estate owner's GitHub login (the account this repo lived under
  pre-org-move and the owner the intel test suite itself uses). With
  `GITHUB_OWNER` unset, the handler now profiles `sa6ag9` out of the
  box; the env override is unchanged. Pinned by
  `tests/github-owner-default.test.mjs` (both handler copies, owner
  unset). Stale pre-move references in README.md / VERCEL_SETUP.md
  (`savagnic/` clone and import paths) were NOT touched by this fix
  and remain as historical text.
- **D4 (fix #93) — committed runtime log untracked.**
  `server_output.log` (403 bytes, blob
  `91d9f200d9aa00d07b0a497a5eef878bb6f12c86`) — a six-line local
  loopback access log — was tracked in the tree despite the existing
  `*.log` ignore rule. It is removed from the tree by this fix and
  named explicitly in `.gitignore` alongside `*.log`. Its content is
  not reproduced here. History is not rewritten: the log remains in
  prior commits, which is the recorded history of the defect.
- **Suite on this PR's head tree:** 83/83 pass, 0 fail (81 baseline
  on pristine master + 2 new owner-default pins); `node --check`
  clean on app.js and server.js.

## Fix landed 2026-11-11 (queue row D2)

- **D2 (fix #119) — duplicated API artifacts de-duplicated.** The
  tree carried the Vercel API layer twice: the live `api/` (+ root
  `vercel.json`) and a snapshot bundle under `artifacts/agent-shell/`
  (`api/` + `vercel.json`). Census of the bundle against the
  canonical copies, by blob and by diff:
  - `connections.js` — DIVERGENT: pre-#26 generation (wildcard CORS,
    no integration-ID validation, a generic fallback answering
    `ok: true` "Credentials stored" for connectors with no real
    tester — the simulated-success behavior #26 ended canonically).
  - `decisions.js` — DIVERGENT: pre-#28 generation (no
    `requireWriteAuthorization` gate, wildcard CORS).
  - `organism-status.js` — DIVERGENT: pre-#28 generation (no
    write-auth gate on `PUT`, wildcard CORS on all methods).
  - `github.js` — byte-identical duplicate (blob `f9effe6abc`).
  - `vercel.json` — same routes, formatting-only divergence.
  Canonical evidence: root `vercel.json` routes `/api/*` to `api/`;
  the hardening trains landed on `api/` only (#26 `e30a0625`,
  2026-11-01; #28 `5f9050e0`, 2026-11-04), while the bundle's
  divergent trio was last substantively touched 2026-09-30; the
  bundle has no `_write-auth.mjs` counterpart at all. Fix #92 above
  records the cost of the duplication: it had to edit the
  `artifacts/agent-shell/` copy of `github.js` alongside the live
  one to keep them in step (that D3 note now describes an archived
  snapshot).
- **Disposition (archive, never delete):** the five bundle files
  moved byte-for-byte to `archive/agent-shell-bundle/` (git records
  renames; blob SHAs unchanged) with a census README there, and a
  pointer README at `artifacts/agent-shell/` naming the canonical
  locations. Nothing was deleted. The archived generation's only
  unique material is the pre-hardening behavior #26/#28 deliberately
  removed; it is preserved in the archive as the record of the
  defect, and no reconciliation is owed back to the canonical
  copies.
- **Tests:** `tests/github-intel-public.test.mjs` and
  `tests/github-owner-default.test.mjs` pinned both copies of the
  intel handler; they now pin the canonical `api/github.js` only —
  the archived snapshot is not a shipped entrypoint. That removes
  exactly the 5 duplicate-copy pins (intel-public 8 → 4,
  owner-default 2 → 1, each duplicate pin having asserted against a
  byte-identical copy). Every other test is untouched and no test
  ever pinned the bundle's divergent trio.
- **Suite on this PR's head tree:** 78/78 pass, 0 fail (pristine
  master baseline control: 83/83; the −5 is the de-duplication
  above, not a regression); `node --check` clean on app.js and
  server.js; the AGENTS.md DOM/JS binding check passes. Tree:
  84 blobs → 86 (5 paths moved, 2 pointer READMEs added).
- **Also censused, not duplicates within this row's scope:**
  `security/capability-gateway.{ts,js}` and
  `security/nonce-ledger.{ts,js}` are a declared spec↔runtime-port
  pair in one directory (each .js header names the .ts as the typed
  specification it ports; `server.js` loads the .js); capability
  sets and the 5000 ms nonce window agree. `README.md` and
  `security/README.md` share only a filename, not an artifact.

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# Savage-AI-style — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-15 (evolution SIA-E3 landing — claim-state linter plus a D2-style examination of the eight remaining unexamined documents; suite and eval re-runs; see the SIA-E3 section)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 6d8a79ff11e0 (the head this refresh branched from; this refresh's own merge commit sits on top)
**Truth status:** ACTIVE BRAND AUTHORITY

## Repository role

This repository is the canonical studio-wide authority for Savage
AI Studios visual identity, shared design semantics, and brand
claim discipline. It is also one of the two SIA platform copies
(see Verified current state).

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `6d8a79ff11e0` — the head the SIA-E3 landing branched
  from. Tree at that head = 295 blobs (materialized and hash-verified
  295/295 by the SIA-E3 crew, 2026-11-15).
- **Tests:** pytest **110/110** (`python -m pytest agent/ dat1/ -q`,
  venv with numpy 1.26.4). Re-run 2026-11-15 for the SIA-E3 pass:
  110 passed, 0 failed. Consistent with the prior independent runs
  recorded in earlier versions of this file. The claim linter's own

# SIA-V6-CEROS — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-04 (head, test count, and PR lists refreshed from live API state; typecheck and CI sections stand at their 2026-11-01 audit state; FALCON diff U11 2026-10-29)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 6373f2225ee8 (this file's own commit sits on top)

## What this repo is

The canonical CEROS implementation and productization source —
attestation, harness, pentest/redteam and toxicity-scoring surfaces
(package.json identifies `@sovereign/quantum-toxicity-mcp` v1.6.0).

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `6373f2225ee8` — the merge of PR #99 (ML-DSA-87 scheme-label correction + test-scoped issuer labels, merged 2026-11-02). Tree = 391 blobs.
- **Tests:** vitest **147/147** at this head (28 files, 0 failed — census primary run 2026-11-03, Tights first-hand). The Nov-1 audit figure was 139/139 at the old head.
- **Typecheck:** `tsc --noEmit` rc=2 — **18 errors**, concentrated
  in `scripts/runCerosDiagnostics.ts`. All 4 tsx script entry
  points are broken on Node 24. (Carried labeled, not reconciled:
  the prior GT claimed ~5,400 pre-existing repo-wide type errors;
  the audit's run measured 18 in the surface it checked. The
  figures measure different scopes.)
- **CI on main is RED** (Verify CerosKernel Boot + CodeQL Analyze
  failing on main itself) — every open PR below is unverifiable
  against that baseline until main's CI is fixed.
- The generic AI Studio README understates/misdescribes this repo
  and is documentation drift.

## Crypto state — corrected by the FALCON diff (U11)

The prior GT claimed "real ML-DSA-87 signing throughout via
triadic/FALCONAttestator.ts." The diff's measured position:

- Real **ML-DSA-87 (FIPS 204)** exists here via
  `@noble/post-quantum`: `src/ceros/falcon-mldsa.ts` is the honest
  implementation (9 caller modules). Its former defect — **no issuer
  binding** — was fixed by PR #93 (merged 2026-11-02, with the registry
  re-issuance recorded in `.breakthroughs/REISSUE-2026-11-02.md`).
- The triadic sibling formerly **relabeled its output `FN_DSA` whenever
  MTU < 1500** while still running ML-DSA-87; the label is corrected to
  `ML-DSA-87` at every MTU by the Lane D change (2026-11-02, below).
  Its key rotation still invalidates all prior signatures.
- **No real FALCON/FN-DSA exists anywhere in the estate.**
- The diff's recommendation (falcon-mldsa.ts canonical; the
  triadic class retired into a wrapper or honestly renamed) was
  **Savage's ruling to make — ruled 2026-11-02 (decision #20);
  see the ratification section below.**

## FALCON ratification — 2026-11-02 (estate decision #20)

Savage ruled on the U11 diff's recommendation:

- **Canonical signature implementation of the estate:
  `src/ceros/falcon-mldsa.ts`** (ML-DSA-87, FIPS 204, via
  `@noble/post-quantum`). Where a real post-quantum signature is
  required, this is the implementation.
- **FALCON/FN-DSA does not exist in the estate.** Code wearing that
  name is something else and must be named for what it computes.
  Applied the same day in SIA-Foundry (PR #18, merged): the keyless
  SHA-256 hash class is now `Sha256HashAttestator`, and the spine's
  HMAC-SHA256 stub is now `HmacAttestatorStub`.
- **Issuer binding** for falcon-mldsa.ts was implemented in PR #93
  (independently configured trusted-issuer registry, pinned keys; a
  receipt's embedded key alone no longer verifies) and **merged
  2026-11-02** (decision #22: the committed `.breakthroughs/registry.json`
  receipts were re-issued under the issuer-bound scheme — see
  `.breakthroughs/REISSUE-2026-11-02.md`). The no-issuer-binding defect
  is closed on main.
- The triadic sibling's `FN_DSA` relabel (Crypto state, above) was
  not changed by this ruling; it is corrected by the Lane D change
  (2026-11-02, below).

## Issuer identity & FN_DSA label — Lane D, 2026-11-02

Savage approved "fix it some other way" for the fact that the registry
re-issuance used the test fixture issuer. Lane D scoped the estate for an
existing production identity first (this repo, agent-pay, proofcrew,
savages-assistants, local estate records): **none exists.** Every estate
system defers issuer trust to operator runtime configuration, and no
operator has ever configured a CEROS production issuer. Nothing was
invented. The honest fix, applied in the Lane D PR:

- The committed registry and fixture issuer are labeled **test-scoped**
  in code and docs (`src/ceros/falcon-mldsa.ts` ISSUER SCOPE note;
  `docs/CEROS_MLDSA_ISSUER_BINDING.md`, "Committed state — TEST-SCOPED").
  Creating a production issuer remains an unperformed operator step.
- The triadic `FN_DSA` scheme label is corrected to the true algorithm
  label **`ML-DSA-87`** (type, sign path, and the mirrored claim in
  `src/kernel/ack.rs`). Label-only: signature bytes and payloads are
  unchanged, no committed artifact carried the old label, and no
  re-issuance was required.
- The triadic **class name** `FALCONAttestator` remains a legacy
  misnomer, but the retirement this text previously left open as a
  ruling has been executed (PR #105, merged 2026-11-09): the class is
  now a keyless compatibility adapter over falcon-mldsa.ts — it holds
  no keys and runs no signing algorithm itself; signatures carry an
  `issuerId` bound by the registered-issuer verifier, and legacy
  pre-adapter signatures (no `issuerId`, ephemeral per-process keys)
  fail verification closed.
- The adjacent `FALCON-512` labels were removed from the CEROS
  signature type, governance compiler, inventory, and portal; the
  compiler no longer emits a placeholder signature.
- The voucher UI and hash-only provider now identify their output as a
  Keccak-256 digest, not a zero-knowledge proof or solvency attestation.
- The label/compiler/provider corrections above are landed on main
  (PR #102, merged 2026-11-09 after rebase onto the current main),
  together with PR #103 (promotion-rubric input validation in
  `classifyPromotion`), PR #104 (fail-closed release dependency
  acceptance; landed as a module — no release path calls it yet),
  and PR #107 (the mock WASM registry's `signSmartContractPayload`
  and `runWithFuelMeter` now throw `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of
  fabricating a signature and fuel figures with `Math.random()`;
  governed execution fails closed until a real signer/meter exists).
- Capability pass, 2026-11-10 (PRs #109–#112): **R-9** — the shipped
  entrypoint `src/main.ts` boots again (the kernel's OrganismRegistry
  import was one directory level short of the declared sibling layout,
  and its documented runner could not resolve the module graph), and
  the boot-check workflow was rewritten to fail when the entrypoint
  fails (`scripts/boot-check.mjs`: real boot + `/status` + a real
  `/api/cycle` + clean SIGTERM shutdown; sibling checkouts require the
  `CEROS_SIBLING_TOKEN` secret). **R-1** — PromotionEngine's build
  dimension no longer awards full points to caller attestation:
  CALLER-attested exit codes cap at 3, strictly below the gate-EXECUTED
  tier's 5. **D6 paymaster half** — the paymaster's hard-coded payout
  default (the Uniswap V2 Router address) is removed; construction
  fails closed without an explicitly configured wallet, and the "ZK
  handshake" is renamed to the Pedersen commitment attestation it is,
  with a strict Schnorr opening-proof verifier (the old verifier
  accepted every input) and issuance that refuses balances below the
  threshold. **Governed WASM** — real execution restored: the host
  compiles and runs caller-supplied module bytes on the platform
  WebAssembly engine under the existing identity/ABC/CRI gates, meters
  fuel by a declared schedule over measured quantities, and signs the
  ML-DSA-87 receipt only over executed work, bound to the module's
  SHA-256. **Isolation + governed imports built (CEROS-E1 completion,
  2026-11-15):** execution now runs in a dedicated worker thread
  (`src/ceros/governed-wasm-worker.mjs`) under a declared deadline
  (default 2000 ms, per-invocation override, 60 s ceiling) — a
  non-terminating module is terminated and refused with
  EXECUTION_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED instead of blocking the calling thread
  (before this build it hung the host forever; measured by probe: an
  infinite-loop module never returned and the probe process had to be
  killed externally). Host imports are governed by policy
  (GOVERNED_IMPORTS in governed-wasm-host.ts): a module may import
  only `savage.clock_ms` (requires the declared `read` side effect)
  and `savage.write_sink` (requires `write`); imports are inspected on
  the compiled module before execution and anything else is refused
  with IMPORT_NOT_GRANTED (before this build the import object was
  empty and every import-requiring module trapped at instantiation).
  The signed receipt now also binds the enforced deadline and the
  granted imports. Suite: governed-wasm tests 12 → 19, full repo
  suite 210 → 217, tsc clean. NOT built (stated, not hidden):
  instruction-level fuel metering, governed network/payment host
  functions (no import admits them), non-numeric arguments, and
  module fetching (callers supply bytes).
- **R-9 remainder — ceros-ci.yml's two decorative checks (2026-11-13).**
  R-9's core (entrypoint boot + the boot-check workflow) is verified
  fixed on main: with the sibling layout in place,
  `scripts/boot-check.mjs` passes on the shipped entrypoint and exits 1
  when the entrypoint is deliberately broken. Two checks of the same
  defect class remained in `ceros-ci.yml`: the boot-check job's
  "Verify CerosKernel exports" step required `./dist/index.js`, and
  the yield-smoke job required `./dist/ceros/ContinuousYieldGenerator.js`
  — both behind `|| echo '...skipping...'`. Neither path is produced by
  any build here (tsconfig sets `noEmit`; `npm run build` emits
  `dist/server.cjs`), so both steps skipped on every run and could not
  fail. They now run from source via tsx —
  `scripts/verify-exports.mjs` (CerosKernel + bootOrganism load from
  `src/index.ts`) and `scripts/yield-smoke.mjs` (ContinuousYieldGenerator
  constructs and reports its stats shape) — each exiting non-zero on
  failure, proven in both directions locally.
- **D2 — triadic scoring failure propagation (2026-11-11).**
  `src/triadic/scoring.ts`: `computeNDBIndex` and `computeCRI` no
  longer substitute fabricated constants for missing or failed inputs.
  The old `scores.ndbIndex || 0.5` and `(scores.cri || 0.7) *
  evidenceMultiplier` silently turned an absent dimension into a
  plausible score (and, via `||`, rewrote a legitimate 0 to the
  constant; a NaN/Infinity evidence multiplier also flowed through
  silently). A missing or non-finite dimension — or a non-finite
  multiplier — now throws the module's definite scoring-failure error,
  the propagation discipline `computeWeightedScore` already used; gate
  composition (the `PromotionEngine.scoreTriad` idiom) converts the
  throw into a zeroed dimension and a definite verdict. Valid inputs
  score identically (values pinned by tests against the pre-change
  tree). Verified at main `6ec6bf44`: suite 193/193 (35 files) before;
  210/210 (36 files) after, including 17 new tests in
  `src/triadic/scoring.test.ts` (10 of which fail on the pre-change
  tree — every propagation case — while all pinned-value cases pass
  on both). Reviewed and deliberately unchanged: the display-only
  `summarizePromotionForDisplay` default (documented non-authority;
  defaults to the harshest label), the replay harness's ledgered
  NO_TOPOLOGY_HASH placeholder (the failure is recorded in the same
  result and cannot reach PROMOTE), the spontaneity metrics
  divide-by-zero guard, and the `src/ceros/scoring.ts` telemetry
  listeners (a metrics-file write failure cannot mask a score).

## Identity

Ruled: **D1 — the `ceros` name points at this repo.** Executed

- **ARS scores (/40)** — Source: this repo's own ARS scoring model
  (`operators/autonomous-cashflow-hunter/scoring-model.md`), self-assigned.
  Claim state: **reported (self-assigned), unverified** — planning
  judgments, not measurements. Labeled in
  `breakthrough-system/MASTER_SURFACE_BREAKTHROUGH_MATRIX.md`,
  `operators/autonomous-cashflow-hunter/sample-candidate-report.md`
  (the worksheet the cited 37/40 originates from), `Boss11.md`, and the
  capabilities matrix.
- **Counts from the 11-repo census** (repos wired 9/11, loops 3/3,
  scorecard 10/10s, sprint velocity counts) — Source: this repo's
  2026-07-03 census and sprint bookkeeping. Claim state: **reported
  (self-recorded)** as of 2026-07-03, and **stale** as current state
  against the 40-repo estate census of 2026-11-01. Labeled in the state
  packet and `REPO_BY_REPO_SPRINT_REALITY_REPORT.md`.
- **Ceiling-analysis figures** (`reports/config-vs-structural-ceiling-analysis.md`)
  — the 50µs "achieved" figure has no run record in this repo: Claim
  state **unverified**; 10µs / 4KB are declared targets.
- **`master-index.json`** — file-level provenance already declared in
  `_meta` (`ground_truth_source`, `last_updated`); a `metric_provenance`
  note was added to `_meta` recording that its assertions are as reported
  by the subject repos, not independently verified. (The index's
  staleness itself is defect D1, a separate fix.)

**Not edited, with reasons:** `analysis/MASTER_PORTFOLIO_STATUS.{md,json}`
already carry SUPERSEDED / frozen-snapshot labels with a pointer to the
current source (D3 fix, 2026-11-09). `research-memory/` files are dated
primary run records — the record is the source — and the pass-7 closeout
already flags its one unrecovered figure as reported-only in-line.
Definition documents (CRI formula and thresholds, triadic thresholds,
tier bands, the 15-standard constitution) state rules, not measurements.
Planning documents state targets and projections in target/projection
framing. `analysis/combined-ecosystem-report.md` reproduces source
material verbatim and now says so at its head.

## Mechanical provenance gate (evolution, 2026-11-15)

The convention above is now mechanically enforced — before this build
nothing checked it, and the next editor could silently add an unlabeled
figure and revive the failure class fix #114 closed by hand.

- **Capability:** `tools/check_metric_provenance.py` (stdlib-only Python,
  zero new dependencies) inventories every displayed metric — throughput,
  latency/time, percent, fraction-score, decimal-score and multiplier
  figures — on every display surface (71 of the tree's 77 blobs scanned;
  this file and the `research-memory/` primary records are exempt per
  the determinations above), and exits 1 naming file + figure when a
  displayed metric lacks its Source · As-of · Claim-state label or
  carries a claim state outside the admitted set
  (`verified` / `reported` / `contradicted` / `unverified` / `stale`).
  Definitions, formulas, thresholds, declared targets, projections,
  directives, prices, dates, version strings and plain counts are not
  metrics under the convention as #114 applied it and do not
  false-positive. Run it: `python3 tools/check_metric_provenance.py`
  (`--list` prints the per-surface inventory). Tests:
  `tests/test_check_metric_provenance.py` — the repo's first test suite
  (16 tests, all passing).
- **Metric, before → after:** displayed metrics under mechanical
  provenance enforcement: **0 of 167 → 167 of 167 (100%)**. Checker
  exits 0 on the current tree: #114's labels have **no gaps** — no
  labels were added or changed by this build, and no provenance was
  invented. Planted controls on a scratch copy: 2/2 caught (one added
  unlabeled figure and one stripped label each failed the gate, naming
  the file and figure).
- **Honest limit:** the gate enforces *labeling*, not truth — a figure
  labeled `contradicted` passes exactly like one labeled `verified`,
  by design. Whether a labeled figure is true remains an audit
  determination, not this tool's.

# SIA-Foundry — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-15 (seed-generated arbiter enforcement list
evolution, this branch; prior: 2026-11-11 promotion-path census + fix #126)
**Canonical branch:** jules/foundry-genesis-v1 @ 54889c9d3f (pre-evolution tip)

## What this repo is

The shared constitutional contracts, schemas, and cross-repository
primitives — the `@sia/foundry` package. It is a donor/foundation
layer. Not to be conflated with **savage-foundry**, the separate
repo that holds the D4 custody commit of the Foundry build tree.

## Verified current state

- **Head (pre-evolution base):** `54889c9d3f` on the default branch
  `jules/foundry-genesis-v1`. Tree = 72 blobs.
- **Tests:** vitest **91/91** on the pre-evolution tip (re-run
  2026-11-15); **99/99** with this evolution's enforcement-list tests;
  `tsc` rc=0 (build + typecheck) before and after.
- The estate's declared cross-repo dependency graph has exactly 2
  seams, and both are on `@sia/foundry` (audit emergence pass) —
  this package is the estate's one declared coupling point.
- Products ON now: 0 (proof plumbing; the envelope is dormant by
  the repo's own report).

## Known defects / honest gaps

- CI trigger coverage (resolved 2026-11-13, estate fix program; found
  as an adjacent finding of fix #126). `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and
  `.github/workflows/schema-validate.yml` — the two workflows living on
  this branch — triggered `pull_request` only against `main`, while
  this repo's default branch is `jules/foundry-genesis-v1`. Pull
  requests against the default branch (every fix-program PR: #21, #22,
  #23) therefore received no CI runs at all. Both workflows now also
  trigger on `jules/**` pull requests, mirroring ci.yml's existing
  push coverage; nothing else about the jobs changed. Validation was
  local: YAML parse + branch-pattern simulation over the event matrix
  (before: PR→default does not fire; after: it fires; PR→feature
  branches still do not) plus a local execution of the workflows' own
  steps (typecheck, tests 65/65, build, export checks, arbiter smoke,
  constitution check, schema validation). No live Actions run is
  claimed for this change — the first post-merge PR against the
  default branch is the live proof.

- Governance ledger durability (D5; resolved 2026-11-13, estate fix
  program queue row 101). `src/governance/GovernanceLedger` was an
  in-memory array whose `verify()` echoed the constructor option
  (`walAtomic: walMode === 'atomic'`), and
  `InvariantRuntimeKernel.computeRealCRI()` returned 1.0 on an empty
  ledger. The ledger is now a real write-ahead log: with a `walPath`
  configured, appends are JSON lines carrying a SHA-256 hash chain,
  `syncWrites: true` fsyncs each append, construction replays the log
  (valid-prefix recovery after a crash), and `verify()` recomputes the
  chain from disk and can fail — tamper and torn-write cases are pinned
  by `src/__tests__/governance-ledger-wal.test.ts` (10 tests). Without a
  `walPath` the ledger is memory-only and `verify()` reports
  not-atomic: memory is not a write-ahead log. `computeRealCRI()`
  returns 0 when no scored outcomes exist — an empty ledger is evidence
  of nothing. Boot integration: `src/orchestration` layer 3 resolves
  the WAL path from the `governanceWalPath` constructor option or
  `FOUNDRY_GOVERNANCE_WAL_PATH` and fails closed without one; its CRI
  self-suspension now applies to a measured CRI (a fresh ledger boots
  with CRI 0 recorded; CRI-gated operations — settlement, composition
  gates — stay closed until real outcomes accrue). Suite 65 → 75,
  typecheck and build clean.

- Arbiter evidence (D8; resolved 2026-11-13, estate fix program queue
  row 93). `schemas/constitutional-arbiter.ts` adjudicated the scorer's
  asserted `lawCompliance` booleans and verified nothing — any caller
  could assert every flag true and pass. A checked law (C1–C5, G4, C7,
  S2, E6, E7, E1) now counts as held only when it is asserted AND backed
  by evidence items (`PrimitiveScoreResult.evidence`, new
  `LawEvidenceItem` type in `schemas/law-schema.ts`) whose SHA-256
  digests the arbiter recomputes over the offered artifacts;
  asserted-but-unverified laws are violations and are named in the
  decision's `unverifiedLaws`. C7 requires two verifying items — its
  own text declares "a verifiable chain of receipts, objections, and
  constitutional proofs". The class header no longer claims enforcement
  of every law tier; it states the checks actually performed. The CI
  smoke fixture (`scripts/arbiter-smoke.mjs`) now carries real
  evidence. 7 new tests in
  `src/__tests__/constitutional-arbiter.test.ts`; suite 65 → 72.
  Adjacent and unchanged (outside this row's scope):
  `checkFoundationLaws` in `schemas/laws.ts` still reads asserted flags
  for C1–C4 (its C5 CRI floor is a computed check) — it is a scorer-side
  helper, not the arbiter. The arbiter remains consulted by no
  promotion path (see the D2 entry below); this fix governs what its
  adjudication means where it is used — its tests, the smoke check,
  and downstream consumers of the schemas package.

- Arbiter enforcement list — seed-generated (EVOLUTION, 2026-11-15).
  The last hand-maintained law surface is now generated. Before: the
  ConstitutionalArbiter's checked-law list (`C1–C5, G4, C7, S2, E6, E7,
  E1`, with per-law comments and the C7 two-evidence chain rule) was
  hand-coded in `schemas/constitutional-arbiter.ts`, with **0 mechanical
  ties** to any declared policy — verified on the pre-build tree: no
  script, workflow, or package script referenced the list, and
  `check:manifest` covered the D9 manifest only. After: the enforcement
  policy is declared in the seed corpus
  (`schemas/organism-manifest.seed.json` →
  `constitutionalArbiterEnforcement`: `totalCheckedLaws` plus ordered
  `checkedLaws` entries carrying id, the arbiter's per-law note
  verbatim, and `evidenceRequired`), `scripts/generate-enforcement.mjs`
  generates `schemas/constitutional-arbiter-enforcement.ts` from it, and
  the arbiter derives its list and evidence floors from that generated
  module. `npm run check:enforcement` is a byte-level drift check that
  **names the drifted law**; CI runs it alongside `check:manifest`.
  Adding a law to the enforcement set is now a one-source change:
  one entry in the declared policy + regenerate. Metric: drift
  injections on a scratch copy caught **3/3** — (a) G4 entry removed
  from the committed list → check fails naming G4; (b) G5 added to the
  declared policy only → check fails naming G5; (c) S2's note edited in
  the committed list only → check fails naming S2. Runtime behavior is
  identical: same 11 laws, same decision order (order is observable —
  `adjudicate()` reports violations in checked-law order — and is
  pinned by `src/__tests__/constitutional-arbiter-enforcement.test.ts`,
  including the exact violation order when nothing holds and the C7
  chain floor), same evidence semantics; the pre-existing arbiter
  suite is unchanged and green (suite 91 → 99, typecheck clean, build
  + arbiter smoke + constitution check pass on the built package).
  Count-surface census: no boot or runtime surface counted the checked
  laws before (the 60-law `FOUNDRY_MANIFEST_TOTAL_LAWS` is the seed
  law total, a different count, already generated under D9); the
  generated module states and exports the checked-law total
  (`CONSTITUTIONAL_ARBITER_CHECKED_LAW_TOTAL`, re-exported from
  `schemas/index.ts`). Honest limits — surfaces that remain
  hand-maintained: `schemas/laws.ts` (the C1–C5 derived view; not
  generated, but drift-pinned against the seed by
  `cardinal-law-drift.test.ts`), the hard-veto designation
  (`HARD_VETO_LAW_IDS` declared in the manifest generator itself), the
  arbiter's non-list enforcement constants (the C10 description
  screen, the S10 risk threshold 0.25, the 0.85 promotion floor — code
  logic, not law lists), and test/CI fixtures that deliberately
  restate the checked set as independent oracles
  (`constitutional-arbiter.test.ts`, `scripts/arbiter-smoke.mjs`'s C7
  two-receipt fixture).

- Promotion/arbiter gating (D2; resolved 2026-11-11, estate fix #126).
  A full census of the promotion paths on this branch found two live
  bypasses, both now closed on this branch:
  (1) `orchestrators/CrossRepoOrchestrator.emitCrossRepoEvent('PROMOTION')`
  consulted no arbiter at all — the "verdict" was a string the caller
  placed in the event payload, and the event was emitted downstream
  even when that string said FAIL (demonstrated at runtime before the
  fix: bus log recorded `constitutionalResult: FAIL, emitted: true`).
  It now obtains a `GovernanceArbiter` clearance itself (payloads must
  carry the promotion's `score` and `evidence`; missing values fail
  closed), records rejections with `emitted: false`, and throws before
  the event reaches any consumer.
  (2) `src/orchestration/CrossRepoOrchestrator.runOneGovernedCycle`
  discarded the return value of `CandidatePromotionBus.submit(...)`
  and published the cycle's PROMOTION event on the PROMOTE verdict
  alone; the event type is now gated on the bus clearance (a rejected
  submission surfaces as CANDIDATE, never PROMOTION).
  The triadic bus's handler fan-out was already veto-controlled, but
  its `probeHealth()` reported `bypassImpossible` from the mere
  presence of the arbiter deps — it returned true even with the veto
  stubbed out (demonstrated). The probe now exercises the veto with a
  poison submission (score 0, no evidence) and reports false if the
  rejection does not hold. Negative tests:
  `src/__tests__/promotion-arbiter-gate.test.ts` (10 tests).
  Remaining honest gaps, unchanged by this fix: the `schemas/`
  ConstitutionalArbiter (law adjudication over primitives) is still
  consulted by NO promotion path — it is exercised only by its tests
  and `scripts/arbiter-smoke.mjs`; the promotion gate arbiter in both
  orchestrator trees is `GovernanceArbiter.check`, and that check is a
  score-floor + evidence-count rule that does not consult the loaded
  law registry (laws drive `testVeto`/`hasLaw`/`getLaw` only). The
  bus's `constitutionalArbiter` dep is a `GovernanceArbiter` instance
  (`src/foundry.ts`) — the naming conflates the two arbiter classes.
  The divergent `main` branch carries the same two bypasses; this fix
  lands on the default branch only.

- Default signing key shipped in the tree (resolved 2026-11-11, estate
  fix #112; state: on branch
  `knights/fix112-sia-foundry-d7-default-signing-key`, PR open, merge
  pending Tights'/Savage's act): `HmacAttestatorStub.init()` in
  `orchestrators/CrossRepoOrchestrator.ts` fell back to a published
  literal (SHA-256 fingerprint `18ed6a1089b6…`) when `FALCON_KEY_ID` was
  unset, so anyone with repo access could forge PROMOTION/PATENT/YIELD
  signatures. The literal is deleted from the tree; signing requires an
  operator-provided key (constructor or `FALCON_KEY_ID` env), spine
  ignition fails closed without one, and the old key is refused by
  fingerprint if ever presented. Standing residue: the key remains in
  git history and must be treated as compromised forever — signatures
  made with it are never trustworthy.
- Cardinal-law canonicality (resolved 2026-11-09, estate fix program R-5):
  `schemas/laws.ts` previously gave C2/C3/C5 different names and texts than
  the law corpus (an earlier GT state). The canonical source is
  `schemas/organism-manifest.seed.json` — the manifest generator's declared
  source of truth, the manifest `src/foundry.ts` serves, and the input the
  ConstitutionalArbiter is fed. `schemas/laws.ts` is now a derived
  enforcement view carrying the seed's C1–C5 names/descriptions verbatim,
  pinned by `src/__tests__/cardinal-law-drift.test.ts`. The CRI 0.60 floor
  inside `checkFoundationLaws` is an enforcement parameter of that view
  (estate-wide promotion floor), not part of C5's canonical text.
- Dual orchestrators (resolved 2026-11-11, estate fix program D4 / fix
  #116; landed by amendment after fixes #112 and #126 merged): two
  divergent classes named `CrossRepoOrchestrator` existed. The declared
  and live one is `src/orchestration/CrossRepoOrchestrator.ts`:
  `docs/ACTIVATION-SEQUENCE.md` names it as the full Constitutional
  Spine implementation, the package root (`src/index.ts`; package.json
  `main` / exports `"."`) exports it, and it is the implementation wired
  into the `src/` runtime (its `constitutionalSpine` singleton is the
  boot object in `src/orchestration/server-boot-example.ts`). The
  parallel `orchestrators/CrossRepoOrchestrator.ts` - imported by
  nothing in the runtime tree, only by its barrel and its test suites -
  is archived at `archive/orchestrators/` with its barrel and the three
  test suites that exercise it (`cross-repo-orchestrator`,
  `hmac-attestator-key`, `promotion-arbiter-gate`), and the
  `@sia/foundry/orchestrators` subpath export is removed, so the package
  now exposes exactly one `CrossRepoOrchestrator`. The archived copies
  are the current post-#112/#126 versions, refreshed at landing from
  default head `89be03da` - NOT the `31a3ab7b` copies this PR was first
  filed with: the archived implementation carries fix #112's fail-closed
  signing and fix #126's arbiter-gated PROMOTION (per-file provenance
  and hashes: `archive/orchestrators/README.md`). The archived suites
  still run under vitest against the archived code; the archive is
  excluded from the package build (tsconfig) and from the package
  exports. Recorded dropped capability: keyed HMAC attestation
  (`HmacAttestatorStub`) existed only in the archived implementation
  and was never on the live path; the surviving spine attests with the
  keyless `Sha256HashAttestator` (a SHA-256 content hash, not a
  signature). Porting keyed attestation onto the single orchestrator is
  an owed follow-up, not done here.
- A shared contract existing here is not evidence that downstream
  repositories are synchronized or deployed.
- The audit's named short-build (not built): a proof-envelope
  interoperability adapter across the estate's proof dialects.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing — the train parked this repo's only open PR (below).

## Parked PRs

- **#16** — dependabot npm_and_yarn group bump whose base is this
  repo's default branch, itself another workstream's branch.
  Unblock: merging into that branch is the owning workstream's call.

## Where it is going

No direction ruled by Savage for this repo specifically. (D4
concerns savage-foundry's custody, not this package.)

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# Breakthrough-System — Ground Truth

**Pass 2 — full code-proven refresh. Last verified: 2026-11-11**, against
main `1d37c5b010a172d9c10b3ed568178e068daf7d3f`. Method: the full tree was
read from the GitHub API (every non-`node_modules` blob git-SHA-verified
against the API tree listing) and the source and tests were read directly —
no claim below rests on a README or a prior version of this file. Measured
on that exact tree after `npm ci`: `npm run typecheck` rc=0; `npm test`
**76/76 passed (11 files)**; `npx tsx discovery-run.ts` exit 0 (output in
"How to verify").

This pass supersedes the 2026-11-03 verification header and the
Tonight-Sprint-era sections of the previous version of this file. The
2026-11-09/10 build records (evidence-completeness, evidence-bound
discovery) are preserved, condensed, under "Verified build history"; their
code was re-read in this pass and the records stand.

**Canonical branch:** main. Open PRs at this verification: #27
(CI miner-dispatch gating), #28 (miner-governor `BLOCKED_UNVERIFIED`
hardening) — both open and unmerged; nothing on either branch is state
about main.

## What this repo is

Two systems, neither of which discovers or mines anything in the
search/experiment sense:

1. **The miner** (`main.ts` + `ingestion/ classification/ ground_truth/
   scoring/ promotion/ projection/ reports/`) — a repo-activity heuristic
   scorer. Given a GitHub token it fetches branch/PR/last-commit
   *metadata* for 8 named repos, emits exactly **one record per repo**,
   classifies it REAL / PARTIAL / CLAIMED / DANGEROUS from branch-and-PR
   shape, and applies fixed arithmetic weights (including a boost from a
   hand-written primitive registry). It never reads a file of code from
   any repo, generates no hypotheses, and runs no experiments. Its live
   path has **never been run end-to-end** (see component 10).
2. **The organism / discovery pipeline** (`src/organism-registry.ts`,
   `classification/law-classifier.ts`, `scoring/law-scorer.ts`,
   `src/discovery/`, `src/verification/`) — an evidence-bound promotion
   pipeline: candidates are scored only on sealed measurement records
   from external measurers, adjudicated by an in-repo arbiter and a
   fail-closed batch gate, and confirmed by an independent checker before
   anything is promoted to gold. Its entry points are `discovery-run.ts`
   (a manual runnable gate over this repo's own artifacts) and the test
   suite. It is not wired into `main.ts` or into any schedule.

In estate terms this repo is a research/evidence input. Its
classifications do not promote any claim between CODED / TESTED /
DEPLOYED / LIVE / CUSTOMER-USED / REVENUE-VERIFIED states, here or in any
sibling repo. Products ON now: 0 public (1 estate-internal classifier
CLI).

## Component state

Claim-state labels: **verified** (read in code and, where runnable,
exercised this pass) · **contradicted** (the code or configuration
disproves the claim) · **scaffolded** (real code, wired to nothing) ·
**absent** (no code path exists) · **blocked** (cannot be exercised; the
blocker is named) · **reported** (a document asserts it; no code stands
behind it).

| # | Component | State | Evidence (2026-11-11 unless dated) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Miner ingest (`ingestion/RepoIngestor.ts`) | verified | Metadata only: branches + PRs fetched via `ghFetchPaged` following `Link` pagination to exhaustion with a 50-page hard cap; truncation and pages-followed recorded on the snapshot. Last commit + open-issue count are single reads. Constructor throws without `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Owner defaults to `sa6ag9` (`GITHUB_OWNER` override, `RepoIngestor.ts:33`). No file contents are ever fetched. |
| 2 | Miner classify (`classification/TruthClassifier.ts`) | verified, with limits | Exactly one `TruthRecord` per repo. REAL requires commit ≤30d + ≥1 merged PR + ≥1 evidence string; the EvidenceLinker always emits a COMMIT citation (component 3), so the evidence condition by itself never gates. DANGEROUS = dangling `jules/*` branch + 0 merged PRs + >2 branches, **unless** the repo is in `GENESIS_EXEMPT_REPOS` — which still contains **Breakthrough-System itself** (and SIA-Foundry): a standing self-exemption, declared here, owned by a separate fix row. Since 2026-11-09 every record also carries a completeness assessment (component 4). |
| 3 | Evidence linking (`ground_truth/EvidenceLinker.ts`) | verified | Emits COMMIT (unconditionally), MERGED_PR, OPEN_PR, BRANCH citations stringified from the same snapshot. Each citation carries a `confidence` (0.3–1.0) that **nothing consumes** — the scorer reads only `evidence.length`. |
| 4 | Evidence completeness (`ingestion/EvidenceCompleteness.ts`) | verified | `assessCompleteness` → COMPLETE / TRUNCATED / UNKNOWN with `factor = 0.5 ^ truncatedLists` (one list truncated → 0.50, both → 0.25; UNKNOWN is assigned the fully-truncated 0.25 — completeness is never assumed). Carried classify → score → report; the factor and its derivation are published per repo in the report. Limits: covers the two paginated lists only; the discount is proportional, never total. Derivation: "Verified build history" + `reports/evidence-completeness-redo-2026-11-10.md`. |
| 5 | Miner scoring (`scoring/BreakthroughScorer.ts`) | verified mechanics | Classification baseline (REAL 0.90 … DANGEROUS 0.10) × evidence-count multiplier × recency step function × completeness factor, plus the registry boost (component 6) in layer1 and a merged-PR bonus (≤0.10). Every multiplier is written to a `scoringTrace` published in the report — a genuinely good property. A record that never passed through classification is scored with factor 1 and state NOT_ASSESSED: no discount applied, none claimed. |
| 6 | Primitive registry (`src/registry/primitives.ts`) as boost source | **contradicted** | 150 primitives + 150 duals, **all 300 hard-coded literals with `impl_status: 'LIVE'`** — mechanical census this pass: LIVE 300, PARTIAL 0, STUB 0. No code anywhere transitions a status, and nothing checks that a named primitive exists in its `repo_home`. Per-repo LIVE boost sums re-measured this pass: Infineum **+0.385**, SIA-V6-CEROS +0.191, SIA-v6 +0.129, Breakthrough-System itself +0.125, Savage-AI-style +0.106, SIA-Foundry +0.086, SIA-Ecosystem-Map +0.061. 30 entries are homed to `savage-command-center` (+0.089) — an id no `ALL_REPOS` entry uses (the ingestor's id is `savage-command-center-os`), so that boost can never apply. The header's claim that scores rise "as impl_status moves STUB → PARTIAL → LIVE" has no implementing code, and `src/tests/smoke.test.ts` asserts 150/150 LIVE, enforcing the status quo by test. |
| 7 | Promotion governor, miner (`promotion/PromotionGovernor.ts`) | verified | Threshold rules over the score exactly as the README's Promotion Thresholds table states; DANGEROUS hard-blocks. PR #28's additional `BLOCKED_UNVERIFIED` state exists only on its unmerged branch and is **not** main's behavior. |
| 8 | Future projector (`projection/FutureProjector.ts`) | verified mechanics, one stale key | Attaches a hard-coded per-repo domain/monetization/next-move string from a static map and a horizon bucket derived from promotion state; nothing is projected from data. The map's key is `savage-command-center`, but the record id is `savage-command-center-os`, so that repo falls through to "unknown domain" / "TBD" (key comparison this pass; proven by execution in the 2026-11-08 audit, keys unchanged since). |
| 9 | Report (`reports/BreakthroughReport.ts`) | verified | Writes `reports/output/BREAKTHROUGH_REPORT_<date>.json`: per-repo classification, promotion, scoring trace, completeness record + line, and a summary `incompleteEvidence` list naming every repo whose evidence was not COMPLETE. No report artifact is committed anywhere in the tree (verified by tree search this pass) — no live run has ever produced one here. |
| 10 | Live miner run | **blocked / unverified** | Never run end-to-end. It requires `BREAKTHROUGH_GITHUB_TOKEN` with read access to all eight private repos; that credential is not provisioned. CI's miner job runs only on explicit `workflow_dispatch` with `run_miner=true` and fails closed at its credential step until the secret exists. PR #27 (miner dispatch-only gating) remains open. |

## Repo-id enforcement, self-exemption removal, CI self-check (added 2026-11-11)

- **REPO_IDS are now enforced (D8).** The registry's declared contract —
  every entry's `repo_home` "must match a repo name in ALL_REPOS" — was
  enforced nowhere, and it was false: 30 registry entries (primitives
  P-116–P-130 and duals D-116–D-130) carried the stale id
  `savage-command-center`, which is not a scanned repo, and the
  projector's domain map was keyed by the same stale id. Measured on
  pristine main (`1d37c5b0`): the scanned repo `savage-command-center-os`
  scored `primitiveBoost=0.0000` and projected as "unknown domain / TBD".
  Now `repo-ids.ts` holds the one canonical list (`REPO_IDS`);
  `ALL_REPOS` re-exports it; the projector's map is typed
  `Record<RepoId, …>` so a missing or stale key is a compile error;
  the 30 entries and the projector key carry the real id
  `savage-command-center-os`. Measured after: boost `0.0550`, real
  domain projection. `src/tests/repo-ids-enforcement.test.ts` fails
  the suite if any `repo_home` leaves `REPO_IDS`, if any scanned id
  loses its projection context, or if any scanned id's boost stops
  reaching the scorer (negative control: reverting one `repo_home`
  to the stale id fails the suite, naming the entry).
- **No self-exemption (D7).** `TruthClassifier`'s genesis-exempt set
  included Breakthrough-System itself, so the miner could never flag
  its own repo DANGEROUS. Measured on pristine main: an identical
  dangerous-shaped snapshot classified Breakthrough-System PARTIAL
  and Infineum DANGEROUS. Breakthrough-System is removed from the
  set (its genesis branch merged in PRs #24/#26) and the enforcement
  tests prove it now classifies DANGEROUS under the same shape as
  any other repo. `SIA-Foundry` remains in the genesis-exempt set —
  a bootstrap policy for a sibling repo, stated here rather than
  hidden; it is not a self-exemption.
- **The self-check runs in CI.** `discovery-run.ts` — this repo's
  declared end-to-end verification over its own artifacts — previously
  ran only by hand. It is now the `npm run discovery` script and the
  `discovery-self-check` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, running
  ungated on every push and pull request. The job also requires both
  positive self-claims (DISC-PKG, DISC-README) to be independently
  confirmed on the tree, so a self-claim that stops verifying turns
  CI red instead of sitting silently in quarantine (negative control:

  discovery-run.ts's own contract (`59009731…` → `85510d72…`).

## Persistent cycle ledger (added 2026-11-13, step zero M1)

`src/ledger/cycle-ledger.ts` is an append-only JSONL store. When an
`OrganismRegistry` is constructed with a `CycleLedger`, every
`runCycle` appends one schema-tagged line — the cycle's manifest delta
(registrations + status outcomes) and its full `CycleResult` — before
returning, and the ledger becomes the cycle-numbering authority
(numbering continues across process restarts instead of restarting at
the manifest's literal 1). A malformed or foreign-schema line makes
reads throw: a corrupt ledger is refused, not repaired silently.
`discovery-run.ts` attaches a ledger only when
`BREAKTHROUGH_CYCLE_LEDGER` names a path, so the CI self-check run is
unchanged. Suite: 14 files / 93 tests (5 ledger tests: persistence

uninstantiated in production), and no committed `ledger/*.jsonl` exists

- **"Discovery happens here."** No code in this repo discovers or mines
  anything in the search/experiment sense. The miner grades repository
  activity from metadata; the organism pipeline promotes candidates only
  on sealed measurements fed to it.
- **"300 primitives are LIVE" as an earned or verified status.** All 300
  are hand-written literals; no status ever transitions and no existence

  into every miner score is unverified by construction.
- **"Five GOLD, verified breakthroughs."** `breakthrough_submission.ts`
  is a literal list; nothing was measured, run, or verified behind it
  (component 24).
- **"`ORGANISM_STATUS.md` describes this repo."** Retired (component 26):
  its schedule, org, auto-update, and integration claims were
  contradicted by `ci.yml` and the code.
- **"The miner classifies discoveries."** Granularity is one record per
  repo; no individual discovery, file, or PR is ever itself classified

  its headline DANGEROUS rule (component 2).
- **"Promotions are governed by the SIA-Foundry arbiter / CEROS
  orchestrator."** The gatekeepers are in-repo implementations of the
  declared contracts; the external systems are not integrated
  (component 13).
- **"The repo runs as shipped."** The tracked `node_modules` are not the
  install path; `npm ci` is required before anything runs (component 27).
- **"A live miner run has been verified."** It has not — the credential
  does not exist yet and the run remains blocked (component 10).
- **The discovery reports are this software's output.**
  `FINAL_IDE_DISCOVERY_REPORT.md` and `reports/FIRST_RUN_REPORT.md`
  describe candidates, hypotheses, and paths the current code cannot
  emit (component 28).

## Verified build history (scoped records; code re-read in this pass)

- **Evidence-completeness scoring (added 2026-11-09; redone 2026-11-10).**
  The miner grades the quality of its own evidence: since the pagination
  fix the ingestor records truncation and pages followed per list, and
  `assessCompleteness` turns that into the record of component 4. The
  redo replaced the first landed rule (a single linear term with a 0.50
  floor: fully-truncated confidence 1.00 → 0.50 as landed) with per-list
  multiplicative composition (→ 0.25 redone), on the derivation that
  three of the four evidence types are computed from the two lists
  themselves and every classification gate reads them — full derivation
  and the regenerated before/after measurement in
  `reports/evidence-completeness-redo-2026-11-10.md`. Verified by
  `src/tests/evidence-completeness.test.ts` and
  `src/tests/evidence-completeness-measurement.test.ts` in the current
  suite.
- **Evidence-bound discovery (added 2026-11-10).** The organism pipeline
  previously certified itself: the law scorer passed every law unless a
  caller explicitly asserted `false`, unbound dimensions awarded full
  weight, and both gatekeepers were stubs that could not veto — proven on
  the pre-change tree (main `86347b6d`) by three fabricated primitives
  with a completely empty signal set scoring **1.0, 1.0, 1.0** and all
  being promoted to gold. The replacement is components 12–16; the
  identical empty-input run now scores **0.0 ×3 and promotes nothing**.
  Interpretations recorded at the time and still standing: (1) the floor
  applies to the evidenced fraction of *all* bound laws — the former
  per-dimension weighting covered only 19 laws and capped some families
  below the floor for every possible candidate; dimensions survive as
  reporting groups. (2) The gatekeepers are real in-repo implementations
  because the named external systems are sibling repos, not importable
  packages. (3) The pipeline is material-agnostic; the verified
  end-to-end run uses this repo's own artifacts because the named

  estate transfer and unprovisioned credentials — a run over those

- **2026-11-03 Tonight Sprint (PR #26).** Its changes are visible in the
  current code and CI: the canonical eight-repo inventory under owner
  `sa6ag9` (including `savage-command-center-os`), fail-closed full-scan

## DiamondMiningEngine removed — dead code (added 2026-11-15, fix #155)

`src/optimization/diamond-mining-engine.ts` is **removed** (audit defect

# polygraph-v3 — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 (live API state; audit evidence 2026-10-29; Phase 2 fix evidence 2026-10-29)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 294b45f040

## What this repo is

Agent evaluation/evolution research runtime. Its cycle metrics
(`latency`/`throughput`/`quality`) are **SIMULATED PROJECTIONS**
from a seeded, symmetric mutation operator — every cycle result
carries `metrics_provenance: "simulated_projection"`. Promotions
are gated-simulation records, NOT measured self-improvement. That
labeling is the repo's own, and the audit confirmed it is honest.

## Verified current state — test history, carried labeled

- **Head:** `294b45f040`. Tree = 34 blobs.
- *2026-09-30 (prior GT):* 19/19 tests pass after that era's
  cleanup campaign.
- *2026-10-29 (audit, at the frozen head):* **23/24** — one real
  bug: `NameError: metrics_provenance` at `arbiter_kernel.py:418`
  killing the calibration pipeline. (The 24/24 figure in Codex's
  report was REFUTED at that head by both the lane and the
  verifier.)
- *2026-10-29 (Phase 2 fix):* the NameError was fixed and PR #694
  merged (`1b290379edf2`, tree proof clean); the suite stands at
  **24/24** after the fix. Current main includes the fix.
- Recorded, uninvestigated: a GitHub notice (2026-10-29) reported a
  polygraph-cycle workflow run FAILED on main at the fix commit.
  No investigation is on record.

## What is real vs simulated (audit-confirmed)

- The constitutional spine (`src/polygraph/constitutional.py`) is
  wired into the promotion path as a real gate; CEROS publication
  occurs only when `CEROS_DIAMOND_BUS_URL` is set and the verdict
  is PASS.
- The WASM sandbox executes code for real only when `wasmtime` + a
  WASM binary are present; otherwise it runs a validation-only
  fallback labeled `simulated=True, executed=False`.
- Embeddings are real OpenRouter neural embeddings only when
  `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set; otherwise a deterministic lexical
  feature-hashing embedding (real lexical signal, no deep
  semantics).

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **No benchmark workload is attached** — the named gap in the
  repo's own README. Until one is, no improvement claim of any kind
  is valid from this repo's cycles.
- Research/evaluation donor until separately packaged and validated
  for customers. Products ON now: 1 (self-improvement research
  runtime, internal/CI use).

## Step zero (2026-11-13, Savage's fire order)

- **PR #702 merged** (fitness/GDI separation + candidate-diff
  preservation). Re-baselined on the merged code: suite 28/28; a
  candidate that performs the reference workload correctly and faster
  measures GDI 0.0 (aligned), while the structured-fallback template —
  which does not perform the workload — measures quality 0.0 and blocks
  at GDI 0.4682. Both directions are the gate working; the remaining
  defect is candidate supply (patch-first intake is the fix).
- **Actions cycle repaired.** The post-2026-11-03 failures were not
  code: the jobs never started (account billing annotation, verbatim
  in the run record) and the workflow was later disabled manually. It
  is re-enabled; dispatched run 43497603898 on the post-#702 main
  succeeded end to end and serialized state to cycle 498.
- **Mutation provider is fallback-only, by declaration.** The repo's
  one Actions secret is named `OPEN_ROUTER_KEY`; the workflow and the
  provider both expect `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, so every cycle has run
  with an empty key (1,438/1,438 fallback mutations on record). Wiring
  the name is a one-line change that starts billable OpenRouter calls —
  it awaits Savage's explicit ruling, as does any spend.
- **Independent constitutional scoring (this PR).** The gate no longer
  derives triadic scores from the candidate's own fitness
  (`auto_score`'s affine map); `core/independent_scoring.py` recomputes
  them from the cycle's measured evidence (Dreamer governor pattern:
  recompute, tamper-on-inconsistent-claim, zero-dimension rejects).
  Unmeasured candidates now score utility/feasibility 0 and cannot be
  constitutionally promoted. Suite 38/38 (10 new tests).
- **Patch-first candidate intake (M2, this PR).**
  `core/patch_candidates.py`: a candidate is a patch against a
  designated target (intake manifests in `targets/intake/`), and
  fitness is the TARGET's own tests + benchmark measured in pristine
  vs patched copies — regressions and no-gain patches are rejected on
  evidence, and the real target tree is never modified. First target:
  `targets/scratch_calc`, whose bundled example candidate (closed-form
  sum_of_squares) measures improved on its own suite. What is NOT
  true: the live cycle's proposer does not emit patch candidates yet —
  wiring a generator to this intake is the D-M1 step, and the kernel's
  cycle still proposes via the (fallback-declared) mutation provider.
- **M2 benchmark hardening (follow-up PR).** Post-merge verification
  under concurrent host load exposed two measurement defects: test or
  one-shot benchmark wall times could manufacture a speed claim, and
  the scratch benchmark's six-decimal per-call output rounded a real
  closed-form result to exactly 0.0, which truthiness checks mistook
  for missing data. The harness now uses only the declared benchmark,
  measured in alternating paired rounds with a majority-win rule, and
  treats 0.0 as data via explicit None checks; the scratch benchmark
  times a 30-call workload sample at nanosecond-scale printed
  precision. Full suite 52/52, including a concurrent-load run.
- **The shared PR applier (M4, this PR).** `core/pr_applier.py`: on a
  confirmed promotion — every gate verdict passing, evidence digest
  present — it opens ONE PR applying the candidate's files to the
  target repo, with the full cycle receipt as the PR body. The client
  protocol it drives has no merge operation at all, so the applier
  cannot merge and never writes to the base branch; a human merges.
  Unlawful receipts are refused with nothing written (test-proven
  against a recording client). What is NOT true: no live promotion
  has flowed through it yet — it fires for real when the loop's first
  gated promotion lands (the L1 step), and its production client
  takes its token from the environment, never from code.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing — the train took no action in this repo. (The #694 fix
above predates the train.)

## Parked PRs

None — no open PRs.

## Where it is going

No direction ruled by Savage for this repo. The audit flags the
research program EXPERIMENT-FIRST; attaching a real benchmark
workload is the gating step for any future claim.

## Estate rule

## What this repo is

Organism self-model/scheduler core — an internal organ scheduler
whose CI heartbeat coordinates parts of the SIA family. Internal
infrastructure; no independent revenue or customer deployment.

Zero regressions at each step.
