## Update 2026-11-09 (EVO-7 — Bounce QC: measurement engine + export receipts)

- **Bounce QC engine — real.** `server/lib/audioQc.ts` (original
  code, no new dependencies) measures any rendered or posted audio
  buffer: duration/format facts from the decoder, BS.1770
  integrated loudness **by calling `integratedLoudnessLufs` in
  `server/lib/wav.ts`** (the bounce master's own measurement — not
  re-implemented; engine-vs-direct agreement proven in tests within
  the stated 0.05 LU tolerance; measured diff 0.005 LU, the receipt
  rounding), true peak by 4x windowed-sinc interpolation
  (interior-only evaluation; <= 0.01 dB error on pure-tone fixtures
  at 1/6/8/12/16 kHz and at the fs/4 band edge, including peaks
  straddled between samples), sample peak, full-scale sample
  count/fraction (clipping evidence), and a silence map (-45 dBFS
  floor, 0.7 s minimum; leading/trailing/max-internal). Every
  measurement is deterministic and unit-tested (13 engine tests).
- **Export measurement receipt — real.** Every `POST
  /api/export/bounce` now measures the encoded file bytes and
  returns a receipt (`starr.bounce-receipt.v1`): artifact facts +
  the file's full SHA-256, the measurements, the declared
  thresholds, and verdicts, sealed by a SHA-256 hash over the
  canonical receipt body (the sia-v6-core receipts pattern). The
  receipt is also written beside the WAV and served at
  `GET /api/download/bounces/:file/receipt` (auth-guarded; bounces
  rendered before Bounce QC have none and the route 404s saying
  so). `verifyBounceReceipt` (in `audioQc.ts`) re-verifies a
  receipt, optionally against the file bytes; tamper tests prove a
  changed measurement or a different file fails verification.
- **Verdicts — measurements vs declared thresholds, nothing else.**
  Clipping present (error), true peak above -1 dBTP (warning),
  internal silence over the declared limit (default 2.0 s; the
  bounce caller may declare `qc.maxInternalSilenceSec`), loudness
  outside the master profile's target +/- tolerance (default
  1.0 LU; `qc.loudnessToleranceLufs`, `qc.truePeakMaxDbtp` also
  declarable). **No perceptual/"quality" score exists anywhere in
  this machinery.** The reference gate's neural scorer (NISQA) is
  trained on speech; its numbers must never be presented as a
  music-quality metric, and they are not used here.
- **Upload analysis — extended.** `POST /api/audio/estimate` now
  also returns the same engine's measurement block + verdicts for
  the posted audio (one engine, not a copy).
- **Neural music layer — rejected per Savage's building law
  (2026-11-09: no third-party engines, models, or weights in the
  repos).** A learned perceptual layer ships only when it is
  Savage-built and Savage-trained; until then the deterministic
  measurements above are the whole claim.
- **Gates at landing:** suite **131/131 -> 146/146** (13 engine
  tests + 2 route tests added; the PR #44 auth negative controls
  are inside the 146 and still pass), DSP oracle **15/15**, root
  strict `tsc` **0**. Zero new dependencies (package.json changed
  only to wire the new test file into `npm test`).
- **Proof hardening (2026-11-10):** the EVO-7 claim is backed by
  a committed, runnable measurement —
  `evidence/measure-bounce-qc.ts` regenerates the before/after
  numbers: engine absent at `24e5f1d3` (0% of bounces measured);
  on this tree the fs/4 fixture reads sample peak **-3.46 dBFS**
  vs true peak **-0.44 dBTP** (intersample detection gain
  **3.02 dB**), the 6 kHz straddled fixture fires the
  `true-peak` verdict, receipts verify intact and fail on a
  tampered measurement, and the engine suite passes **13/13**.
  Recorded run: `evidence/evo7-bounce-qc-measurement.json`.
- **Limits, stated:** true-peak interpolation is evaluated on the
  interior only — the first/last 8 samples contribute their sample
  peak; blocks under -12 dBFS sample peak are not interpolated
  (a > -1 dBTP peak hidden there would require sustained
  near-Nyquist content at near-full scale — disclosed in the
  module header). A full measurement of a dense 60 s stereo
  buffer takes ~4.6 s on the build VM; sparser/shorter audio is
  proportionally cheaper. No client surface renders the server
  bounce result today, so the receipt's display surface is the
  API response + the downloadable receipt JSON.
- **Elevation ledger (existing features — proven state -> next
  step):** export bounce: real + BS.1770 (S-2) -> measured +
  receipted (this update) -> next: a client display for the
  receipt once a client surface renders server bounces.
  Audio estimate: tempo/key computed (S-3) -> + QC measurement
  block (this update) -> next: a calibration set for its
  confidences. MIDI import: real SMF parser (S-1) -> next:
  multi-track (type-1) + sysex verification pass. Bundle: real
  ZIP (S-7) -> next: embed stem audio once the storage path is
  decided (the bundle README already states plainly that it does
  not). Judge: engine 0.3.0 vendored, scores carry the engine
  version (PR #45) -> next: Phase 2 server persistence
  (`server/routes/judge.ts`), previously sequenced after the
  43-tsc pass — root tsc is 0 since 2026-11-08, so it is
  unblocked. Transduce: refuses unsupplied features (S-4) — no
  elevation claimed; honest refusal is its state.
- **Standing residue (unchanged by this update):**
  `shareJoinRouter` (`GET /api/share/join`) remains defined but
  unmounted — mounting it opens a public product surface, which
  is Savage's decision; the question is recorded, the router is
  left exactly as-is. S-8 (three parallel genome models), S-9
  (Modal wiring doc mismatch), S-10 (baked-in Supabase fallback
  coordinates), S-11 (Postgres integration test self-skips
  without `TEST_DATABASE_URL`) all remain open as previously
  recorded. Whether any Vercel project serves `main` remains
  **unknown**; nothing in this update deploys or repoints
  anything.

## Update 2026-11-10 (STARR-E1 — Certified Bounce, Breedable Sound)

EVO-7's internal QC receipt is now the customer-facing product
claim. Every bounce (`POST /api/export/bounce`) additionally issues
a **certified master receipt** (`starr.certified-receipt.v2`,
`server/lib/certifiedReceipt.ts`), written beside the master as
`<file>.cert.json`, returned in the response as `certifiedReceipt`,
and served at `GET /api/download/bounces/:file/certified`
(pre-STARR-E1 bounces 404 honestly).

What the certificate carries that the v1 receipt did not:

- **Two artifact bindings**: the master file's SHA-256 (as v1) AND
  a SHA-256 of the decoded PCM content — an encoding-independent
  content hash, so a byte-faithful re-encode still verifies and a
  changed sample never does.
- **The sound's genome lineage, per stem** (`server/lib/lineage.ts`):
  the voicing genome's id, species, generation, origin, fitness,
  mutation count, measured 7-chromosome signature, parents, and
  crossover/mutation provenance. Claims are labeled by how much the
  server could stand behind them: **SERVER_VERIFIED** when the
  declared genome id resolved against the server's genome store and
  the record + parents were loaded server-side; **CLIENT_ASSERTED**
  when the client supplied the record (the browser genome engine
  synthesizes the stems, so this is the normal label today — sealed
  after assertion, never upgraded); **ABSENT** with an explicit
  reason when no genome voiced the stem (imported audio, Faust WASM
  voices). Lineage is never blank and never fabricated; a malformed
  claim degrades that stem to an ABSENT naming the refusal, and the
  bounce itself never fails over lineage.
- **One seal over everything**: certificate hash over the embedded
  v1 receipt (verbatim, its own seal intact) + lineage + content
  hash. Overall verdict is CERTIFIED only when no v1 gate verdict
  fired (the v1 engine grades a true-peak crossing as a warning; the
  certificate does not call a master with any gate finding
  "certified"), otherwise REVIEW.

Standalone verification is shipped as a buyer tool
(`tools/verify-certified-receipt.ts`): given the certificate JSON
and the master WAV it re-checks both seals, both hashes, and
re-derives the five gate measurements from the audio — the receipt
is never trusted to grade itself.

Proof (Evolution Rule v2; harness
`evidence/measure-certified-receipt.ts`, results
`evidence/certified-receipt-results.json`, fixtures are the repo's
own synthetic-render material bounced through the real HTTP route):
BEFORE — complete certified receipts carried by buyer-facing
exports: **0 of 6 (0%)** (the v1 receipt alone lacks the content
hash and the lineage block, scored field by field). AFTER —
**6 of 6 (100%)** issued, **6 of 6 (100%)** verified standalone,
**0 intersample-overshoot escapes** across the set; negative
controls pass (one tampered receipt field fails verification; one
flipped audio byte fails verification). Engine-level controls in
`server/lib/certifiedReceipt.test.ts` additionally prove the
SERVER_VERIFIED path against an in-memory genome store, the
binding refusal (a certificate cannot be sealed over bytes the v1
receipt does not describe), and the hot-master case (a master whose
true peak crosses the gate seals REVIEW and re-measures as exactly
1 overshoot escape). Suite: **146 → 157 tests, all passing**;
`tsc` clean. Zero new dependencies — `node:crypto` plus the repo's
own engines only.

Honest edges, unchanged and unlabeled-upgraded: GPU song generation
remains an external-engine client (503 when unconfigured); ARI chat
remains a labeled 501 stub; the route's mastering chain normalizes
every bounce to the profile target under a 0.98 peak ceiling, so
route bounces cannot overshoot — the certificate's overshoot-escape
property is proven at engine level (above), and the export-set run
includes a deliberately hot, intersample-peaking input that the
mastering chain catches and the shipped master then certifies clean
with receipt-verifiable numbers. The SERVER_VERIFIED lineage label
requires a deployment with the genome store reachable from the
export path; in a no-database deployment claims resolve
CLIENT_ASSERTED or ABSENT, labeled as such. No client surface
renders the certificate yet (the JSON + buyer tool are the shipped
surface). `main` was not touched; this lands on `master` only, and
the star@main disposition remains Savage's/Tights' open question.

## Update 2026-11-10 (fixes #104/#105 — S-10 and S-11 closed)

- **S-10 — baked-in Supabase fallback: present as a module,
  absent as a running path; now removed.** Verified from code.
  `client/src/core/cloudProject.ts` was the only application
  source importing `@supabase/supabase-js`. It built a Supabase
  client from `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` / `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`
  with **baked-in fallback coordinates** (a hard-coded project URL
  and publishable key as `||` defaults), so the client was always
  "configured"; it authenticated through Supabase (`auth.getUser`,
  magic-link `signInWithOtp`) and persisted projects and takes to
  Supabase tables and storage — a second auth + persistence path
  beside the wired JWT auth (S-5/S-6). Also from code: **nothing
  imported it** — no caller anywhere in the tree — so it never
  ran; it was an armed, unreachable path, one import away from
  reactivating a parallel auth system. Disposition: **removed**,
  following the S-6 precedent (a fallback is deleted, not kept
  politely). The module is deleted; `@supabase/supabase-js` is
  removed from `package.json` / `package-lock.json` (exactly the
  8-package `@supabase` subtree; no other lock entry moved — the
  Deno edge functions under `supabase/functions` resolve their own
  `jsr:` build and never used the npm package); the
  `VITE_SUPABASE_*` entries are removed from `.env.example`
  (flagged here, per AGENTS.md); and the `StoredTake.audioPath`
  comment in `client/src/core/projectStorage.ts`, which described
  a live cloud-sync location, now records the field as legacy —
  the data shape is retained so stored projects keep loading.
  **Untouched, deliberately:** the `supabase/` migrations and edge
  functions (the archival bundle whose deletion
  AZURE_DEPLOYMENT.md gates on the Azure reconciliation sign-off;
  they are not an application auth path) and the server-side
  `SUPABASE_*` env schema / pooler `DATABASE_URL` (the database
  layer, not auth). Negative controls in
  `server/routes/truthfulness.test.ts` now scan `client/src` +
  `server` and fail if any application source imports the
  Supabase client, carries a `.supabase.co` coordinate, or calls
  `signInWithOtp`, and assert the removed module stays removed —
  demonstrated failing on the pre-fix tree (exactly the 2 new
  controls red, naming `cloudProject.ts` on all three needles)
  and passing after. The wired JWT auth is now the only
  authentication path in the application source, by construction
  and by test.
- **S-11 — Postgres integration test: it already ran in CI; its
  local skip was invisible in the count, and now is not.** Two
  halves, separately evidenced. (1) *The CI leg pre-dates this
  fix:* the test job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has provided a
  `postgres:16` service and set `TEST_DATABASE_URL` for the test
  step since the test was introduced (commit `47e43c2913`,
  2026-11-05, which added both), and the workflow run on master
  tip `5034c421` (2026-11-10) completed green. The env gate is
  proven live locally: with a present-but-unreachable
  `TEST_DATABASE_URL` the suite executes and fails (exit 1)
  instead of skipping, before and after this fix. (2) *The actual
  defect was the count:* the suite used a describe-level skip,
  which node:test's tallies **do not count at all** — a
  database-less run of the pre-fix tree printed `tests 157 /
  pass 157 / skipped 0` while the Postgres suite contributed zero
  tests and sat out, indistinguishable from a full run, and this
  file quoted the total as "all passing". The test file now
  registers a **test-level** skip when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is
  unset (counted — `skipped 1`, named in the output) and runs the
  unchanged suite body when it is set. **Current count, stated
  with its environment:** the suite is **160 tests** — in a
  database-less run, **159 pass + 1 skipped** (the Postgres
  integration test, named above); in CI, where the database
  exists, **160 pass**. The earlier figures in this file
  (131/131, 146/146, "146 → 157 tests, all passing") are landing
  records of their dates and stand as written; the 157 statement
  did not name that whether the Postgres test sits inside the
  count depends on the environment, and is superseded by the
  statement above. Gates at landing: full suite as stated; root
  `tsc` 0; client `tsc` 0; `npm ci` from the updated lockfile
  clean; `npm run build` green. Zero new dependencies (one
  removed). `main` was not touched; this lands on `master` only.
- **Standing residue (updated):** S-8 (three parallel genome
  models) and S-9 (Modal wiring doc mismatch) remain open as
  previously recorded. `shareJoinRouter` remains defined but
  unmounted — unchanged, Savage's decision as recorded.
  Whether any Vercel project serves `main` remains **unknown**.

## Update 2026-11-15 (STARR-E2 — Breed-by-Measurement)

The atoms tier's breeding loop is closed. `breedAtoms`
(`client/src/core/atoms/breed.ts`) already recombined two sounds and
**measured** the offspring's traits — but nothing selected on those
measurements: callers picked parents and seeds by hand, so breeding
was random search. New pure module
`client/src/core/atoms/targetBreed.ts` adds
`breedTowardTarget(founders, sampleRate, target, options)`: given a
founder library and a target trait profile, it breeds generation
after generation with tournament parent selection and an elitist
survivor pool, both driven by measured trait distance to the target
(distance normalized per-trait by the founder library's own spread),
and returns the winning sound plus a per-generation convergence
history. Fully seeded — same founders + target + seed reproduce a
run bit-for-bit.

- **Metric (frozen benchmark, `client/src/core/atoms/targetBreed.test.ts`):**
  generations-to-target vs random breeding — the identical
  generational structure and budget (12 offspring/generation,
  survivor pool 12, founders always available, cap 100) with every
  selection step replaced by a uniform draw, i.e. the pre-STARR-E2
  instrument. Frozen setup: 8 synthesized founders; trait set
  brightness / rms / sustainLevel; target {0.45, 0.45, 0.5} (an
  interior point — the closest founder is 0.309 away, tolerance
  0.06); 12 seeded trials (1000–1011), both arms.
  **BEFORE (random, measured on the pre-build tree): median 14
  generations, mean 21.0. AFTER (directed): median 4, mean 5.5 —
  3.5x on the median, both arms 12/12 reached.** The >= 2x bar is
  asserted permanently in the test suite; every number above is
  deterministic and reproduces exactly.
- **Suite:** BEFORE on base master `f53f4992c`: 197 tests / 194 pass
  / 2 fail / 1 skipped — both failures pre-existing in
  `server/routes/truthfulness.test.ts` (`POST /api/export/bounce`
  returns 404 in a local run), measured on the pristine base before
  any STARR-E2 change; fix-program input, not this evolution's
  scope. AFTER: **202 / 199 / the same 2 / 1 skipped** — zero
  regressions, the 5 new tests green; root `tsc` 0. Zero new
  dependencies.
- **What is NOT true:** no UI surface yet — `BreedingChamber` /
  `AudioBreeding` still pick breeding parents by hand; wiring
  `breedTowardTarget` into them is named remaining work, not done
  here. Target profiles cannot name `pitchHz` (null for unpitched
  sounds). The `genomeEngine` chromosome system is untouched; its
  fitness remains the aesthetic heuristic recorded in
  `docs/sound-genetics.md`.

# Reversal — verified working baseline

Last checked: 2026-11-04. Source base: main 2cd92e5919b8599f5e62ed760cc28993d4025290 (Steps 1–4 landed: lexicons + CMUdict + LICENSE, the declared re-baseline, the product flesh-out, the Generation-2 Dreamer round; plus the fluency-clamp re-baseline, engine 0.3.0, suite 77/77; plus the Step 5 validation declaration + corpus, PR #9 merged 92085d9e), with the Step 5 validation EXECUTION (this change) as a draft-PR branch on top; the PR #3 merge was 7f1472f16c15aeb41efdf8e3173cc2d0457520e6 and the PR #2 repair baseline was e5372b5655.

Reversal is a browser-local lyric scoring, rewrite ranking and genre arrangement planning tool. It supplies 22 deterministic text heuristics and preset musical specifications. Its lyric candidates are templates drawn from per-genre, per-section template families (Step 3, DECLARATION §2.8) — still templates, not finished songs. It does not generate audio, produce complete original songs, or predict commercial success. The sixteen research mechanisms (Gen-0's five, Gen-1's five, and Generation 2's six) and the exposure layer are wired into the interface as working panels (PR #3; Gen-2 in Step 4); they are unvalidated heuristics, not established market advantages.

## Verified in this repair

- Original production build failed with TS6133 for two unused songBuilder parameters. The repair removes the unused parameters while preserving template output and strict compiler checks.
- Node 24.22.1; npm test: 66 tests pass (4 CSV regression + 18 engine + 7 lexicon + 10 re-baseline acceptance + 27 Step 3: 7 golden-corpus + 6 projects + 4 arrangement export + 10 template/genre/panel). npm run build: TypeScript and Vite production build pass. npm run lint: the committed ESLint ruleset (.eslintrc.cjs) passes with --max-warnings 0 (Step 3, §2.10).
- Step 3 product flesh-out (DECLARATION §2.4–§2.10, draft PR on f9a4594dc9): save/reopen projects in the browser (IndexedDB + localStorage fallback) with portable .reversal.json export/import — scores never stored, reopened projects re-scored, future schema/engine versions rejected with a clear message; playable arrangement export — a deterministic MIDI file (tempo, section markers, one chord per bar) plus arrangement JSON, chord tones resolved from each section's Roman-numeral progression in its declared key through the committed numeral map in src/engine/arrangement.ts (declared interpretation: in a minor key the tonic numeral is the minor tonic; minor-key tones stay within the natural/harmonic/melodic union); mechanism-panel depth — per-section VFTI in built arrangements, Cringe-Delta batch mode against the line a candidate would replace, the structure bundle over built arrangements, ECCEI what-if weight controls; a pinned 20-line golden corpus (evidence/golden-corpus-v1/, corpus SHA-256 b72cb3e039c812c49ab1e8944938aa46da4df4aebe19bed77d22302d318ae118) with full-row expectations and property tests; section-aware template families (src/engine/lyricTemplates.ts, original in-repo editorial data, origin logged in LEXICON_SOURCES.md); three new genre profiles (boom-bap, country, rock — data-only). MEASURED DEVIATION, not fixed: §2.7's assumed "every metric within [0,10]" property fails for processingFluency, which has no upper clamp in the v0.2.0 formula (10 - (avgWordLen - 4) * 1.5; measured 11.25 on short-word lines, formula ceiling 14.5, M ceiling ~10.64). The golden suite asserts the true formula bounds for those two fields and [0,10] for the other 24. Clamping it is a scoring-formula change and stays Savage-gated; the demo/rank baselines (5.51 / 5.69; 5.49 / 4.94) are untouched by this step. RESOLVED 2026-11-04: Savage ruled the clamp later that day — see the fluency-clamp bullet below.
- PR #3 wiring was verified independently before merge: the five engine modules are byte-identical to the pre-wiring baseline (no scoring-formula change) and the demo-chorus composites reproduce exactly (5.28 / 5.47). hookCompression (computed but excluded from the M composite) and voiceConsistency (hardcoded constant 2) were labeled in the interface at that step, not silently fixed; the Step 2 re-baseline below supersedes those labels.
- Step 2 declared re-baseline (DECLARATION §2.1 + §2.2, approved by Savage 2026-11-04 as part of the declaration package): the engine's first deliberate formula change. (1) voiceConsistency is now a real register comparison — each line's register fingerprint (average word length, syllables per word, familiarity ratio, long-word rate) is scored by its weighted absolute deviation from the song's median fingerprint (declared constants in scorer.ts: equal weights, scale 2, clamped 0-10); lines scored with no song context keep the declared neutral fallback of 2. Reason: one quarter of Family D was a constant for every line of every song. (2) hookCompression is now counted in the M composite — M is the mean of all seven Family-A metrics. Reason: unique-token ratio is a compression/fluency measure by Family A's own logic, and permanently displaying a metric the formula ignored was a standing liability. Engine version 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 (package version + the ENGINE_VERSION constant, stamped into every scored row and therefore every CSV export). Baselines: demo-chorus composites 5.28 / 5.47 (v1, engine 0.1.0) -> 5.51 / 5.69 (v2, engine 0.2.0); the v1 values are preserved as a commented record in test/engine.test.mjs. The full old-vs-new record over the locked golden corpus (the 32-line Step 1 measurement corpus + the demo/rank/extra lines the suite pins, 40 line-instances; corpus SHA-256 981e9bef997edb5104585c62b97ef97a05ae6bf3968b8870ecf49925eb87022c) is evidence/rebaseline-step2/diff-report.md: 160 of 1080 compared numeric values changed, largest composite move 0.29, no flag or confidence-band changes anywhere in the corpus. This PR also re-pins the two Step 1 drift assertions Step 1 deliberately left red (rankCandidates writerly 4.77 -> 4.75 on the Step 1 engine, then to 4.94 here; VFTI openVowelRatio 0.5 -> 0.4 and fitScore 5 -> 6, both Step 1 CMUdict drift).
- Step 4 Generation-2 Dreamer round (DECLARATION §1.2–§1.4): the Dreamer method (skills/dreamer.md) is codified as a typed pipeline in src/dreamer/ (stage types + records, a deterministic primitive-pool snapshot, and the gate's numeric core); ideation is recorded as attributed data, never a runtime model call. Six candidates were specified against the declared contradiction (a lyric can be strong line-by-line and weak as a recorded song section) from information theory, signal processing, behavioral economics, prosody/phonetics, plus the declared vertical step, and codified in src/engine/candidates/. ALL SIX PASSED the §1.3 gate on the locked probe (the Step 3 golden corpus + the Step 2 re-baseline corpus: 8 groups, 60 line-instances): hand-computed worked examples reproduce exactly; determinism ×100 byte-identical per group; non-degeneracy against 32 per-line reference series (22 metrics + 5 composites + 5 per-line mechanism outputs) with max |r| of 0.8726 (Song-Relative Surprisal vs repetitionSpacing), 0.3145 (Section Crest Factor), 0.7011 (Marginal Repetition Value), 0.6930 (Section Rhyme Cohesion), 0.4450 (Line Contour Curvature), 0.7700 (Peak-End Section Score) — all under the pre-registered 0.98 threshold; zero rejections (src/engine/GEN2-REJECTIONS.md records the outcome and the closest calls). The mechanisms are ADDITIVE panels (App section 8) via src/engine/inventedMechanisms.gen2.ts + GEN2_MANIFEST: no existing formula, weight, or composite changed, no existing test re-pinned, and the v0.2.0 baselines reproduce exactly (demo chorus 5.51 / 5.69; rankCandidates 5.49 / 4.94). The full round record — declaration, pool hash a9a8e8e2, specs, complete correlation rows, per-line probe values, stage log — is committed at evidence/dreamer-rounds/gen2/ and is re-derived and asserted by test/gen2.test.mjs (suite: 74 tests, all passing; build and lint clean). Each mechanism's truth grade is PARTIAL: the measurement is real, the musical interpretation is an unvalidated heuristic pending the Step 5 validation pass.
- Fluency-clamp re-baseline (Savage ruling 2026-11-04 16:38 PT: "Clamp fluency at 10 and publish the re-baseline"; draft PR from main 628e520324): the engine's second deliberate formula change, executed with the Step 2 discipline. processingFluency — the one metric whose formula had a floor only (ceiling 14.5 at avgWordLen 1) — now clamps to [0, 10] in scoreLine, in the codebase's existing clamp idiom; scorer.ts differs from the Step 4 base only at that line (plus its ruling comment) and types.ts only at ENGINE_VERSION. Published diff (evidence/rebaseline-fluency-clamp/, generated by committed tooling and regenerating byte-identically): both golden corpora re-scored with the pre-clamp engine (0.2.0) and the clamped engine (0.3.0) — combined, 42 of 60 line-instances changed and 124 of 1,620 numeric values moved, every one of them processingFluency, M, or compositeScore; largest composite move 0.07; largest processingFluency move 1.5 (the clamp itself); zero flag changes, zero confidence-band changes. Per corpus: the Step 2 corpus moved 29/40 lines (86/1,080 values, max composite move 0.06); the golden corpus v1 moved 13/20 lines (38/540 values, max composite move 0.07). New pins: demo chorus 5.51 / 5.69 -> 5.51 / 5.68; rankCandidates 5.49 / 4.94 -> 5.45 / 4.90; cringeDelta -0.30 -> -0.34; the v0.2.0 values are preserved as a commented record in test/engine.test.mjs, and the Step 2 record is untouched (its NEW scores are preserved verbatim as this record's OLD scores). §2.7's declared property now holds as written — every metric, M included, lives in [0, 10] — and the golden suite asserts exactly that (Step 3's true-bounds deviation assertion is resolved, its history kept in the test comment). Gen-2 gate re-run against the clamped engine (its 32-series correlation reference set includes processingFluency): all six candidates stay ACCEPT, max |r| moved at most 0.0069 (Song-Relative Surprisal 0.8726 unchanged; Section Crest Factor 0.3145 -> 0.3158; Marginal Repetition Value 0.7011 unchanged; Section Rhyme Cohesion 0.6930 unchanged; Line Contour Curvature 0.4450 -> 0.4519, its worst reference now processingFluency itself; Peak-End Section Score 0.7700 -> 0.7679), no candidate near the 0.98 threshold; the gate evidence was regenerated (pool hash a9a8e8e2 -> 85a1d2df, the hash covering ENGINE_VERSION) and the pre-clamp round record is preserved in evidence/rebaseline-fluency-clamp/. Engine version 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0 (package.json + package-lock version fields + ENGINE_VERSION, in sync per the suite). Suite: 77 tests, all passing (74 + 3 fluency-clamp record tests); build and lint clean. Starr's vendored Judge (sa6ag9/star) stays pinned at engine 0.2.0 by design — its drift test holds it; re-vendoring is a separate later step, deliberately not in this PR. LANDED 2026-11-09 (estate fix program, reversal D2): the re-vendoring step has now executed — star PR #45 re-vendored the Judge from this repo @ 64e7fc1a40 (engine 0.3.0) under a regenerated PROVENANCE.json manifest; exactly scorer.ts and types.ts changed against the 0.2.0 pin, and Starr's suite re-pinned to the 0.3.0 baselines above (demo chorus 5.51 / 5.68; rankCandidates 5.45 / 4.90) at 131/131.
- Step 5 validation — DECLARATION SEALED + CORPUS ASSEMBLED (2026-11-04, draft PR from main 1d915e799f; the scoring run itself has NOT happened and no corpus item has been scored by this lane): `evidence/validation-step5/DECLARATION.md` pre-registers the test of engine v0.3.0 exactly as the governing declaration §3.5 requires — one primary hypothesis (headline composite vs documented-hit class, positive), the four family composites (C negative: it is a risk composite), all 22 base metrics with declared directions (Family D all negative), and the six Gen-2 candidates (five positive; line-contour-curvature negative — it measures contour breakage). Methods fixed in advance: song-level means over scored lines, Spearman ρ + AUC on the pair set, top-quartile precision for the composite, Benjamini–Hochberg within families, |ρ| ≥ 0.30 effect floor; verdicts SUPPORTED / REFUTED / AMBIGUOUS with the copy consequences §3.5 assigns; results publish whatever they show; no number may be tuned after scoring begins, and any post-scoring change requires a new declaration version and a full re-run. Corpus (`evidence/validation-step5/corpus/`, intake-verified: strict UTF-8 decode, SHA-256 per item in MANIFEST.md, lyric-line counts, outcomes in outcomes.csv): **22 scored items** — Savage's own catalog: 8 (4 voice-note lyric transcripts, uncorrected auto-transcripts with the source caveats carried into the manifest; 4 Suno clips with play counts 2–5, descriptive only) — and a public-domain pair set of 14 (8 documented hits vs 6 no-chart-located, all published 1891–1927), plus 1 metadata-only record (Old Town Road, unscored). Gaps, stated in the manifest rather than padded over: the modern charted stratum contains **zero** scoreable texts because post-1928 lyrics are under copyright and no lawful text was available (never scraped); Savage's catalog yielded lyric text for only these 8 songs (other known titles exist as audio/production material only); "no-chart-located" is an intake-search result, not proof a song never charted; My Blue Heaven was excluded because only its chorus could be lawfully verified. EXECUTED 2026-11-04 (this change, draft PR from main 2cd92e5919): run under the sealed declaration with the committed code paths unmodified — 22/22 corpus items scored, zero failures, the pair set 14/14 (above the §6 minimum of 12); determinism proven by two independent clean-checkout runs producing byte-identical score tables (song-scores.csv SHA-256 0912a5a0e9feeaa007c95dd4e415449128de5dec152582891e083d3a064e47a3); statistics exactly as declared (Spearman ρ + AUC, exact two-sided permutation p over all 3,003 outcome assignments, Benjamini–Hochberg within families, |ρ| ≥ 0.30 effect floor). VERDICTS over the 33 declared hypotheses: **0 SUPPORTED, 1 REFUTED, 32 AMBIGUOUS**. H-P (headline composite) AMBIGUOUS (ρ +0.18, exact p 0.57) — so under §6 no validation claim of any kind enters buyer copy and the product continues under the pre-validation claims discipline. Top-quartile precision 0.50 against the 0.571 base rate. The one REFUTED: Gen-2 section-crest-factor, declared positive, measured ρ −0.68 (BH q 0.076) — its declared-direction claim is refuted on this corpus; all six Gen-2 candidates remain truth grade PARTIAL with these results attached to their record (none validated, none deleted or renamed). Full record: evidence/validation-step5/RESULTS.md + song-scores.csv + per-line-scores.json + statistics.json, published whatever they show per §7. Engine src/ is byte-identical on this branch; no formula, weight, or marketing copy changed on the basis of this test.
- Step 7 launch preparation (this draft PR, from main 455956871858): the app carries the official product name (Reversal — Lyric & Arrangement Studio), a Get Reversal pricing section for the ruled $49 one-time Studio and $299 one-time Studio Session offers, and a single checkout configuration module (`src/config/checkout.ts`). Both Stripe Payment Link values are deliberate placeholders; placeholder/non-HTTPS values unit-test to a disabled "Checkout opens shortly" control, and no fake link is shipped. Copy stays inside the Step 5 claims fence and states the validation outcome without cherry-picking (0 SUPPORTED / 1 REFUTED / 32 AMBIGUOUS; no predictive claim). Local verification on this branch: npm ci completed; the prior 77 tests still pass and 3 checkout tests bring the suite to 80/80; production build and lint pass; a browser check of the production build returned 200, rendered the pricing section with both controls disabled, and reproduced the current engine 0.3.0 demo pins [5.51, 5.68] (rankCandidates [5.45, 4.90]). Vercel project `reversal` (`prj_2atDY7pa19ec6eE8uaAWEGnFLWz7`) was created for the rehearsal; the savageaistudios-site project was not touched. The preview deployment itself is BLOCKED in this environment: Vercel's GitHub integration cannot access the private sa6ag9/reversal repo (create_deployment from Git source and project Git-linking both returned repo-not-found), and the connector's file-upload route cannot carry the 3.2 MB bundle; the unblock (grant the Vercel GitHub app repo access, or one dashboard/CLI deploy) and the full remaining launch sequence are recorded in evidence/launch-step7/LAUNCH.md. Production is NOT live and no Stripe purchase proof exists yet.
- Browser workflow: score two supplied lines, rank two rewrites, render three arrangement variations, download the actual CSV. Independent CSV parsing confirms both lyric strings, including quotes and comma, round-trip exactly.
- CSV values now follow CSV quoting rules and neutralize spreadsheet formula prefixes in user text. Numeric negative scores remain numeric values. Download URLs are released after use.
- Inputs have accessible names. Interface descriptions identify the planner as templates and explain the scoring limits.
- Dependency resolution is pinned in package-lock.json. Node 24 is required for the built-in TypeScript test loader.

## Remaining product work

A private working review was deployed successfully on 2026-11-04: https://reversal-savage-review-20261104.springmimosa.chatgpt.site . Its static build uses the same source tested above; evidence/productization-20261104/deployment.json records the native receipt. No public paid deployment, checkout, buyer, paid fulfillment, measured willingness to pay, calibrated hit prediction or competitive advantage is established by these checks. Save/reopen projects and playable arrangement export — this file's previously named next enhancement — landed in Step 3 above. The Gen-2 Dreamer round landed as Step 4 above. Step 5 declaration + corpus LANDED (PR #9 merged 2026-11-04, merge 92085d9e, independently verified before merge: declaration sealed with zero results inside; corpus 22 scored items + 1 metadata-only record, all SHA-256/line counts recomputed 22/22; one uncorroborated secondary figure named in the verify report - Darktown 'over 1M record copies'). The validation EXECUTION is COMPLETE and merged (PR #10 merge 1c119a15, independently verified bit-identical before merge - all 33 tests recomputed from the raw scores with zero divergence): 0 SUPPORTED / 1 REFUTED / 32 AMBIGUOUS across the 33 declared hypotheses; H-P AMBIGUOUS, so no validation claim enters copy; the Gen-2 six remain PARTIAL, with section-crest-factor's declared-direction claim refuted on this corpus — full record in evidence/validation-step5/RESULTS.md. The Starr install (Step 6) landed 2026-11-04 (star PR #40). Prices are already ruled ($49 one-time / $299 Studio Session, 2026-11-04). # Macsense-2 — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 (live API state; audit evidence 2026-10-29; merge-train evidence 2026-11-01)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 0b62de1849
**Repository state: UNARCHIVED (verified live 2026-11-04: `archived` = false; the archive recorded below has been lifted)**

> **Delivery note (historical):** this refresh was prepared
> while the repository was archived and read-only, and was
> delivered locally with the 2026-11-01 refresh-pass report
> (`~/workspace/estate-audit/GROUND-TRUTH-REFRESH-PASS-2026-11-01.md`).
> It has since landed in-repo (the post-unarchive landing); the
> repository is unarchived as of the 2026-11-04 live check.

## What this repo is

MacSense creator product trio: an Android app (the "Ari" assistant
client — DAW/mastering view models, FlowCapture, Gemini flows), a
gateway server, and a web studio (static + node tests). A codebase
distinct from macsense-ari; per its own record, the pair's
monetization/disposition decision was intentionally deferred by
Savage.

## The archive — unexplained

This repository was **archived at the account level** when the
2026-11-01 pass recorded it. No D1–D12 ruling archives it (D2
archived durak only), and the 2026-11-01 merge train treated it
as a live repo. The archive's origin is not in any record
available to this pass. **Update 2026-11-04: the repository is
unarchived (live `archived` = false)** — the question of the
archive's origin remains as recorded; the state itself is
resolved.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `0b62de1849`. Tree = 316 blobs.
- **Tests (audit-run, Lane D):** web **44/44** — once the static
  server is running (`npm run serve`, port 4173, an undocumented
  precondition; without it the smoke test fails ECONNREFUSED — a
  harness precondition, not a code defect). Server **7/7** incl.
  build.
  *Install record — reconciled 2026-11-09 (M-3):* the corrections
  appendix recorded an install `ci_rc=1` against a dossier line
  claiming rc=0 for one install path; neither source record is
  preserved in this repo, so the path was rerun against the
  current tree. Every install path the tree defines returns
  rc=0: `web/` `npm install` rc=0 and `server/` `npm ci` rc=0
  (direct reruns, 2026-11-09, with web tests 44/44 and server
  tests 7/7 passing on the installed trees), and the
  Android/Gradle path's CI job (`build-test`, incl. Gradle
  setup and dependency resolution) is recorded **success** at
  the current head (check runs, 2026-11-04 batch, read via
  API). The dossier's rc=0 is the record that matches the tree;
  the appendix's `ci_rc=1` is not reproducible on any install
  path and is superseded. The one failing job in that CI batch
  is `release`, which failed at *Assemble release APK
  (unsigned)* — a build step, not an install step (carried
  under M-2).
- **Android: NOT RUN** — no Java/Android SDK in the audit
  environment. The Android surface is CODED only.
- The gateway refuses to start without GEMINI_API_KEY.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- Nothing deployed is evidenced (vercel.json + Dockerfile exist;
  live state UNREACHED).
- Products ON now: 0 customer-usable.

## Gateway auth gate — M-1 fail-open FIXED (2026-11-10, PR pending merge)

The estate audit's M-1 (HIGH) finding: `requireClientToken`
(`server/src/middleware/auth.ts`) was a **no-op when
`MACSENSE_CLIENT_TOKEN` was unset** — documented in-code as a
rollout convenience — and it was the only gate on
`/v1/ari/chat`, the route that spends the server-side Gemini
key. The gateway refused to start without `GEMINI_API_KEY`, so
the natural misconfiguration was a publicly reachable,
unauthenticated proxy. Reproduced on the pre-fix tree before
changing anything: the server booted tokenless and an
unauthenticated `POST /v1/ari/chat` passed the gate and reached
the Gemini upstream call (502 `upstream_error` from the route,
i.e. the request got all the way through); the suite even
pinned the pass-through as expected behavior.

The gateway now **fails closed**, in three layers, all declared
in `server/src/config.ts` / `server/src/middleware/auth.ts`:

1. **Boot refusal in production:** with
   `NODE_ENV=production`, config throws at import time when
   `MACSENSE_CLIENT_TOKEN` is unset or blank — same fail-fast
   pattern the code already used for `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The
   process never listens.
2. **Loopback containment otherwise:** the server binds
   `HOST` (new config, default `127.0.0.1`; previously it bound
   every interface). Outside production, a non-loopback `HOST`
   without a client token also refuses to start.
3. **Gate refuses, never passes:** `requireClientToken` with
   no token configured answers **503
   `{error, code: "gate_not_configured"}`** instead of calling
   `next()`. That state is reachable only on a loopback-bound
   non-production server, and even there no chat request
   reaches the upstream.

Declared ungated surfaces, unchanged and named: `GET /health`
and `GET /readyz` (liveness/readiness probes, no key spend),
and the static web studio. With a token configured, behavior
is unchanged: missing/wrong bearer → 401 `unauthorized`;
correct bearer passes. CORS, rate limiting, and the Gemini
client are untouched.

Tests: server suite 7 → **14 passing** (tsc build + `node
--test`): the pre-existing pass-through test was rewritten to
pin the 503 refusal (the fix's whole point is that the old
expectation was the defect; no other existing test was
modified in substance — one config default assertion updated
for `clientToken` `null` → `""` plus the new `host` field),
five new config cases (production unset/blank token refuses,
production with token boots, non-loopback tokenless refuses,
HOST honored with token), and a new end-to-end file
(`server/test/gateway-fail-closed.test.js`) that boots the
real compiled server and probes it over HTTP. Verified
additionally by direct probes of the built server: production
tokenless boot exits non-zero naming `MACSENSE_CLIENT_TOKEN`;
tokenless loopback boot serves `/health` 200 and refuses
`/v1/ari/chat` 503.

**Refused / not built, named plainly:**

- The audit's alternative "bind to localhost by default" was
  adopted as the containment layer, not as a substitute for the
  token: a production deploy behind a platform router
  (Vercel/Azure configs exist in-tree) needs the interface
  reachable, so production requires the token — both halves of
  the audit's fix, each where it works.
- No per-route or IP allowlist was added: none is declared
  anywhere in the code, and inventing one would change the
  product's access model without a ruling.
- The Gemini client has no upstream timeout (a hung upstream
  holds the request open); that is a separate latent gap, not
  M-1, and was left untouched rather than bundled silently.
- The stale header block at the top of this file (canonical
  head `0b62de1849`, tree 316 blobs) predates the current main
  (`1dc2b8565`, 323 blobs); it is a pre-existing staleness, not
  corrected here beyond this section.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing — the train parked this repo's only open PR (below).

## Parked PRs

- **#92** — "Merge systems integration into main." CI green (11
  checks), diff read in full by the train, mergeable — but the
  merge API returned 404: branch protection blocks this token, and
  the branch's vercel.json build/install-command removals need
  author confirmation. (The archived-state sentence that stood
  here is superseded: the repo is unarchived, verified live
  2026-11-04, and #92 remains open, unmerged.) Unblock:
  protection change or UI merge + vercel.json confirmation —
  the vercel.json ruling is Savage's.

## Where it is going

No direction ruled by Savage for this repo. The open fork is
PR #92's vercel.json change (Savage's ruling); the archive
question above is closed as a state matter.

## Verification ledger (added 2026-11-09)

The M-3 dispute above happened because this repo kept no durable
record of its own verification: two documents disagreed and neither
source record survived in-repo. That class of dispute is now
settled by reading the tree. `verification/ledger.jsonl` is an
append-only, machine-readable ledger — one JSON entry per
measurement, each recording surface (`web`/`server`/`android`),
job, workflow run id, commit, timestamp, per-step outcomes, the
suite counts the job itself measured (or `null` when no count was
preserved — never reconstructed), and a `source` field
(`ci`, `ci-evidence`, `local`, `local-reconciliation`) so
provenance is never blurred.

- **Writers:** the `verification-ledger` job in
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (android) and
  `.github/workflows/web-ci.yml` (web, server) runs after the
  measured jobs on pushes to `main` and on manual
  (`workflow_dispatch`) runs on `main`, and commits the appended
  ledger back with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` — the write grant
  (`contents: write`) is scoped to that job only (in `web-ci.yml`
  it overrides the workflow-wide `contents: read` for that job
  alone). The recording can never fail the build it records: the
  entry builder warns instead of throwing, the job is
  `continue-on-error`, and the commit step exits 0 even if the
  push cannot land. Failed jobs are recorded faithfully as
  failures. Gateway behavior is untouched by this machinery.
- **Reader:** `node verification/read-ledger.mjs` renders the
  latest state per surface/job; `--check` exits 1 when any
  surface's latest entry is a failure. Fixture tests:
  `node --test verification/read-ledger.test.mjs`. Full format
  documentation: `verification/README.md`.
- **Seed (2026-11-09):** the first entries record the M-3
  reconciliation state — web 44/44 and server 7/7 measured
  locally on the post-M-3 tree (`local-reconciliation`), and the
  android jobs from CI check-run evidence at `719c066a`
  (`ci-evidence`: `build-test` success; `release` failure at
  *Assemble release APK (unsigned)*, the M-2 item). The ledger's
  first recorded failure is therefore deliberate: the record says
  what is true. As of the seed, `read-ledger.mjs --check` exits 1
  on android/release — that is M-2's state, not a ledger defect.
- Not wired: `azure-webapp.yml` and
  `vercel-production-deploy.yml` also execute the web suite as
  part of deployment; the ledger's web surface is recorded by
  Web Studio CI on the push to `main` that precedes any deploy
  of that commit.

- **On-demand exercise + commit-back state (redo,
  2026-11-10):** PR #97 added `workflow_dispatch` to both
  workflows and extended the `verification-ledger` job guards
  to admit dispatched runs on `refs/heads/main` alongside
  pushes. That half is proven: dispatched runs Web Studio CI
  42784847843 (success) and CI 42784841481 (success) executed
  their ledger jobs the same day, and `build-entry.mjs` built
  genuine `"source": "ci"` entries for them (job logs:
  "ledger: recorded web/web-test success for run 42784847843",
  "ledger: recorded server/gateway-build success for run
  42784847843", "ledger: recorded android/build-test success
  for run 42784841481"; the merge-push runs 42784770703 /
  42784770734 built theirs as well). **None of those entries is
  in this ledger, and the count on `main` is unchanged: 4
  entries, 0 with `"source": "ci"`.** The commit-back push is
  rejected by branch protection on `main` — GH006, quoted from
  the job logs: "Changes must be made through a pull request"
  and "2 of 2 required status checks are expected". The
  `github-actions[bot]` token cannot satisfy the required
  approving review or the required status checks on a direct
  push, and the commit step's warn-and-exit-0 design swallowed
  every rejection, so the loop reported success while recording
  nothing. This is the second, deeper reason no `ci` entry has
  ever landed; the first (no dispatch path, push-only guard) is
  fixed. Landing entries now requires a governance decision
  outside workflow config — a push bypass for the Actions app,
  a dedicated ledger branch, or PR-based recording — which is
  Savage's to rule. Until then the loop is exercisable on
  demand and its entries are genuinely built in CI, but they
  do not persist to `main`.

## M-2 gateway CI lane — completed (2026-11-15, estate fix program)

- The gateway CI lane exists and is the `gateway-build` job of
  `.github/workflows/web-ci.yml`: it builds the gateway, runs the full
  server suite (`npm test` — the startup matrix in `server/test/`,
  14 tests at this head), exports counts for the verification ledger,
  and builds + boots the combined production image.
- The lane was **red at head `02cd4f6a`** for a provisioning reason,
  not a gateway defect: Web Studio CI run 42892891778 (2026-11-10)
  shows `gateway-build` failing at *Boot combined studio container*

These entries record two scoped corrections. They do not refresh the

## 2026-11-11 — MKT-E2: MCP Proof conformance receipts over stdio (scoped)

Before this entry, MCP Proof evaluated MCP servers only over Streamable
HTTP (`evaluate()` builds an `McpHttpClient`); it had no stdio transport,
no shipped conformance content, and no way to record a server that fails
to start — a failed `initialize` threw, so no receipt could say
"evaluated, and it did not run." External servers evaluated with sealed,
independently verifiable receipts: **0**.

What landed (products/mcp-proof): a stdio transport
(`src/stdio-client.ts`, argv-array spawn with `shell: false`, child
environment scrubbed to PATH plus explicit extras, per-request timeouts,
stderr confined to a truncated in-memory tail that never enters a report
or receipt); `evaluateStdio()` on the same grading/snapshot/receipt core
as the HTTP path (a failed handshake signs a `failed-to-initialize`
receipt instead of throwing, unless the caller opts out); reference-server
conformance profiles and a runner (`src/profiles.ts`,
`src/conformance.ts`); CLI modes `--stdio-command` and `--conformance`;
and 10 new tests against a real spawned fixture server (suite 65 → 75,
all passing).

Measured run, 2026-11-11T08:56Z, against clones of
modelcontextprotocol/servers @ `e1dc4b18` and servers-archived @
`9be4674d` (evidence: `products/mcp-proof/evidence/conformance-2026-11-11/`):
**13 external servers evaluated, 13 sealed receipts, 13/13 verified
independently** with `packages/receipt`'s standalone verify CLI
(public keys only); a deliberately tampered receipt was rejected
(exit 8, body-hash and signature failures). Split honestly: 7 servers at
full scope with real read-only calls (14 cases, all passing); 6 at
partial scope (handshake, snapshot and unknown-tool probe only — no real
tool invoked, and the receipts say so), of which redis
failed-to-initialize (it does not answer `initialize` when its Redis is
unreachable) and sqlite notably answers unknown tools without an error.
7 further servers were not attempted, each named with its reason in the
evidence summary.

What is NOT true after this entry: the Apify actor surface remains
HTTP-only (stdio/conformance are library + CLI); signer key custody is
unchanged and still the standing blocker recorded in catalog.json (the
run's keystore lived outside the repository; only its public keys are
published in the evidence directory); no receipt has been sold or issued
to any customer; and the partial-scope receipts claim no tool behaviour
for the servers they cover.

## FacturForge state

At the audit freeze, marketplace's FacturForge Stripe verifier was
finished and exemplary but **wired to no route**; the live $19
Payment Link fulfilled by manual dashboard review. The train chain
(#125–#149) landed the FacturForge hardening/fulfillment work with
CI green — but an end-to-end **paid → delivered proof (TEST-mode
checkout, real entitlement, refund/revoke) has NOT been executed**.
That proof remains the acceptance path, here and for the site's
merged webhook (PR #4, a Phase 2 verification debt).

**Update 2026-11-04 — the FacturForge stack #156–#169 MERGED +
VERIFIED** (Blitz Wave 3; tree proof: merged main equals the
verified tip on all 27 stack paths, `catalog.json` carrying both
main's stripeOffers and the stack's counts, zero non-stack paths
changed). The stack closed a live revenue-bearing defect — on
pre-stack main, presenting the operator key generated invoices
outside the prepaid store: no entitlement, idempotency, or quota
(#156) — and built the buyer-delivery layer (one-time signed
credential redemption, fail-closed direct-TLS delivery and
receipt, origin-bound certificates), HTTPS-only operator startup,
buyer binding to Stripe Checkout (#166), and a read-only
grant/receipt/quota status CLI (#167). It composes cleanly with
the site ledger (site PRs #17/#18): no second fulfillment writer,
no second webhook path. **F-6 accepted consciously at landing:**
#158 narrows the G4 no-egress release gate to permit exactly the
`node:https` `createServer` import in a file that calls it
(acceptance recorded on PR #158, comment 6630301856). **F-8
(runbook):** refund → grant revocation remains a deliberate
operator action (`revoke(grantId, reason)`); nothing propagates
it automatically. **Still NOT established:** the end-to-end
paid → delivered → refund/revoke proof remains gated on a
test-mode Stripe key (rk_test), which does not exist yet; no test
in the stack makes any Stripe call; site PRs #15/#16 (the stack's
cross-repo workflow pins their heads) remain unmerged drafts and
must land or be preserved.

## 2026-11-10 — paid→delivered proof path built; D1 corrected (estate fix program)

**New shared package `@savage/delivery-ledger`** (`packages/delivery-ledger`,
19 tests): an append-only, hash-chained order ledger that binds a verified
payment event to the delivery it paid for and issues self-contained
receipts. A delivery can be recorded only against a recorded payment, must
name that payment entry's hash, and must name every delivered artifact by
SHA-256. A buyer or auditor verifies a sale with
`savage-delivery-verify --payment <file> --delivery <file>` **from the
receipts alone** — no ledger, database or network. Order states are
fail-closed: `FULFILLED` (both sides, receipts attached), `UNFULFILLED`
(payment, no delivery), `UNKNOWN_ORDER`, `CHAIN_INVALID` (never
FULFILLED). Forged or cross-order receipt pairs fail verification; the
negative controls are in the package's test suite.

**Level change, measured** (`packages/delivery-ledger/LEVEL-CHANGE.md`
and `LEVEL-CHANGE.json`, reproducible via `tools/measure-delivery-proof.mjs`):
the share of completed deliveries carrying a cryptographically verifiable
paid→delivered receipt went **0% → 100%** of the wired flows (16/16
catalog offers driven through the ledger), and one-delivery verification
effort went from *no command exists — manual, unbounded* to **one command,
median 0.401 s**. The before-measurement is a census plus execution on the
pre-change tree: the only commerce receipt type was the payment-only
`VerifiedPurchaseReceipt`, the delivery modules defined no receipt type,
and the built verifier rejects the legacy records (exit 8).

**What is NOT true:** no live transaction has been recorded in the
ledger. Nothing in a deployed path calls `recordPayment`/`recordDelivery`
yet — the ledger is not wired into the site's fulfillment worker (site
PR #52, itself not deployed) or any webhook route, and the first live
paid→delivered→refund/revoke transcript remains gated on a test-mode
Stripe key (rk_test), exactly as recorded in the FacturForge state
above. Customers 0 / revenue $0 is unchanged by this build.

**D1 corrected:** every catalog `stripeOffers` link (16) and
`FACTURFORGE_PACK.paymentLink` (plus its webhook/test mirrors) now points
at a generation-2 link on the account of record
`acct_1UYG8zCG8Je0vWdb`, taken from **`stripe-links.json`** — the Stripe
API inventory of 2026-11-08 (all 76 links active). The
`stripeOffersVerifiedLive: "2026-11-02"` stamps, which referred to the
retired gen-1 account `acct_1UDhFvCA21F1OObS`, are removed, and
`tools/verify-catalog.mjs` now fails any catalog payment link that is not
in the registry. The claim made is account provenance + API-active;
hosted-page rendering flickers independently of the API flag and is
re-checked at promotion time.

## 2026-11-10 (later) — receipt pairs issuable as signed SRE-1 envelopes (estate fix #81)

The delivery ledger's "custody unresolved" boundary (audit D4) is now
resolved at the standard layer. Signer-key custody exists in
**savage-standard** (SRE-1 envelope signing under a committed public key
registry; estate fix #78), and savage-standard's universal verifier now
understands this ledger's receipt pair natively (its
`marketplace-delivery-pair` dialect, fix #81): a pair minted by this
package can be formed into the pair native
(`savage/delivery-receipt-pair/1`), wrapped in an SRE-1 envelope, and
signed, and the verifier checks the envelope signature AND recomputes
both receipts' entry hashes and receipt digests, the four pair bindings,
and the artifact digests — proven end to end in savage-standard's
`tests/test_delivery_pair.py` on a pair minted by this package's own
compiled code from main `bfaa3a18`, plus this repo's boundary text:
the ledger header and `DELIVERY_RECEIPT_BOUNDARIES[3]` now state the
signed-envelope route exists (previously: custody "unresolved").

**What remains NOT true:** no production estate signing key exists —
savage-standard's registry holds only a destroyed demo key, so no
production pair can be signed until the operator mints the real key
(their act, on their machine). This package's minting code does NOT
wrap-and-sign at issuance: the deployed fulfillment path is unchanged,
nothing in a live path calls the envelope machinery, and bare receipts
remain hash-bound exactly as before — the signature lives on the
envelope, never on the receipt. Receipts minted before this change
carry the previous boundary text and verify exactly as before (the
boundary strings are receipt data, not verification inputs).
*(The final sentence of this paragraph is superseded by the fix #83
section immediately below: the package's issuance path now DOES
wrap-and-sign at issuance when a key is configured. The deployed
fulfillment path remains unchanged.)*

## 2026-11-10 (later still) — issuance wraps and signs at issuance (estate fix #83)

The delivery ledger's issuance path now performs the wrap+sign itself.
`packages/delivery-ledger/src/issue-signed.ts` exports
`issueSignedPair(pair, options)`, returning an `IssuanceRecord`
(`savage/delivery-issuance/1`): the pair exactly as minted, an explicit
`signing` statement, and — only when signing ran — the signed SRE-1
envelope. The operator CLI is `savage-delivery-issue`
(`src/issue-cli.ts`): it loads a JSONL ledger, refuses any order that
is not FULFILLED, and issues that order's pair.

**Design — pipeline/subprocess, chosen from the code.** The module
contains NO envelope, canonicalization, digest or RSA code: it drives
savage-standard's own `savage-verify` CLI (wrap → sign → verify
self-check) as a subprocess, so the envelope is produced by the same
implementation that verifies it. A TypeScript reimplementation of
SRE-1 was rejected (fix #81's ruling: a second implementation drifts,
and the standard is the estate's neutrality point); a pure
manifest hand-off was rejected because issuance would then return
without proof that a verifying envelope exists — the self-check below
is the difference. Runner resolution: `savageVerify` option ??
`$SAVAGE_VERIFY` ?? `savage-verify` on PATH; a `.py` path runs as
`<python> <path> -m savage_standard.cli`; a directory path (the
standard's unpackaged source tree) runs as `<python> -m
savage_standard.cli` with `PYTHONPATH` set to it; the interpreter is
`python` option ?? `$SAVAGE_VERIFY_PYTHON` ?? `python3`.

**Key-optional law (never a fake pass, never a silent skip).** Key
path: `keyFile` option ?? `$SAVAGE_SIGNING_KEY_FILE` (mirroring
savage-standard's own convention). No key configured → issuance
behaves exactly as the pre-#83 mint path and returns
`signing: {performed: false, reason: "no signing key configured …"}` —
the absence is on the record. Key configured → ANY failure (CLI
missing, key unreadable, signing refused, verdict below expectation,
signature leg not passing) throws and fails the issuance; there is no
silent unsigned fallback. The self-check requires the produced
envelope to verify VERIFIED when `artifactsDir` is supplied
(VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL otherwise) AND its `envelope-signature` leg to
PASS against the registry the verifier consulted (`keysRegistry`
option / `--keys`, defaulting to savage-standard's shipped registry).
The key is chosen by the operator's registry, not by this module:
savage-verify signs under `--key-id` when passed, else the registry's
first active non-demo key, else its first active key. This module
never opens, copies or logs the private key — only savage-standard's
signer reads it.

**Evidence (measured on this tree, savage-standard @ b12cb607).**
BEFORE: a pair issued through the pre-#83 mint path produced an
issuance record of `{status, orderId, receipts}` — no envelope object,
no `signatures` member, no `savage/receipt-envelope/1` anywhere.
AFTER, with a throwaway 2048-bit operator key in a temp dir: issuance
returns pair + signed envelope; issuance itself refuses to return
unless savage-standard's verifier reports VERIFIED with artifact
bytes and a passing signature leg; the test suite re-verifies the
envelope independently through the standard's CLI (VERIFIED,
`envelope-signature` pass). Tamper control: a claim-edited copy of an
issued envelope with its `envelope_digest` honestly recomputed (the
standard's own machinery) is REJECTED by the standard's verifier with
the `envelope-signature` leg failed. Suites: delivery-ledger 19/19
baseline before; after: 24 tests — 19/19 legacy pass unchanged, and
the 5 issuance tests pass when `SAVAGE_STANDARD_DIR` names a
savage-standard checkout (they skip cleanly without it, so the suite
runs exactly as before in this repo alone). savage-standard's own
suite is untouched: 74 passed. Zero new third-party dependencies in
either repo. No private key material exists in any tree: throwaway
keys live only in test temp dirs.

Two fixture notes, disclosed: the tests' fixed `recorded_at`
(2026-11-10T23:30:00Z) precedes the keygen wall-clock `not_before` the
standard's CLI stamps on a fresh key entry, and the standard's
signature leg — by its own declared rule — reports an out-of-window
envelope as unverifiable; the test helper therefore clears
`not_before` in its temp registry (the assertion under test is the
signature itself, not an issuance-time window). And savage-standard's
verifier checks the signature against the registry it is GIVEN: a
signed envelope checked without `--keys` against the shipped registry
(which holds only the destroyed demo entry) reports the signature leg
unverifiable — issuance accounts for this by pointing its self-check
at the operator's registry.

**What remains NOT true:** no production estate signing key exists —
the shipped registry still holds only the destroyed demo entry
(residue #25, unchanged), so production issuance runs unsigned, with
the absence stated on every record, until the operator mints the real
key. NO live caller exists: nothing in a deployed path calls
`recordPayment`/`recordDelivery` or `issueSignedPair` — issuance
today IS this package's mint path, and that is exactly what is wired.
Deployment of the site's fulfillment worker remains the operator's
12-step checklist (savageaistudios-site, docs/AUTOMATED_FULFILLMENT.md);
nothing was deployed by this fix, and savageaistudios-site was not
touched. The private key remains an operator artifact that never
enters any repository.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `326b7ab7abfa5a3774466e068a1e1199c4d6f0c8` (live main tip at the 2026-11-15 verification; the merge of PR #434). Tree = 889 blobs in this evolution's tree (888 at the cited head, +1 for the new `scripts/verify-ground-truth.mjs`).
- **Tests:** the union `npm test` run (exit 0, 155 suite
  headers) recorded in the commerce-stack section below covers
  the tree through PR #442. For the PR #443–#446 landing the
  evidence is narrower and is stated as such: the targeted
  commerce suite (`npm run test:m5-commerce`) ran **exit 0** at
  the pre-merge top head and CI `npm test` was **green** at that
  head — a suite-evidence landing, with **no line-by-line
  review** performed. **2026-11-09 re-verification:** the full
  union `npm test` chain ran end-to-end **exit 0** at
  `de309b96` (the head this refresh started from) and again
  **exit 0** on the PR #449 tree, both runs ending in the

  failure, so completion is a pass for every suite in it.
- **Issue #168 still OPEN** (re-verified live 2026-11-09; re-verified live again 2026-11-15 — still OPEN, same title):
  "Final production closure: bind current main to authoritative
  ACA proof." Closing it needs a fresh Level 3 run and Savage's
  call. Production closure is **not established**. Standing
  caveat, verified in code: the Level 3 proof runner's payload
  (`scripts/prove-level3-production.mjs:19`) is a trivial
  `assert.equal(2+2, 4)` — it proves the isolated runner
  executes against production, not production behavior, and no
  closure claim may rest on it until a behavior-bearing closure
  run exists.
- The two repo-level CI items named in the 2026-11-04 catch-up

  **external-scan digest mismatch** is **stale/contradicted** —
  at `de309b96`, `npm run verify:external-scan-policy` exits 0

  whether the failure persists in the CI environment
  specifically is **unknown** (not exercised here), so it no
  longer stands as an open defect on local evidence. The
  **Stage-5 dependency-vulnerability gate** is a CI-side audit
  policy that local runs cannot exercise — carried as

- **Secret separation landed 2026-11-09 (PR #449, defect D2):**
  the operator session secret no longer falls back to

## Evolution 2026-11-15 — `verify:ground-truth` (mechanical re-check)

**Capability:** `npm run verify:ground-truth`
(`scripts/verify-ground-truth.mjs`, Node stdlib only, no new
dependencies) mechanically re-checks the claims in the block below
against the live checkout and fails, naming the claim, when this
file and the tree disagree. It follows the repo's existing
`verify:*` idiom (cf. `verify:external-scan-policy`, whose policy
check it also re-runs as GT-09).

**Metric:** BEFORE — GT falsifiable claims under mechanical
re-check = 0 (no `verify:ground-truth` in `package.json`, no
verifier script). AFTER — 10/10 enumerated claims mechanized
(GT-01…GT-10, plus the GT-00 block-parse guard). Planted-drift
control on a scratch copy: every checked claim mutated in turn
(wrong head, wrong count, wrong membership, and each other claim's
target) → verifier failed naming that claim, 10/10 caught; the
unmutated tree passes.

**Claims block (machine-readable; the verifier parses exactly this):**

<!-- GT-CLAIMS-BEGIN -->
```json
{
  "snapshotHead": "326b7ab7abfa5a3774466e068a1e1199c4d6f0c8",
  "blobCount": 889,
  "unionDirectRefs": 122,
  "unionUniqueRefs": 121,
  "unionLeafRuns": 148,
  "unionUniqueLeaves": 147,
  "level3PayloadLine": 19,
  "absentPath": "src/crew/crew-runner.mjs"
}
```
<!-- GT-CLAIMS-END -->

**Mechanized (10):**
- GT-01 snapshot-head consistency — header, Head bullet and the
  claims block cite the same head.
- GT-02 snapshot-head ancestry — the cited head is HEAD or an
  ancestor of HEAD in a git checkout, or equals `$OVERMIND_GT_HEAD`
  when the commit object is not local; otherwise SKIP (reported,
  never counted as a pass).
- GT-03 blob count — tracked-file count of the tree equals the
  claimed count (889 in this evolution's tree).
- GT-04 union-suite membership — every `npm run X` in the union
  `test` chain exists (122 direct refs, 121 unique), the recursive
  expansion matches the claim (148 leaf runs, 147 unique), and
  every leaf's node target file exists.
- GT-05 Level 3 trivial payload — `scripts/prove-level3-production.mjs:19`
  is the trivial `assert.equal(2+2, 4)` payload the standing
  caveat above describes.
- GT-06 auth session-secret separation (PR #449 / D2) — the
  session secret is read only from `OVERMIND_AUTH_SESSION_SECRET`,
  production config requires it at ≥ 32 chars and distinct from
  `OVERMIND_CELL_SECRET`, and no fallback to the cell secret exists.
- GT-07 auth session secret not provisioned — no file under
  `.github/workflows/` mentions `OVERMIND_AUTH_SESSION_SECRET`.
- GT-08 crew-runner absent — `src/crew/crew-runner.mjs` is absent
  on this tree (the unlanded M7 item above).
- GT-09 external-scan policy — the sibling
  `verify:external-scan-policy` exits 0 with `policy-ok`.
- GT-10 README pointer — README.md links this file and states
  that it wins.

**Deliberately NOT mechanized (and why):**
- Issue #168's live state and title, and the open-PRs state —
  GitHub-side state, not falsifiable from a checkout; a checkout
  script has no API credential. (Both were re-verified live by

**Canonical branch:** main @ 9bcd2a241e59790a7b392dd666a297e5bf748ec6

## What this repo is

Evidence-first neutral content discovery and controlled short-form
experiment engine — the estate's canonical surface for candidate
discovery and neutral dry-run evaluation. It supports the
advertising/content distribution engine; monetization is
downstream of actual publication and measured conversion.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `9bcd2a241e59790a7b392dd666a297e5bf748ec6` (pre-fix-#96 main; PR #12 and the stacked draft PRs #3–#11 also sit on top of this line — see Open PRs). Tree = 40 blobs.
- **Tests (zero dependencies):** **25/25 pass** (`node --test`) at `9bcd2a24`;
  **27/27 pass** with the fix-#96 change below (2 tests added).
- Products ON now: 1 — internal discovery/experiment pipeline
  library.

## Merged in the 2026-11-03 Tonight Sprint train

- **#2** — live public demand signals + evidence-bound portfolio
  offer review. Read-only GETs to the official Hacker News Firebase
  public API produce schema-validated observations (points are NOT
  relabeled as likes); a deterministic reviewer matches them against
  an explicit offer catalog. Every output is non-commercial proof:
  matches are `human_review_required`, and the records state
  `outreach_performed: false`, `buyer_intent_verified: false`,
  `revenue_verified: false`. This is a research capability, not
  sales evidence.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- Experiment/ranking output does not prove publication, audience
  response, or revenue unless channel receipts and metrics are
  added — none are.
- The audit's named short-build (not built): wire one live signal
  source + one approved publishing channel into a running discovery
  loop (days; mostly approvals, not code). PR #2 wires the signal
  source only; no publishing channel is connected.

## Fix #96 — offer-review source-trust allowlist parameterized (D2)

- `buildOfferReview` (`src/offer-review.mjs`) hard-coded trust to the
  single source name `hacker_news_official_api` inline in its
  observation gate; no caller could widen or replace the trusted set
  without editing source. It now accepts a `trustedSourceNames`
  option in the function's existing options object, defaulting to the
  exported frozen constant `TRUSTED_SOURCE_NAMES` =
  `["hacker_news_official_api"]` — the historical list, verbatim.
  Supplied lists are validated (non-empty array of unique non-empty
  strings) and fail closed with `invalid trusted source names`;
  the URL-pattern and `confidence === "observed"` legs of the gate
  are unchanged.
- Proof: suite 25/25 before → 27/27 after (2 tests added pinning the
  default list and the override governing); a fixed offline probe
  (collect + review) produces byte-identical output before/after in
  default mode; an override adding `hacker_news_algolia_public_search`
  accepts that source (rejected by default), and a replacement list
  rejects the historical source.
- Scope limit, stated plainly: the URL leg of the gate still pins
  `news.ycombinator.com` item URLs, so the parameter governs the
  source-name dimension only. A future source on another host still
  needs its URL shape admitted — that was not D2's target and is not
  claimed here.
- Note for the stack landing: the gpt/* stack tip carries its own
  one-line variant of this gate (it adds
  `hacker_news_algolia_public_search` inline). When the stack lands,
  that line should be re-expressed through this parameter.

  evolution draft #12); none merged.

No direction ruled by Savage for this repo.

## Fix #100 — defect D4: BOM in root package.json (2026-11-10)

Scoped entry for D4 only; the head pin and figures above are unchanged
(GT currency is a separate queue row).

- **Defect:** the root `package.json` began with a UTF-8 BOM

- **Fix:** the 3 BOM bytes were stripped; the remaining 144 bytes are

# agent-pay — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-05 (completion push: PRs #86/#87/#88 merged — see the final addendum)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 8c4e804b27bd (see the addenda at the end of this file)

## What this repo is

AgentPay: the proof-carrying IOU / agent-payment library (pure ESM,
`node --test`) — signed mandates, Ed25519 signed route quotes,
serialized budget reservation, a sealed ledger, and an
independent-witness anti-rollback layer. Note: it *mirrors* the
savage-agent-protocol surface with its own dependency-free copy
rather than consuming that package (protocol gate item 1, PARTIAL).

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `88f2991746` — the merge of PR #27. Tree = 133 blobs.
- **Tests:** at the audit freeze (head `281fc2c499`) the suite was
  **16/16**, with digest-only proof and no signatures. The
  2026-11-01 merge train landed the full 25-PR chain (#1, #3–#26)
  plus #27; post-merge main was re-fetched and re-tested by the
  coordinator: **238/238 tests pass**, byte-identical to the
  pre-verified stack tip.
- What the chain landed (per its own documents): Ed25519
  provider-signed quotes with a trusted issuer registry, signed
  owner/operator mandates with spend limits, file-serialized budget
  reservation that fails closed, a signed ledger seal, and an
  independently-keyed witness service for anti-rollback.

## Superseded text

The prior version of this file described a Phase 2 *review branch*
(`terra/phase2-agentpay-payout-reconciliation-20261029`) as this
repo's ground truth. That branch's substance reached main through
the train chain above; the branch document no longer describes
main and is replaced by this file.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **No real provider execution:** no authentic Stripe payout has
  been observed end-to-end; bank receipt / irreversibility is NOT
  VERIFIED and NOT IMPLEMENTED. A provider-reported "paid" payout
  may later fail.
- No hosted deployment, no live charge, no customer, no revenue.
  Production gates named by the chain's own docs remain open
  (shared transactional store, independently witnessed checkpoints
  operated by a separate operator, key lifecycle/revocation, real
  third-party bid acquisition, toll collection).

grew monotonically 12 → 132 blobs, zero shrinks) and **#27**
(witnessed-reservation lock-theft rejection; tree 132 → 133).

## Addendum — 2026-11-04 (Tights): flaky ledger-race family CLOSED — PR #74 merged
- **Root cause PROVEN** (declaration-first lane; DECLARATION.md filed before any fix work; evidence in the lane's DIAGNOSIS.md): the descriptor-bound readers required **ctimeNs exactly equal** across two stat calls inside one read. On this class of filesystem (coarse/multigrain timestamps) an untouched file's reported ctime advances mid-read with no writer — captured red-handed with ctimeNs the ONLY diverging field (+1.000 ms quantization steps) under parallel suite load. Baseline main `94e0593b`: 2/10 full-suite runs green, 14 false failures rotating; parallel repro 22/150 false failures on writer-free files.
- **Fix (PR #74, merged):** ctimeNs removed from the intra-read equality guards in 7 modules (file-ledger, private-ledger-read, private-ledger-continuity, payout-file-transaction, private-issuance-input, private-witness-log ×2, verified-capture-store). Retained: dev/ino, size, mtimeNs, nlink, and ALL SHA-256 fingerprint logic. New control test (`test/intra-read-race-control.test.mjs`) proves a genuine mid-read byte-flip still refuses with `changed_during_read`. Disclosed tradeoff: ctime uniquely caught only a same-UID writer that rewrites in place AND restores mtime via utimensat inside the read window — already scoped out by the module headers; persistent changes remain fingerprint-caught.
- **Verification:** lane 7 consecutive green runs 439/439 + parallel repro 0/150; Tights independently materialized the head tree (229 blobs, SHA-1 clean) and ran the suite twice — 439/439 both, control test 3/3. Counts reconcile: 436 (main) + 3 new control tests = 439.
- **Named sibling defect (NOT part of #74, next finishing item):** two-process licensed-unit publication race — `enterprise-license-meter` / `enterprise-licensed-capacity` publish entries by direct write with zero rename calls, so a concurrent scanner can open a half-written entry (`*_entry_changed_or_incomplete`; sighted once on baseline, once on the fixed tree). Fix direction: atomic publication via rename or scan-side reconciliation, under its own declaration-first lane.


## Addendum — 2026-11-04 (Tights): publication race CLOSED — PR #76 merged
- **Defect:** `enterprise-license-meter` / `enterprise-licensed-capacity` publish entries by O_EXCL-creating the final filename and writing bytes afterwards (zero rename calls); a concurrent scanner could trip `*_entry_changed_or_incomplete` on the half-written newest entry (lane repro on pre-fix main: 35/16,132 attempts under reader pressure, snapshots always on the newest entry).
- **Fix (PR #76, merge `7b4e2a65`):** scan-side reconciliation — exported reads retry the byte-identical verification pass only on `entry_changed_or_incomplete`, bounded by caps (100 attempts / 2000 ms); success still requires one complete verification pass, so retry cannot launder bad bytes. Rename/link publication was rejected on three verified invariant collisions (unexpected-file rejection vs temp names, `nlink === 1n` vs link/unlink, O_EXCL exclusivity vs rename-overwrite).
- **Hardening (same PR, after Tights' verification HELD the first version):** the first fix's 50 ms directory-stillness "at rest" exit was itself convicted — a descheduled writer leaves a still fingerprint mid-publication (deterministic repro: a +300 ms completer delay failed both in-flight settle tests at 53-59 ms). The stillness exit and `directoryFingerprint` were removed; settle waits out the full budget, then rethrows the original error unchanged. Disclosed cost: at-rest incomplete entries now reject after up to ~2 s instead of ~55 ms. Two new +300 ms slow-completion regression controls fail on the held code and pass on the fix; the test diff was additions only (+59/-0, no existing test modified).
