Tights independently materialized the final head tree (230 blobs, SHA-1 clean) and ran the full suite 3x — 445/445 each, full logs — plus the settle file 3x 6/6. Post-merge tree proof: main == PR head on all 230 blobs, zero differing paths. Counts reconcile: 439 + 4 lane-1 settle tests + 2 hardening controls = 445.

The witness path is byte-identical to pre-#76 main and imports nothing #76 touched; 58 subsequent witness-path executions (standalone + pristine-main suites) reproduced zero unintentional failures. # savage-agent-protocol — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 (live API state; audit evidence 2026-10-29; ruling D5)
**Canonical branch:** main @ c3c24bd470

## What this repo is

Private vendor-neutral agent authorization, payment, and proof
protocol package — typed primitives + JSON Schemas for spend
authority, payment intents/receipts, and proof envelopes for agent
commerce. An extraction candidate, not production authority.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `c3c24bd470` (unchanged since the audit freeze). Tree = 38 blobs.
- **Verify run (audit, Lane D):** GREEN — typecheck + build +
  **21/21 tests** + `npm pack` dry-run succeeds (14.3 kB). The
  package is mechanically publish-ready and **deliberately
  unpublished**.
- **Proof here is digest-recomputation only: no signatures exist in
  source** (audit). Forgery — not just tampering — is unaddressed
  until a signing layer lands.

## Release gate — RELEASE_DECISION (2026-09-16), restated by D5

The package stays private until its 5 gate items close:

1. agent-pay consumes it or mirrors its API — **PARTIAL:** agent-pay
   currently *mirrors* the surface with its own dependency-free
   copy rather than consuming the package.
2. One proof-carrying payment flow implemented against it — **not
   done** (no live payment flow exists against either copy).
3. Semver policy documented.
4. CI green.
5. Export-safety keeps passing (the test asserting no private
   names/credentials/path escapes leak into the package).

## Known defects / honest gaps

- Missing for adversarial use: an Ed25519/ML-DSA signing +
  revocation layer (the audit's named build, days-scale, unbuilt).
- Private CEROS runtime logic, secrets, and internal strategy are
  intentionally outside this package's boundary.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing — the train took no action in this repo.

## Parked PRs

None — no open PRs.

## Where it is going

Ruled: **D5 — the protocol package stays private until its 5 gate
items close.** Publication itself is a separate decision for
Savage when the gate closes.

## CI gate — tests workflow (added 2026-11-10, fix #80)

- **Pre-existing workflow:** `.github/workflows/verify.yml` has been
  in the tree since 2026-09-16 (blob `a1b933535c`, bytes unchanged
  across the period below) and runs `npm run verify` (typecheck +
  build + tests + pack dry-run) on push and pull_request with
  Node 22. Its Actions runs were green 27 times, most recently run
  42142635848 on 2026-11-06. From 2026-11-06T02:14Z (creation of a
  since-deleted workflow record with path `BuildFailed`) until
  2026-11-10, every push and pull_request event on this repo
  produced only `startup_failure` runs with zero jobs, and the
  verify workflow did not execute. Cause not established from the
  API evidence. On 2026-11-10 the verify workflow executed green
  again on the fix-#80 branches (runs 42915950699 push and
  42915992290 pull_request). verify.yml itself is left exactly as
  found.
- **New gate:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` — job
  `test (Node 22)` on `ubuntu-latest`; triggers: pull_request,

  setup-node 22, `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`,

  (`package.json` engines `>=22`, `@types/node ^22`, and the

  all 8 test files, no subsetting, no continue-on-error, no

## What is NOT true

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

## Addendum 2026-11-11 — P7: quota-ledger and refund-policy wired into the public package API (fix #118, PR open, unverified until merged)

- **Defect (audit P7, verified):** `src/quota-ledger.ts` and `src/refund-policy.ts` shipped in the package tarball with full test suites (13 + 18 tests, imported by relative source path) but were not exported from `src/index.ts`, and `package.json` exposes only the package root (`"."`), so consumers could not reach `replayQuota`, `appendQuota`, or `reconcileRefundEntitlement` at all. A targeted import of the built root on pristine main `dda59cc14d957094e500cc8c13280d911f40aacf` confirmed all three are `undefined` for package consumers while the other 14 public functions resolve.
- **Fix:** `src/index.ts` now re-exports `./quota-ledger.js` and `./refund-policy.js` alongside the existing ten modules, wiring their functions and types (`QuotaEvent`, `QuotaEntry`, `QuotaState`, `RefundSnapshot`, `RefundDecision`) through the single declared entry point. No implementation changed; no subpath exports added; no export name collides with any existing module (full export census taken before the change).
- **Guard:** new `test/package-entry.test.ts` imports the built package by name (`@savagnic/savage-agent-protocol`, resolved through the exports map) and asserts every documented public function exists on the package root, that `dist/index.d.ts` re-exports both modules, and that quota replay/append and refund reconciliation behave correctly through the root. The test builds first if `dist/` is absent, so it also passes under the tests workflow's bare `npm test`.
- **Verified in this change:** pristine main suite 54/54; branch suite **58/58** (54 + 4 new), typecheck clean, `npm run verify` exit 0, tarball still 40 files; post-change built-root probe shows all 17 documented functions as `function`.
- **Census dispositions:** declared-but-not-wired = the two modules above (now wired). Wired-but-not-declared = none. Declared with no implementation anywhere = none among entry points, so no declaration was withdrawn. (`AuthorityDecision` remains a type-only data contract — that is defect P11, a separate queue row, untouched here.)
- **Status correction to the addendum below:** the Pay on Proof addendum was written while its PR was open; PR #38 has since merged and main stands at `dda59cc14d957094e500cc8c13280d911f40aacf` (verified via the GitHub API on 2026-11-11). The "Verified current state" header near the top of this file (head `c3c24bd470`, 21/21 tests) predates both the CI-gate section and these addenda and is stale; the dated sections govern.

## Addendum 2026-11-11 — Pay on Proof conformance standard (PR open, unverified until merged)

- **Added:** `schemas/pay-on-proof-conformance.json` — the frozen conformance fixture for delivery-acceptance evaluation (the PAY-E1 settlement gate's checker standard): 16 cases covering conformant deliveries (incl. extras, nested field paths, deep-equal object fields, scalar type fidelity), product mismatch, missing/digest-mismatched artifacts, field missing/mismatch, missing evidence types, and multi-failure accumulation in the fixed verdict order. Plus `src/pay-on-proof.ts`, this repo's reference implementation of `evaluateConformance` / `validateCriteria`, exported from `src/index.ts`.
- **Why here:** this repo is where the estate's shared conformance fixtures live (the triadic precedent); the standard must be implementable by third parties, so the fixture — not agent-pay's code — is the definition. agent-pay vendors the fixture byte-identically (`test/fixtures/`, SHA-256 `f17b68844434c17051a6f747a3c8f1f50fd9c3cf1e6f68cb4b7cbdf67100c46c` pinned by its agreement test), so drift between the two implementations breaks a suite on whichever side moves.
- **Verified in this change:** `npm run typecheck` clean; suite 52 → **54/54**, including the fixture-agreement test over all 16 cases and declaration-validation tests.
- **What is NOT true:** this repo gains no gate, ledger, or settlement behavior — it carries the checker standard and a reference evaluator only. The gate itself lives in agent-pay (companion PR); no payment rail is integrated anywhere by these changes.

## Addendum 2026-11-13 — fix-program queue rows 131 / 132 / 133 (PRs open, unverified until merged)

State at the start of this pass: main `d8457271f14c8f73ebb8492a59658305412932d6`, suite **58/58**, typecheck clean (all re-run first-hand for this pass; the "Verified current state" header at the top of this file remains stale — head `c3c24bd470`, 21/21 tests — and the dated sections govern).

- **Row 131 (P3 — proof format accepted forged/shaped proofs): PREMISE VERIFIED, FIXED.** `verifyProofEnvelope` performed no runtime schema validation: a probe envelope with `version: '999.0.0'`, empty subject/claim, `createdAt: 'not-a-date'`, and one undigested self-asserted evidence item returned `{ state: 'verified', reasons: [] }`, as did variants with extra properties, an out-of-enum evidence type, a non-canonical digest, and an impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`). Fix: `src/proof.ts` now validates the full envelope — and any nested payment intent/receipt — against the shipped schemas before any binding check runs, and exports the validator as `validateProofEnvelope` so embedders apply the identical contract. The one deliberate tightening beyond the previously shipped schema: every evidence item must carry a canonical `sha256:` digest (a bare `{ type, ref }` item is an unbound assertion); `schemas/proof-envelope.schema.json` now states the same requirement (`digest` required, `pattern: ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$`), so code and declaration move together. Six adversarial tests join `test/proof.test.ts`, including the audit counterexample verbatim and a positive control (a schema-valid, digest-bound non-payment proof still verifies). Suite 58 → **64/64**, typecheck clean. **Scope honesty:** this closes the *shape* hole only. A self-consistent forged intent+receipt pair still verifies, because verification is digest recomputation without a signing layer — that is the CRITICAL queue row 164 (P1) scope, untouched here, and the README now says so in plain language.
- **Row 132 (P4 — conformance coverage partial, declared cases unrun): PREMISE DOES NOT REPRODUCE on current main — closed on evidence, no code change.** The repo declares exactly two machine-readable conformance case sets: `schemas/triadic-conformance.json` (20 cases) and `schemas/pay-on-proof-conformance.json` (16 cases). Both are iterated case-by-case by the canonical suite (`test/triadic.test.ts`, `test/pay-on-proof.test.ts` — each loops every fixture case and asserts the full expected verdict), both tests are inside the `npm test` glob (`test/*.test.ts`), and both CI workflows run that suite (`.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs `npm test`; `verify.yml` runs `npm run verify`, which includes it). The baseline run for this pass shows both fixture tests passing inside the 58/58 suite. The pay-on-proof half of this coverage landed 2026-11-11 (see the addendum above), after the queue row was written; the row is closed by that landing plus the pre-existing triadic coverage, re-verified here — not by new work in this pass.
- **Row 133 (P5 — front-door claims ahead of code): PREMISE VERIFIED, FIXED.** The README's only example built a proof from a receipt with **no `paymentIntent` attached** — the exact shape the verifier rejects (`payment_intent_required`) — so the front door demonstrated a flow that cannot verify (the same defect as `examples/mock-purchase.ts`, which remains a separate queue item). The README also omitted four shipped public surfaces (Pay on Proof conformance, quota ledger, refund policy, triadic/Diamond), claimed framework "compatibility" (MCP/LangGraph/OpenHands/CrewAI) with no integration code in the repo, and stated the idempotency fail-closed claim without its caller-supplied-set precondition. Fix: `README.md` rewritten from the proven state — full public surface, the corrected example, the security model scoped to what the code enforces, and an explicit "what verification does not establish" section (no signatures; `verified` = schema-valid + internally consistent). New guard `test/readme-example.test.ts` executes the documented flow end to end (and pins the old shape's rejection), so the front door cannot drift silently again. Suite after rows 131 + 133 land: **65/65** (verified on the combined tree pre-landing).
- **Observed, left as provenance (not silently rewritten):** `EXPORT-MANIFEST.json`'s verification block (16 tests, 28 files, a 2025-era workflow run id) is a historical export record, not a current-state claim; it is stale against today's tree and is flagged here rather than edited, because its numbers are evidence about the export event, not about current main.

## Addendum 2026-11-13 — row 164 signing layer landed (fix #144) + envelope default flipped (fix #150) + row 111 walkthrough (fix #146, PR #43 open)

This addendum discharges the doc deltas specified in the row-164 design (DESIGN.md §8), which PR #42's filing deferred because the README and this file were mid-flight in PRs #40/#41 at the time.

- **Row 164 (CRITICAL — proof verification authenticated nothing): premise verified, FIXED by fix #144 (PR #42, merged; main `68ad82f2`).** A fabricated intent ("authority-that-never-authorized-this", $9,999) plus a fabricated provider receipt formed a self-consistent pair that `verifyProofEnvelope` returned `{ state: "verified", reasons: [] }` for — proven on pristine main and again on main + the row-131 payload. The build: an Ed25519 attestation layer (`src/signing.ts`, `node:crypto` only, zero new dependencies) with three roles — `intent` (the spend authority's issuer), `receipt` (the payment provider's issuer), `envelope` (the claimant) — each signing a byte-specified canonical five-line string (domain + role separation; `kid` and `signedAt` inside the signed bytes; the envelope digest excludes only `signatures`). Key ids are self-certifying (`ed25519:` + base64url(SHA-256 of the SPKI DER)); trust comes only from a verifier-configured `IssuerRegistry` with per-role bindings, validity windows, and revocation — a key carried inside an envelope is an unexpected property and fails schema validation. `verifySignedProofEnvelope` is fail-closed in three legs: schema (`validateProofEnvelope`) → structure (the existing binding checks, called, not copied) → signatures (unsigned → `proof_unsigned`; a registered key's broken attestation is never silently dropped). Suite chain for the landing: 58 → 64 (row 131) → 87/87; re-measured for this addendum on main `68ad82f2`: **88/88**, typecheck clean.
- **The judgment call, and its ruling.** PR #42 deliberately did NOT flip `verifyProofEnvelope` itself: it kept returning `verified` for unsigned, self-consistent envelopes, with the disclosure "verified ≠ authenticated". That call was the crew's best reading of rows 131/133 scope — stated here, as DESIGN.md §8 requires, as decided-there, NOT decided by Savage. On 2026-11-13 Savage ruled on the question directly ("go with the math"): flip the default. Fix #150 (this addendum's PR) executes the ruling.
- **Fix #150 — the envelope default is now fail-closed.** `verifyProofEnvelope` runs the consistency checks and then rejects any envelope carrying no issuer attestations: `{ state: "rejected", reasons: ["proof_unsigned"] }` (the signed verifier's existing reason code). The consistency core survives under an explicitly honest name — `checkProofEnvelopeConsistency` — whose documentation states in plain language that it DOES NOT VERIFY: its `verified` state means "internally consistent", and a self-consistent forged pair still passes it, because no signatures are consulted. `verifySignedProofEnvelope`'s leg 2 now composes the renamed function; its outcomes are unchanged. What each tier's `verified` asserts: consistency check = schema-valid + internally consistent; default = those, plus at least one well-formed attestation present (genuineness NOT asserted — no registry is consulted); signed verifier = those, plus every asserted fact attested by a registry-trusted key. **Negative control (first-hand, this pass):** the row-164 repro pair (fabricated authority + fabricated provider, bound by `bindReceipt`, built by `createProofEnvelope`) — on pristine main `68ad82f2`, `verifyProofEnvelope` returned `{"state":"verified","reasons":[]}`; on the fix-#150 tree it returns `{"state":"rejected","reasons":["proof_unsigned"]}`, the consistency check still returns `verified` (labeled, expected), and `verifySignedProofEnvelope` against an empty registry returns `proof_unsigned` exactly as before. **Suite: 88/88 → 91/91** (+3 flip tests in `test/proof.test.ts`; the signing premise test now pins all three tiers; `npm run verify` exit 0, tarball 42 files, zero regressions).
- **Consumer disclosure.** In-repo callers of `verifyProofEnvelope` were: `src/signing.ts` (leg 2 — now composes `checkProofEnvelopeConsistency`), the test suite, the README example + its guard test (rewritten to the signed flow in this PR), and `examples/mock-purchase.ts` (row 111's file — see below; untouched here because PR #43 owns it). Estate consumers: agent-pay's settlement gate consumes `verifySignedProofEnvelope` (PAY-E1) — its outcomes are unchanged by this flip; agent-pay's mirrored surface adopting the signing standard is agent-pay's own follow-on (DESIGN.md §8), not built here. Diamond promotion-path authentication remains a separate row's scope — this layer signs the proof path only. Any other consumer of the package default, in any repo, must now present attested envelopes or explicitly call the labeled consistency check: that behavior change is the point of the ruling.
- **Row 111 (P8 — the shipped example demonstrated a rejected flow): FIXED by fix #146, PR #43 — OPEN at this addendum's writing, unverified until merged.** PR #43 rewrites `examples/mock-purchase.ts` as a self-verifying walkthrough: the happy path (authority → intent → adapter → receipt → proof, verified end to end), every error path the proof verifier declares (missing evidence → `unknown`; `payment_receipt_required`; `payment_intent_required`; identity, digest, and terms mismatch; receipt not bound by evidence; receipt digest mismatch), and the execution layer's five declared failures (amount exceeds authority, merchant not authorized, idempotency key reused, provider authorization intent mismatch, receipt amount mismatch). Every demonstrated outcome is asserted by the example itself (it exits non-zero on drift) and a guard test (`test/mock-purchase-example.test.ts`) runs it in the suite; the guard was proven to fail against the old example. Filed suite on its branch base: 58 → 59. **Sequencing note:** PR #43's happy path asserts `verifyProofEnvelope` → `verified` on an unsigned envelope, which was true on its base; under this addendum's flipped default that assertion must be updated when PR #43 is rebased for landing (attach issuer attestations, as the README example now does). PR #43 is not modified by fix #150.
- **Operator residue (unchanged by either fix):** no production issuer exists estate-wide. Minting a real issuer key, keeping its private half in operator secrets off-repo, and registering the public half in verifiers' registries are operator acts; until they happen, no production envelope can be attested.
- **Status corrections to earlier sections of this file:** the "Known defects" bullet calling the signing + revocation layer "unbuilt" is superseded — the Ed25519 layer is built (fix #144) and the default is flipped (fix #150); an ML-DSA leg remains not built (Ed25519 shipped; `algorithm` is the declared agility point). "Parked PRs: None" is stale — PR #43 is open (above). The "Verified current state" header remains stale as previously noted; the dated sections govern.
- **What is NOT true:** this layer does not authenticate real-world providers — it authenticates keys a verifier's operator chose to trust for a provider name; whether the named provider is the real-world provider remains the operator's registry decision. `verifyProofEnvelope`'s `verified` does not assert any signature is genuine. `checkProofEnvelopeConsistency`'s `verified` asserts consistency only, and the function is not a verifier despite returning a `VerificationResult`.

# STAR — Ground Truth

**Pass 2 — re-verified 2026-11-11** against the live tree (every in-repo claim below was re-measured in this pass; claims resting on out-of-repo live checks carry their original check date and are labeled accordingly).
Canonical branch: main @ `bc59edcb78937ee0c9b5cd8c3de028be84ad386b` (unchanged since 2026-11-04)
Project: private `Savages-studios/star-of-the-beginning` (NOT `Savages-studios/star` — the app *Starr* — Savage Forge, Savage Genesis, or Savage Video Studio)
Status: SCENE 1 AUDIOVISUAL PRODUCTION UNDER DEVELOPMENT; NO COMPLETED AUTHOR-APPROVED SCENE

## (a) What this repository is

Not software. This repo is the **manuscript-custody record and film-production bible** for the novel *Star: The Convergence Cycle*, Book One of the STAR series. There is no code, no test suite, and no CI in this repo (verified 2026-11-11: 35 files, all documents/media; zero code, test, or workflow files). The verification standard here is custody (SHA-256) and claim discipline — see (d).

Only two areas hold substance:

- **`manuscript/`** — the complete filed Book One text and the untouched sources it was assembled from, pinned by a SHA-256 custody manifest.
- **`production/skills/`** plus **`.agents/skills/`** — the paper trail and eight repository-local agent skills for adapting Scene 1 to video via external generators (Higgsfield/WAN/Kling/Seedance): generation ledger, prompt library, approved-frame hash lists, shot queue, changelog, learnings.

The other five directories the structure names — `series-bible/`, `canon/`, `assets/`, `marketing/`, `research/` — are **planned structure only**: each contains exactly one placeholder README stating what will belong there, and no content (verified 2026-11-11; see (c) and (e)).

## (b) Declared spec

- `README.md` — declares the separation of manuscript text, series canon, research, marketing, and production assets "so story truth is not mixed with promotional or exploratory material," and names GROUND_TRUTH.md the current-state authority. **As of this Pass 2 landing, the README also states which directories actually hold content and which are placeholder-only** — before this landing it described all six areas as if they held content (corrected; see (e)).
- `AGENTS.md` — manuscript, series bible, and canon stay separate from production experiments and research; an AI image, draft, or marketing output is **not canon** unless explicitly approved by the author; the final repository update for any work must fully refresh GROUND_TRUTH.md (this refresh is that update for the fix-program rows B-2/B-3).
- This file — the current-state authority for repository status. Story canon belongs in `canon/` and the series bible once they exist, not here.

Where any document disagrees with (c)/(e) below, (c)/(e) — proven from the files — win.

## (c) Component state (re-measured 2026-11-11)

| Component | State | Evidence (2026-11-11 unless noted) |
|---|---|---|
| Book One master (`manuscript/BOOK-ONE-MASTER.md`) | **verified** | 653,487 bytes; SHA-256 recomputed `a1b36c17ff555e3c96fbce3caec125c684dc20e7cdc1c74c0edf06d9de6c4cff` — matches `manuscript/SOURCE-MANIFEST.md` exactly |

An animatic using static image pans does **not** count as actor animation (continuity-quality-gate rule).

## Generated video and actual limits (recorded 2026-10-15; not re-verified — media are out-of-repo)

- Earlier 5s Kling entrance video, 4× 5s Seedance Mini videos from wrong/older OpenArt refs, and a 2s actor-free Grok Lite insert were completed; these are **rendered candidates** requiring real film/performance QA.

## Film status / next work (unchanged from the 2026-10-15 record)

1. Complete a signed-in `higgsfield.ai` **website** session under the author's chosen account; verify WAN 3.0/Prime model, free flag, and eligible resolution/duration before any submission. This repo's Higgsfield MCP connection **cannot** spend a website-only Unlimited offer.

3. Inspect 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% and all relevant hands/faces; mark videos PASS/REPAIR/REJECT. One film render passing does not automatically imply other shots pass.
4. Add properly cast dialogue, voice consistency, lip-sync, location ambience, spill Foley, and short subtle magical spark; composite and recut only passed video. Preserve originals and tests.

# savageaistudios-site — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-11 (Knights, fixes #101 + #102 session: API state re-read, tree materialized with every blob SHA-1 verified, suite and censuses run on the exact tree)
**Canonical branch:** main @ `4efd64869a0ced6c4f9bf046b629e09417dba6d7` (this refresh lands on top of that head in its fix PR)

**Verification basis for every current-state figure below:** `GET /repos/Savages-studios/savageaistudios-site/git/ref/heads/main` (head above); recursive tree of that commit = 178 entries / **122 blobs**, each blob fetched and git-SHA-1 verified (122/122); `npm test` and the census commands named in each section, all run on the materialized tree this session. The dated sections after the Historical record banner are retained verbatim from earlier verifications and describe their own dates; where they conflict with the current-state sections, the current-state sections govern.

## What this repo is

The public website for Savage AI Studios (savageaistudios.com,
served by GitHub Pages since the 2026-11-03 DNS flip; the in-tree
`CNAME` is `savageaistudios.com`). A static site — 64 HTML pages, no
build step — plus the estate's commerce machinery in `api/` (Stripe
webhook, purchase ledger, fulfillment engine), which runs only where
an operator deploys `server.mjs`; the public apex is static hosting
and executes none of it. (Overmind's site is ovmtruth.com, a
different surface.)

## Verified current state (2026-11-11)

- **Head / tree:** main @ `4efd64869a0ced6c4f9bf046b629e09417dba6d7`,
  122 blobs — **verified** (API re-read + SHA-1-verified
  materialization, this session).
- **Tests:** `npm test` (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, 16 test
  files) — **118/118 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped** on the exact tree
  above (Knights' local run, Node v24.22.1) — **verified**. The
  previous GT head figures (suite 82/82, 43 links) and the audit-era
  re-measurement (93/93, 62) are both superseded by this section.
- **Pages:** **64 HTML pages** — 11 at root, 45 under
  `products/<slug>/`, plus `products/index.html`,
  `catalog/index.html`, and 6 under `coloring-books/` — **verified**
  (`find . -name '*.html'`). `tests/all-pages-links.test.mjs` pins
  the inventory at exactly 64 and verifies every local href/src path
  and fragment target across all of them.
- **Analytics:** the PostHog snippet (`posthog.init`; the project
  key is a public client key by design) is present in **64/64
  pages** — **verified** (`grep -rl posthog.init --include='*.html'`).
  Whether events are currently being ingested is an account-side
  read — **not established** from this repo.
- **Commerce surface (inventory only):** **19 distinct
  `buy.stripe.com` checkout URLs** in the HTML — 45 page-link pairs
  across 15 files — **verified** with the repo's own collector
  (`collectStorefrontCheckoutLinks` in
  `scripts/audit-stripe-storefront.mjs`, the same inventory the
  suite runs against the real tree). Inventory is not liveness:
  nothing in this repo establishes that any given link currently
  renders or charges (see "What is NOT true").
- **Contact:** the site takes inquiries by **mailto** —
  `mailto:savagnic@gmail.com` appears **200 times across 59 HTML
  files** (waitlist buttons, direct-contact lines) — **verified**.
  There is **no web form anywhere in the tree** (zero `<form`
  elements, zero formsubmit references) since fix #101, below —
  **verified**.
- **Fulfillment:** `api/` holds 5 modules (fulfillment engine,
  fulfillment manifest, purchase ledger, Stripe verifier, Stripe
  webhook). The production manifest wires exactly **6 automated
  SKUs** — the five Glitch coloring-book SKUs and
  `COLORING-BOOKS-BUNDLE-29` — with a held-SKU refusal set —
  **verified** from `api/fulfillment-manifest.mjs`. Deployment
  state: **built, NOT deployed** — no Stripe endpoint registration,
  sender configuration, or live checkout is evidenced anywhere in
  this repo, and the operator checklist in
  `docs/AUTOMATED_FULFILLMENT.md` remains the go-live path —
  claim-state: **reported (standing record), consistent with all
  in-tree evidence**.
- **Open PRs:** **18** — **verified** via the API this session:
  PR #54 (Klaviyo capture, non-draft, titled DO NOT MERGE until the
  dashboard form exists; untouched by fixes #101/#102) and 17 draft
  commerce-chain PRs (#25–#53 range).
- **CI on the main head:** 7 check-runs on `4efd6486` — 5 success,
  1 skipped (`Adjust Configuration`), **1 failure
  (`homepage-static`)** — **verified** via the check-runs API; the
  failure is recorded here as fact and is out of scope for fixes
  #101/#102. Of the 7 workflow files, 3 are branch-locked to
  2026-11 `gpt/*` feature branches (`commerce-reconciliation`,

  `site-refresh` runs on pushes to main, `phase2-stripe-webhook`
  on pull requests to main, and 2 are path-filtered pull-request
  workflows — **verified** from the workflow files.

## Fix #101 (2026-11-11) — the contact form is gone; here is the evidence

Until this fix, `contact.html` carried the site's only form: a POST
to `https://formsubmit.co/savagnic@gmail.com` (raw-email endpoint;
`_next` → `contact-thanks.html`; `_captcha` on; `_honey`
honeypot). That endpoint's FormSubmit activation was **never
established**: no delivery evidence exists in this repo, and
Knights' 2026-11-11 probe could not establish it either — a GET to
the endpoint and a GET to a never-activated control address
returned byte-identical generic "Form should POST" pages (HTTP
200, differing only in per-request CSRF/Cloudflare tokens), so the
non-submission probe does not discriminate activated from
unactivated endpoints. Per queue row 54's own target, the form was
therefore **replaced with the mailto pattern used across the rest
of the site** (the bare `mailto:savagnic@gmail.com` anchor, as in
the waitlist buttons and direct-contact lines). No test submission
was sent: replacement loses no capability the site demonstrably
relies on — there is no record of a form delivery ever arriving —
so the row's probe-and-replace branch governs, not its
last-resort-submission branch. Corrections that rode along:
`legal.html` no longer describes a FormSubmit form; `about.html`'s
CTA no longer says "Use the contact form";
`invoice-readiness.html` now says "Do not attach invoice files to
your email." `contact-thanks.html` remains in the tree (the
suite's page inventory pins it), but nothing routes to it any
longer.

## What is NOT true (current, 2026-11-11)

- Automated fulfillment is **not live**: no webhook-endpoint
  deployment, Stripe endpoint registration, or sender configuration
  is evidenced; delivery for the 6 wired SKUs remains manual until
  the operator checklist in `docs/AUTOMATED_FULFILLMENT.md` is
  executed and proven.
- The 19 checkout URLs are an **inventory, not a liveness claim**:
  per-link rendering/charge state is not established by anything in
  this repo (buy.stripe.com rendering has been observed to flicker
  independently of a link's active flag; re-check at promotion
  time).
- The FormSubmit endpoint's activation was **never proven** — and
  the question is now moot: the form no longer exists.
- **No completed live sale is evidenced in this repo.** The
  purchase-ledger machinery records sales when deployed; nothing
  here proves one has occurred.
- PR #54 (Klaviyo capture) is **not merged**; no Klaviyo form
  exists on main and onsite email capture is **not established**.
- Main is **not all-green**: the `homepage-static` check-run on the
  current head is failing (see CI above).

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

## Historical record (retained verbatim; each entry describes its own date)


**2026-11-04 merge wave:** site stack PRs #10–#16 landed on main in order (merges 15e7c95041→967235e6a2), then savage-marketplace PR #170. Published pages byte-identical: old→new delta = 25 files (24 added, package.json modified), **zero HTML files changed**; the 43 buy.stripe.com URLs on the live pages are unchanged (all old-account — replacing them is the Stripe live-rewire job, untouched by this wave).

## The fulfillment gap — stated precisely

At the audit freeze this site had **no webhook and no fulfillment
machinery at all** (corrections appendix (3) governs: the defect is
absence, not a buggy webhook). Stripe could take payment across
the offers with nothing recording the sale or triggering delivery.

Post-audit merges by the account itself (before the train existed):

- **#2** — Relume upgrade, merged 2026-10-26 (`b4d5611b64`).
- **#4** — FacturForge Stripe webhook, merged 2026-10-30
  (`5d40f90fae`). The lane filing marked it DO NOT MERGE pending a
  **real Stripe checkout/fulfillment proof — which is still
  outstanding**. That is a verification debt on already-merged live
  code, carried as a Phase 2 item (a test-mode proof plan exists
  in the campaign record). The webhook's presence on main is a
  fact; its end-to-end behaviour is UNVERIFIED.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

#1 — this file's predecessor GROUND_TRUTH refresh. (The train took
no other action here; #2/#4 above predate it.)

## 2026-11-02 proposed security increment (branch-only, unmerged)

[PR #8](https://github.com/sa6ag9/savageaistudios-site/pull/8) contains private-ledger directory and symlink hardening and descriptor-bound replay-file validation, on isolated `gpt/purchase-ledger-integrity-20261102`. CI checked exact earlier PR head `95a221abea092291055e7a180cb192562cbee7af`: [run 41466251718](https://github.com/sa6ag9/savageaistudios-site/actions/runs/41466251718) passed Ubuntu (27/27, zero skips) and Windows (25 passed, 2 POSIX-only skipped) with raw logs inspected. Updating this ground-truth note and the Phase 2 documentation will require fresh exact-head CI before any merge.

Remaining gates are **independent security review, actual website webhook deployment and private persistent storage, Windows ACLs, Stripe test-mode checkout verified against correct account/price IDs, buyer fulfillment, refunds/recovery and reconciliation**. No test-mode provider call, customer delivery, production deployment, or funds movement occurred here. Do not claim revenue or launch completion.

## Update 2026-11-03 — PR #17 + PR #18 (Tights, verified first-hand)

- **PR #17 (Issue #9, duplicate-checkout fulfillment)** merged 2026-11-03 (merge commit 2c44f688): two distinct Stripe events for one checkout session now produce exactly one fulfillment record. # savage-faultline — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-10 (local-mode census fix; branch
`knights/fix-f2-local-census`, based on master @ d48383e4)
**Canonical branch:** master @ d48383e4604338f10db0036c44bf6a3918610f06

## What this repo is

The Faultline CLI: cross-repository coupling analysis for multi-repo
estates — seam maps with file:line witnesses, isolation certificates
(machine-checkable proof a repo is safe to archive/delete/hand off),
blast-radius closures, and credential fan-out detection. Zero runtime
dependencies, MIT licensed. Faultline is the estate's "proof for
code" product surface: the site sells the human-delivered Exposure
Audit ($199) and GitHub Forensic Audit ($299) built on this work.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `d48383e4` — master as of 2026-11-10. Tree = 122 blobs.
- **Open PRs:** #2 (`astra/fix-local-empty-repo-report` — fixes the
  distinct F-3 sub-1 KB emptiness defect in `sources/local.py` +
  `cli.py`, adds `tests/test_cli.py`) and #3
  (`evolution/proof-bound-20261105` — adds `analysis/migration.py` +
  `tests/test_migration.py`). Both strictly ahead of master, unmerged.
- **Tests:** `python -m pytest tests/ -q` on master @ d48383e4 →
  **85 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed** (re-verified 2026-11-10). All 18 skips
  are data-gated (`requires_real_data`; the real estate dataset is
  gitignored and absent by design). With the F-2 fix branch:
  **88 passed, 18 skipped, 0 failed** (3 new census regression tests).
- **CLI run-proven** by the audit lane against a live 2-repo probe:
  completed in ~3 s, issued 2 isolation certificates, zero config,
  zero network, zero token.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **F-2 (local census) — fixed on branch `knights/fix-f2-local-census`,
  unmerged:** local mode recognised a child directory of a multi-repo
  root only when it carried a root marker; a marker-less directory of
  pure source was dropped with no warning, so certificates were computed
  over a silently smaller estate (in the 2026-11-07 runs this flipped a
  certificate vs the GitHub-mode run). The branch counts marker-less
  source directories (GitHub mode counts a repository by existence, not
  by manifest) and reports any remaining non-repository child in
  `LocalSource.excluded` with a reason, printed by the CLI — the census
  reconciles: directories seen = repos listed + directories excluded.
  Regression tests: `tests/test_local_census.py`. Note: PR #2 also
  edits `sources/local.py`/`cli.py` (for F-3); the two branches will
  need a trivial merge reconciliation whichever lands second.
- **F-3 (sub-1 KB repos classified empty) — NOT fixed by the F-2
  branch:** it lives in `LocalSource._describe`'s `// 1024` size floor
  and the `cli.fetch` empty-skip — the same two files PR #2 edits, and
  PR #2 carries the fix (byte-measured size, rounded up, plus a
  zero-repo report guard). Bundling it here would collide with PR #2;
  it remains open until PR #2 lands.
- The 18 real-data tests cannot run from the committed tree alone.
- Test-isolation weakness: if a `data/` directory is present, the
  suite silently grades whatever dataset sits in it (observed by the
  audit lane: 3 failures against a probe dataset, green again after
  removal).
- Not published to PyPI; a non-technical buyer can only consume it
  as a delivered report today.
- Extraction is built around the estate's own languages
  (Python/JS/TS + config surfaces); other ecosystems are
  under-parsed, and the tool reports unparsed sources rather than
  hiding them.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing in this repo. (Related: savageaistudios-site #4, the
FacturForge Stripe webhook, was merged 2026-10-30 outside the train;
its real Stripe checkout/fulfillment proof is still outstanding and
is Phase 2 verification debt on the site's offers, which include the
Faultline audits.)

## Parked PRs

None parked. Open and unmerged: PR #2 and PR #3 (see Verified current
state); the F-2 fix branch awaits merge as a further PR.

## Where it is going

No direction ruled. The audit's first-dollars sequence lists the
Faultline sellable audit tool (PyPI publish + one external-estate
validation run) as step 3 — a lane sequence, not a ruling; not yet
executed.

## FAULT-E1 — the rotation blast-radius oracle (2026-11-11, scoped addendum)

Branch `knights/fault-e1-blast-radius`, based on master @ `ac4cf421`.
This addendum covers FAULT-E1 only; other sections stand as written.

- **Built:** `faultline/analysis/blast_radius.py` + CLI subcommands
  `faultline blast-radius NAME` and `faultline verify-blast-radius REPORT`
  (previously the CLI surface was exactly `fetch` and `analyze`). Given an
  identifier name, the oracle emits a sealed report — every reader repo,
  the census's witness (file:line, occurrences) for each read, and the
  census commitment hash + as-of the answer derives from. Verify mode
  re-derives the answer from the cited census and deep-compares; the
  report also carries a digest over its own body. Unknown names fail
  closed (exit 3, "unestablished, not zero"). Classification imports
  `SECRETISH` from `analysis/risk.py` — one classifier, no second list.
- **Census:** `faultline/data/estate-census-2026-11-08.json` — a
  field-for-field export of `identifiers.env` from the 2026-11-08
  full-estate run's `coupling.json` (sha256
  `729bf8f9be2e338f31ef0bd5253b47e70360bdd150d70f125b622c3b1246990f`;
  38 repos, 40 shared env identifiers), provenance stated inside the
  file. Scope limit, stated in the export: shared identifiers only
  (read by ≥2 repos) — the coupling census records coupling, and the
  oracle answers "not in census" outside it. The oracle also accepts any
  raw `operational.build` output via `--census`.
- **Measured (crew evidence, 2026-11-11):** correctness — oracle answers
  agree field-for-field with the source artifact on all 40 identifiers,
  and with a hand-derived ground truth (manual pass, cross-checked
  against the run's narrative report) on GITHUB_TOKEN (10),
  GH_TOKEN (4), OPENROUTER_API_KEY (4), STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (3): 4/4.
  Planted-error control — one witness line corrupted in a scratch census
  copy: verification fails naming `census.commitment`, both directions;
  scratch discarded. Latency — one CLI answer: median 224 ms cold process
  (n=10). Suite: 88 passed / 18 skipped before → 101 passed / 18 skipped
  after (+13 tests in `tests/test_blast_radius.py`, zero regressions).
- **One discrepancy the oracle surfaces:** SECRETISH over census entries
  classifies 12 shared identifiers as credentials; the 2026-11-08 risk
  register grouped 11 SHARED_CREDENTIAL criticals. The difference is
  `PGPASSWORD` (read by 2 repos per the census): the register's pairwise
  aggregation dropped it. The classification rule is the same regex;
  the oracle answers from the census directly.
- **Limits:** census as-of is 2026-11-08 — answers are exactly as current
  as that run, and the report says so on its face. Shared names are
  proven; same *value* across repos remains unknown from code alone
  (unchanged from the audit's standing caveat).

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# star-inference — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-10 (fixes I-3 + I-4 re-verified locally; fix I-1
re-verified locally 2026-11-10; fix I-2 re-verified locally 2026-11-10;
see below)
**Canonical branch:** master (head pin `c43691a778` below is stale — the tree
has since moved to `ee82fc68`; only the sections touched by the 2026-11-10
fix entry were re-verified, the rest of this file is as of 2026-11-01)

## What this repo is

STAR GPU inference service scaffold: a FastAPI sequential job queue
with HARP-pattern contracts, intended to host license-verified model
adapters (compose / sing / song / reason) on a Brev box.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `c43691a778` — unchanged from the audit freeze. Tree = 10 blobs.
- **Open PRs:** none.
- **Tests:** 5/5 contract tests pass, and a live uvicorn smoke test
  behaved per CONTRACTS.md (`/health` ok, draft job → 503, unknown
  job → 404). These counts stand on the verifier's re-runs
  (Corrections Appendix §3).
- The queue + HTTP contract layer is coded and CPU-tested.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **Every model adapter is a DraftBackend.** All four registered
  backends self-check `False` and refuse work (503 / `draft`). No
  model has ever produced output through this service, as far as
  anything in the repo shows.
- ~~**No installable packaging**~~ — **FIXED 2026-11-10 (queue I-3):**
  `pyproject.toml` added (setuptools backend; runtime deps = exactly
  what `app/` imports — fastapi, pydantic — plus uvicorn for the entry
  points). Clean-venv `pip install .` verified; the installed package
  imports from a neutral CWD. Before: pip refused the tree ("Neither
  'setup.py' nor 'pyproject.toml' found") and import from a neutral
  CWD raised `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- ~~**Import-time filesystem side effect**~~ — **FIXED 2026-11-10
  (queue I-4):** `app/main.py` no longer builds the production app at
  import (it previously ran `create_app(db_path="jobs.db")` at module
  level, creating a 12 KB SQLite file in whatever CWD imported it —
  reproduced before the fix). The production app is now built only by
  entry points: `create_production_app()` (ASGI factory), the
  `star-inference` console script, or `python -m app.main`; the job
  store path is `$STAR_INFERENCE_DB` (default `jobs.db`, unchanged).
  Verified after: importing every `app` module from a scratch CWD
  creates no files and emits no output; all three entry points serve
  `/health` byte-identical to the pre-fix baseline; the contract suite
  passes 5/5 before and after (and no longer leaves a `jobs.db` in the
  repo root). NOTE: the old `uvicorn app.main:app` invocation no longer
  resolves — use `uvicorn --factory app.main:create_production_app`.
- ~~**CONTRACTS.md auth not implemented**~~ — **FIXED 2026-11-10
  (queue I-1):** the contract's auth is now enforced in `app/main.py`.
  When a token is configured — `create_app(..., auth_token=...)`, else
  the `INFERENCE_TOKEN` env var (the production entry points resolve
  the env var) — every route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`;
  a missing or wrong token is refused 401 before any route runs
  (constant-time comparison). Before the fix, the production app built
  with `INFERENCE_TOKEN` set answered unauthenticated requests exactly
  as authenticated ones (POST /jobs → 503 draft, GET /health → 200);
  after, the same no-header probes return 401 while a correct token
  reproduces the pre-fix responses byte-for-byte, including the honest
  503 draft posture. With no token configured the service runs open,
  as it always has in-process — CONTRACTS.md's own operator rule
  stands: set the token before exposing any port. Suite 5 → 9 (four
  new auth tests in `tests/test_auth.py`); the five pre-existing
  contract tests pass unmodified.
- ~~**Crashed `running` jobs orphaned forever**~~ — **FIXED 2026-11-10
  (queue I-2):** startup crash recovery now exists in `app/queue.py`.
  `JobStore.reset_running()` resets every `running` row to `queued`
  (clearing result/error; the `created` timestamp is untouched, so FIFO
  order is preserved), and `JobRunner.start()` runs it before the worker
  loop starts — safe because the runner is a single sequential worker,
  so a `running` row at startup can only belong to a dead process. The
  interrupted job re-runs from the start; no partial result is trusted
  or resumed. Before the fix, a kill-and-restart probe (job picked up,
  process abandoned mid-run, fresh store + runner on the same file)
  left the crashed job reporting `running` eternally — its `/result`
  would 409 forever — while a merely-`queued` job completed normally;
  after the fix the same probe ends with the crashed job `done`. Two
  regression tests (`tests/test_recovery.py`) simulate the
  crash-restart cycle and pin that recovery touches only `running`
  rows. Suite 9 → 11; the pre-existing contract and auth tests pass
  unmodified, and the I-4 import-purity property still holds.
- The README's wiring instructions point at `app/backends/<name>.py`
  — that path does not exist; adapters live in the single module
  `app/backends.py`.
- No build, typecheck, or CI configuration exists.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing.

## Parked PRs

None open.

## Where it is going

No direction ruled. Research grade in the audit: THIN — an honest
draft scaffold.

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# Savage-forge — GROUND TRUTH — Pass 2 (verified 2026-11-08)

**Repo:** sa6ag9/Savage-forge
**Status header:** GROUND TRUTH — Pass 2, verified 2026-11-08 by Knights' end-state crew under Savage's direct finish order of 2026-11-08 ~02:31 PT. This file supersedes the Pass 1 audit draft and the repo's prior `GROUND_TRUTH.md` (last verified 2026-11-05, anchor `c5e00d8175`, stale). Default branch: `main` @ `6cd3d1b7f9dbf9fb11d93a82255b27518b0b2cdb`. Tonight's results are stated from executed receipts in `evidence/runs/` (named per item below); where any other document in this repo disagrees with this file, this file wins.

## (a) What this system is and does

Forge is a deterministic, evidence-pinned world engine built in this repo: CPU physics / rendering / audit pipeline code, a causal Gaussian world surface, training infrastructure and models, a learned critic/correction surface, an independent runtime auditor, a SIREN/INR finisher, Sound Genetics audio, and native/formal-verification components (Lean/Dafny fragments, a Rust codec FFI crate, a CUDA codec). Its distinguishing machinery is its proof discipline: ~50 frozen benchmark protocols with pre-declared run records, gate text quoted before measurement, independent oracles, receipts with content-hash pins, and FAIL receipts preserved rather than relabelled.

Prototype-proven before landing (extension corpus `b4bea7ac…`: 10 admitted bundles, 270/270 artifact hashes, byte-identical regeneration, v1-mode parity 617/617 files); landed verification: factory v1 mode byte-identical to the stock generator (169/169 files, corpus id equal), landed v11 corpus reproduces the prototype's admitted bundles artifact-for-artifact (27/27 per bundle, captions/solvers/event counts equal), targeted tests 44 passed (20 pre-existing + 24 new: `tests/test_native_caption_grammar_v11.py`, `tests/test_native_corpus_factory.py`). Solver-limited cells recorded, not forced: fall-onto sphere→sphere and box→sphere fail closed at this solver generation (sustained contact) and quarantine under the resampling rule |
| Demo corpus (`source/evidence/p1-corpus-demo/`) | verified — at 22/1,000 scale | Audit; regeneration reproduces its corpus_id exactly (S9 repeatability) |

## (d) How to verify

- **Full suite:** `cd source && PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q` (ffmpeg required). Auditor on pristine main: 770 passed. Tonight on the integrated tree: **812 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** (skip = the declared torch-absence posture test). Raw logs preserved in the declaring workspace.
- **P1 gate corpus:** recompute the envelope digest and bundle hashes of the assembled corpus → corpus_id `d4798dff…`, 1,136 admitted / 0 quarantined, 30,672 artifacts, 0 errors (verification JSON filed in `source/evidence/native-p1/`).
- **W1 data factory (2026-11-13):** `tests/test_native_corpus_factory.py` + `tests/test_native_caption_grammar_v11.py` — factory v1 mode byte-identical to the stock generator (corpus id + full tree), routing-table solver names per composition class, fail-closed gate quarantines (scope / non-finite / unrealized interaction), grammar v1.1.0 parity on v1-valid snapshots, and a demo-scale factory corpus (7 sampled specs: head-on ×4 class pairs, chain, cascade, chain-scene) that admits 7/7, verifies every artifact hash, has its coverage block independently re-derived, and regenerates byte-identically.
- **P1 run:** `source/evidence/native-p1/p1-eval-receipt.json` is the machine verdict; `checkpoint-reproduction.json` proves the checkpoint reloads and re-evaluates. Re-running `scripts/run_native_p1_vae.py` against the same corpus reproduces the run under its declared record.
- **S5 proofs:** `tests/test_mesh_physics.py` (floor-mesh matched baseline) and `tests/test_friction_physics.py` (μ=0 matched baseline + closed forms).
- **S6:** receipts in `source/evidence/sound-genetics-interop/` bind genome hash, engine-file hash, and output hash; re-running `genesis.sound_genetics_interop` against STAR's engine modules reproduces them.
- **Determinism:** demo twice → byte-identical (S9 repeatability evidence).
- **GEN-E1 (2026-11-10):** `genesis-render --out <dir>` renders the demo deliverable with its sealed `render-manifest.json`; `genesis-verify <dir>` re-renders from the manifest alone and byte-compares every output (exit 0 = verified). `source/tests/test_render_manifest.py` carries the positive controls and the four tamper controls. The manifest's own limitations field restates the coverage limits in §(e).
- **GEN-E2 (2026-11-11):** `genesis-edit-diff --out <dir> --body emerald --velocity 1.2 0 0` performs the edit (base + edited GEN-E1 deliverables plus the sealed `edit-diff-manifest.json`); `genesis-edit-verify <dir>` recomputes the diff from the delivered artifacts and confirms or rejects the report (exit 0 = verified). `source/tests/test_edit_diff.py` carries the positive controls, the byte-determinism check, five tamper controls, and the non-finite negative controls. Corpus measurement (BEFORE 0/6 → AFTER 6/6, tamper 30/30 rejected) filed at `source/evidence/gen-e2/`.

## (e) What is NOT true

- **No Genesis product can be sold or advertised today.** "Nothing is deployed, sold, or customer-usable today" remains TRUE (verified again tonight; S9 commercialization is BLOCKED-with-proof and user acceptance is NOT GRANTED). VS-1 stops at 5/8 on main (WO06 in PR #47; WO07/WO08 not started); Campaign V2 §5 blind grading has never run.
- **The native VAE did NOT pass its P1 quality gates.** PSNR 24.397 dB < 30 and SSIM 0.7265 < 0.90, measured on the declared validation protocol after 50 steps (~5% of one epoch). Any claim that Genesis's learned model meets its declared reconstruction bar is contradicted by the filed receipt. What IS true: the structural gates (corpus, causality, finiteness, decode exactness, checkpoint reproduction) pass, and the failure is retained, not hidden.
- **Cinematic/production quality is UNPROVEN.** No blind grading has ever occurred; the demo is explicitly `not_a_cinematic_benchmark` by its own manifest.
- **GPU physics does not exist in this repo**, and no GPU metrics exist. GOAL.md defers GPU feasibility to a later cost-gated experiment.
- **The G3 scaffold has still never executed a model call** (`model_execution_verified: False` on its receipt paths). Tonight's executed learned backend is the separate native VAE; do not conflate them.
- **Red Queen's founder mechanics do not exist here.** The S8 adapter implements only the declared interface (challenges/benchmarks/mutation proposals); the founder record itself marks the exact design "placeholder only."
- **The demo corpus is still 22 clips.** The 1,136-clip gate corpus is a separate assembled evaluation corpus on the declaring workspace (hash-bound by its verification record), not a replacement of the committed demo corpus.
- **The prior GT's suite figure (600 passed) is STALE** (accurate at its head); the Pass 1 draft's "no learned model has ever executed" was true when written and is superseded by §(c) as of tonight's run.
- **GEN-E1's manifest + verifier do NOT cover the learned paths.** The native learned backend (`native_corpus_render` / the S7 VAE path), the VS-1 delivery paths, box-session/glTF export paths, and the generation-delivery paths ship **no** render manifest and are **not** re-renderable through `genesis-verify`. Capture-and-pin covers only content explicitly captured as an asset into a GEN-E1 deliverable; no learned component's output has been captured into one yet, and the seam does not make any learned output deterministic — it freezes one captured output as a fixed file. GEN-E1 monetizes the deterministic engine only; the learned backend's S7 quality gates stand **FAILED-and-retained** exactly as §(c) records, and nothing in GEN-E1 changes or launders that verdict.
- **MP4 byte-identity is encoder-build-bound.** The manifest pins the exact ffmpeg build string; a different ffmpeg build produces a different MP4 and the verifier reports it as an identity mismatch rather than passing it. Frame/audio/graph bytes are encoder-independent.
- **No D2/D3 production corpus exists.** The W1 data factory is landed and proven at demo scale only: production volumes/quotas, the sealed synthetic test slice and the novelty slice, and the assembled production manifest (v1-mode D0/D1 ∪ v11-mode D2/D3 under one factory corpus extending `d4798dff…`) are design-only in the factory SPEC and unbuilt. The prototype extension corpus (10 bundles, `b4bea7ac…`) is demo evidence and counts toward no gate; no training run has consumed D2/D3 data.
- **GEN-E2 covers only edits performed through `genesis.edit_diff.render_edit`.** The older `genesis-edit` experiment path (`genesis.engine.run_edit_experiment`, LayeredVisual revisions) still emits only its internal locality-audit aggregate — no diff report — and the VS-1 counterfactual/reversible paths and the box/capsule delivery paths keep their own internal audits; none of those outputs carry a GEN-E2 report, and no claim below extends the 6/6 corpus result beyond the demo scene's fixture corpus. The pixel diff covers the rendered frame sequence only: audio and MP4 bytes are bound by the GEN-E1 render manifests, not diffed. The diff is exact pixel inequality on decoded RGB frames — it proves *what changed*, never that the edit is good; nothing in GEN-E2 touches the learned backend or the S7 quality gates, which stand FAILED-and-retained exactly as §(c) records.

## (f) Evidence basis

Pass 2, 2026-11-08. Sources: the estate audit `savage-genesis.md` and branch-delta audit (Pass 1 basis, preserved); tonight's completion-drive artifacts, all filed in-repo: S5 doc + tests, S6 doc + receipts, S7 doc + run record + receipts, S8 doc + benchmark, S9 package, Campaign V2 Genesis-side package, and the after-suite run (812 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed). Default-branch head: `main` @ `cb1bc829e7e3ef2a90ddde5ffba795b2068643f6` (PR #46 merge); tonight's changes land as PRs `knights/*` on top of it.

# Repo-Vibe — verified public-badge privacy repair

2026-11-04. Source base 98c13fb5c2cad2364fec822f5bd7ac7b5a4989bc.

## Implemented and verified

Public badge requests check unauthenticated repository visibility on every request, including cache hits. Private, inaccessible and unknown-visibility repositories never return cached data. Badge statistics never receive an installation token or environment token. The existing tara/public-badge-privacy branch supplied the original privacy repair and three regression tests; it was adapted without rewriting that branch.

Cache entries expire after 300 seconds and at the UTC day boundary, bounded to 256 entries. Invalid owner/repository paths reject before network access. Webhook bodies reject invalid/negative/oversized Content-Length, transfer encoding and invalid envelope shapes.

The old GitHub App manifest callback consumed a one-time conversion but discarded returned credentials. Automatic setup routes now return 410 before any network request. Existing signed push-webhook invalidation still works. No live credentials were exchanged during verification.

Original baseline: 4 pytest tests passed. The privacy repair finished with 13 passed, 0 failed. A follow-up data-quality repair adds 4 focused regressions: failed or malformed commit details never produce a partial line total, CI lookup failure stays distinct from a successful empty workflow list, and the 30-commit ceiling is labeled as a sample. Current local result: 17 passed, 0 failed. Raw privacy evidence is under evidence/privacy-20261104/ and evidence/data-quality-20261104-local.txt.

2026-11-09 addendum (estate fix program, repo-vibe D1+D2): the retired GitHub App auth machinery — `make_jwt`, `installation_token`, `token_for` (including its `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment fallback) and the `_installations` bookkeeping — and the dead `manifest()` builder were deleted from `app.py`. They had no live callers since the setup routes were retired behind 410 responses; the badge path is public-data-only and now has no token code path at all. The privacy property above ("badge statistics never receive an installation token or environment token") is now structural, and is pinned by `test_server_security.py` (environment-token behavioral check + machinery-absence check). Suite after the removal: see the landing PR.

2026-11-15 addendum (estate fix program, repo-vibe D3): the server now serves threaded. `app.py` built a single-threaded `HTTPServer`, so one slow upstream GitHub call (the badge path blocks on it per uncached request; timeout 20 s) serialized every other request behind it — measured on the pristine tree: two badge requests with a 0.6 s upstream took 1.32 s wall. The server is now built by `app.make_server()` as a `ThreadingHTTPServer` with daemon threads; the same probe takes 0.69 s. `test_server_concurrency.py` pins the behavior (two slow requests complete in under the serialized floor). The shared badge cache stays a plain dict — its get/pop/set are atomic under the GIL, so a race can at worst duplicate an upstream fetch; the per-request visibility checks are unchanged. Suite: 17 passed before, 18 passed after. The "single-process HTTP serving limit scale" line under Remaining limits stands (one process, threaded — not a fleet).

## Remaining limits

No hosted deployment, installation, customer or revenue is verified. Public API quota and single-process HTTP serving limit scale. Activity is still capped at 30 daily commits and explicitly labeled as a sample at the cap. Detail-fetch failures now suppress the line total; CI lookup failures now display UNKNOWN. This is a verified privacy and data-quality repair, not completed commercial productization.

# savage-router — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-04 (Router drafts landing — Tights first-hand verification: diffs read in full, CI-equivalent suites run on exact PR heads + baseline control, post-merge tree proof)
**Canonical branch:** main @ b96e51842c57457089c6a0ead6876813c0327157 (post-PR #9 merge; this file's own commit sits on top)

## What this repo is

Two things in one repo: (1) a small, stdlib-only, OpenAI-compatible
cascade model router (free-first, quota-proof cascade, default-deny
billable-provider gate), and (2) a larger "learning collective"
layer — console, deliberation engine, markdown brain with a
proven-rule ledger, and a curator.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `b96e51842c57457089c6a0ead6876813c0327157` — merge of PR #9. Tree = 74 blobs. (PRs #3 and #4 were merged earlier on 2026-11-03; PR #6 was squash-merged at `f0f7327586`.)
- **Tests (Tights local run, 2026-11-03, CI-equivalent steps):** compileall OK; `test_router.py` PASS; router safety **5/5**; conversation **9/9** (baseline 5/5); console **13 passed**; curator **19 passed**; learning **41 passed**. Zero regressions vs the baseline control.
- **Tests (2026-11-04 landing verification, exact PR heads):** the control reproduces the counts above exactly; the conversation suite grows **9 → 14 (PR #7) → 15 (PR #8) → 18 (PR #9)**; dictation `node --test` **6/6** on #8/#9; PR #9's newly CI-wired `tests/test_collective.py` **9/9**. Every CI step exits 0 on every tree; failure sets identical (empty). The drafts' CI is real executed CI on the exact heads (runs 41619540499 / 41626024673 / 41634312538; 3.11 + 3.12, all success).
- Router and console services also run locally on the VM
  (127.0.0.1:20129 / 20130) — a local deployment, not a public one.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **The deployed copy is older and less safe than this repo**
  (conflict C11): the running `router.py` predates the repo's
  `billing_class` gate, 1 MiB body bound, and nonlocal-bind refusal.
  Repo truth and deployed truth differ.
- The billable gate is a **boolean** (`ROUTER_ALLOW_BILLABLE`) with
  **no monetary cap anywhere**.
- `unittest discover` still fails on the learning/curator suites (script-style suites that call `sys.exit()` at module level); since PR #6, CI invokes the conversation, console, curator and learning suites directly, so they are CI-gated even though discover remains unsupported.
  script-style suites that call `sys.exit()` at module level, and CI
  does not run them at all.
- Nothing in this repo proves a live provider completion or a
  dollar of revenue.

## Merged in the 2026-11-03 trains

- **#3, #4** — merged earlier on 2026-11-03 (LibreChat console code; deployment still candidate-only, Scout-only roster).
- **#6** — squash-merged in the Tonight Sprint train at `f0f7327586d42b6a57d47eb3e8cb0014b43a7c66` (tree proof PASS, 68 → 69 blobs). Shared conversation history now fails closed on a corrupt/invalid store instead of erasing it, and writes are durable and atomic (unique temp file, fsync of file and directory, a single canonical source). Not a hosted multi-instance lock and not a backup system; one canonical store on one filesystem.

## Merged 2026-11-04 — the stacked drafts

- **#7** — accessible transcript paging for the console
  (DIRECTION §4: screen-reader-first console as the control
  surface). Landed via a resolution merge commit: the stack
  rooted on PR #6's kept branch (squash divergence), and the
  three files both sides had touched resolved to the branch
  versions after proof that main's and the root's copies were
  byte-identical.
- **#8** — voice dictation safety (dictation module + tests).
- **#9** — collective seat-failure isolation: a failed seat is
  recorded as a generic failure entry under its own identity,
  the group is marked `failed` with `failed_seat_ids`, provider
  exception text never enters the transcript, and a seat whose
  learning receipt fails is not accepted as complete.
- Tree proof: merged main == PR #9 tip tree on all 74 paths,
  this file excepted (main's newer version kept by design).
  No test in the chain was modified, deleted, or loosened —
  every test-file diff is pure addition. Unproven, as the PRs
  themselves disclaim: real Android/TalkBack behavior and live
  hosted multi-seat operation (the registry still holds only
  Scout; tests stub the providers).

## Parked PRs

None — no open PRs.


## Where it is going

Savage superseded the router design with **Murmuration** on
2026-10-28 (the router concept was scrapped as the estate's agent
architecture). This repo remains the record of the built router and
its learning loop; the local services still run. No new direction
ruled for this repo itself.

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# savage-foundry — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-01 (live API state; audit evidence 2026-10-29)
**Canonical branch:** main @ 5876f690c2

## What this repo is

The Foundry record: a disassembly atlas of frontier agent mechanisms
and the Savage composite design (COMPOSITION v2), plus — since the
D4 custody commit — the full build tree that previously existed only
in an unversioned VM directory.

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `5876f690c2` — a GROUND_TRUTH-only commit on top of the D4 custody commit. Tree = 8,738 blobs.
- **Open PRs:** none.
- At the 2026-10-29 audit freeze this repo was **53 Markdown files
  and zero code** (verifier-counted). Its headline "87.5% built"
  claim referred to a local-only build tree (`~/workspace/foundry-build/`,
  920 MB) that had never been committed anywhere; the audit's
  out-of-repo check of that tree's most complete phase ran 149
  tests: 145 pass / 4 fail under load (clean-host re-run UNREACHED
  at audit time).
- **D4 executed 2026-10-30:** custody commit `db0c44accf41` landed
  **8,684 entries** (8,676 files + 8 symlinks; 943,572,895 B source)
  on main; head and tree verified after landing.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- Two Python venvs under `scratch/` (~97 MB) were included in the
  custody commit per the mandate's exclusion list. **Removed
  2026-11-09** on Savage's ruling (PR #3, merged; main head
  `8d40e14538dc`): `scratch/genesis-venv-density/` (47,117,718 B)
  and `scratch/genesis-venv-main/` (44,554,881 B) — 91,672,599 B
  in total. A root `.gitignore` now excludes `scratch/genesis-venv-*/`.
  The removed trees remain recoverable from git history (custody
  commit `db0c44accf41`; `e4837476`). Verified absent from the
  main tree at the merge head.
- Post-custody test state of the committed tree has **not been
  re-verified**; the 145/149 figure is pre-custody, out-of-repo
  evidence under load, with flake-vs-regression unresolved.
- **D7 (duplicate design documents at root) — resolved
  2026-11-10** (estate fix program): `COMPOSITION.md` (blob
  `4a23dee3e8`) is the single canonical composition text.
  `COMPOSITION-V2.md` (was byte-identical to it) and
  `COMPOSITION-V2-DRAFT.md` (the pre-adoption working draft —
  diff-verified as fully contained in the adopted text, which
  adds §0) are now pointer stubs naming the canonical file and
  its blob SHA. The draft remains recoverable from history
  (blob `4336de44cd`). The wider drafting lineage
  (`COMPOSITION-DRAFT.md` → `math/wave2/COMPOSITION-WAVE2-DRAFT.md`
  → draft → adopted) is a referenced chain of record — each
  stage is name-cited by the math/wave-2 batteries and reports
  that produced it — and was deliberately not consolidated.
- **D10 (`donors/` names imply full repos) — resolved
  2026-11-10** (estate fix program): `donors/README.md` added.
  `donors/` holds curated subsets from 6 estate repos — 97
  subset files plus 25 committed `.pyc` caches — not repo
  copies; the README records the per-donor census, the
  byte-identical carries into the build trees, and that
  per-donor source commits were never recorded (the subsets
  entered in custody commit `db0c44accf41`, 2026-10-30).


- **D8 — judges' estate roster drift (corrected 2026-11-10):** the
  breakthrough-classifier judge's roster (`phase1/judges/breakthrough/
  estate.mjs`) asserted a "measured 36-repo estate" (PHASE0-REPORT.md
  §1, 2026-10-15). The assertion and the listed entries agreed with
  each other (36 = 36) but both had drifted from the estate itself:
  3 listed repos no longer exist (durak,
  NS-SIAV6-OS-siav6-orchestration, Overmind-new) and 10 live repos
  were unlisted. The roster is corrected to the estate measured from
  the Savages-studios org on 2026-11-10: **43 repos in the org; the
  roster's inclusion rule counts the live estate — the 42
  non-archived repos (the archived `actions-pilot` excluded), with
  `savages-assistants` included as it was on the original list.** The
  fix-queue row that opened D8 stated the estate as 38 (the pre-
  migration personal-account count); 38 is recorded here as history —
  today's measured figure under the stated rule is 42. The count is
  now derived (exported as `ESTATE_REPO_COUNT` = the list's length)
  and a drift check in `tests/judges-breakthrough.test.mjs` fails
  whenever the derived count, the listed entries and the declared
  expectation disagree; the check compares in-repo sources only (it
  cannot call GitHub), so the org-side recount remains a manual step.
  Scope note: `ESTATE_OWNER` still reads `sa6ag9` and `RepoIngestor`
  still snapshots under it — flagged for a separate ruling, not
  changed by D8.

## D2 / queue row 134 — the two divergent lineages are one tree (2026-11-13)

Until this entry, no single checkout contained the composition:
Phase 3's bloodlines lived only in `phase1/`; the Phase 4–6 lineage
(`overmind-crew/tree` → `phase5/tree` → `phase6/tree`) had no
bloodlines, and every package was still named `foundry-phase1`.
**Canonical tree: `phase6/tree/`** — renamed `savage-foundry`,
carrying spine, seal, SAP, judges, bloodlines (Phase 3), Skill Forge
memory + crew (Phase 4), rewiring (Phase 5) and tiers (Phase 6) under
one package with one suite. The superseded snapshots (`phase1/`,
`overmind-crew/tree`, `phase5/tree`) are archived in place —
retained verbatim, `var/` evidence included, each with an
`ARCHIVED.md` pointer; nothing was deleted. Merge resolutions were
unions, not picks: `laws/laws.mjs` restores the Phase-3 seating
(Tier C types `promotion-verdict`/`promotion-ceremony` + the three
bloodlines laws) alongside the Phase 4–6 laws — bloodlines'
ceremony code classifies its receipts through that registry and the
Phase 4–6 form refused them; the judges estate roster is the
D8-corrected 42 (fix #99), which had landed only on the phase1
lineage. Verification (2026-11-13, this host, a Genesis training run
concurrent): the unified suite runs 176 tests — the canonical
tree's 149 plus bloodlines' 26 and the D8 drift check — with all
27 added tests passing. Honest residue, all pre-existing and none
caused by this change: the Phase-4 gate still fails LEASE_EXPIRED
(queue row 156, the supervisor/lease defect), and three
wall-clock-sensitive tests (replay gate, executor fence, dead-man
synthesis — the last is row 99's known flake, proven against the
untouched tree in an interleaved control) fail intermittently under
host load on both the pre- and post-unification trees. BUILD-STATUS
still aggregates the old snapshots; restamping it from this tree is
row 80's work. The live Phase-3 gate was not re-run (its fuel line
is row 113's subject); Phase 3's committed verdict — gate (ii)
failed on an exact tie, loop killed back to design — is preserved,
not resurrected.

## D5 / queue row 80 — BUILD-STATUS and the front door restamped from the unified tree (2026-11-13)

Row 80 was explicitly gated on row 134 and is prepared against
PR #7's branch head `b6a53940ce8adc12fe4ef9102e22182db992e143`
(base `main` `b87762e523ae8fad380fa631493682e6018f24b5`); PR #7
was still open when the restamp was measured, so the row 80
payload is staged to land after it. The 2026-10-15
`BUILD-STATUS.md` headline — “87.5% built — 7 of 8 phases
complete and verified” — is **superseded as a current-tree
claim**: it aggregated the divergent snapshots, and its
“Tights re-ran 125/125 / 149/149” figures are historical
snapshot counts, not counts of the unified suite. The “86%
delivered” second cut is likewise retired as a headline: it
grades phase-receipt improvement claims in
`COMPONENT-EVOLUTION.md`, not the unified tree. The restamped
`BUILD-STATUS.md` and root `README.md` state the measured
position instead, with the superseded figures kept visible.
Verification (Knights, 2026-11-13, host `htch-runtime`, Node
v24.22.1, Genesis training concurrent): boot 5/5 layers live
with 18/18 probes passing; unification seam 38/38; full unified
suite **174/176, 2 failed** — the Phase-4 gate test
(`LEASE_EXPIRED`, row 156) and the Phase-1 replay-gate test
(dispatch failed at `obj-066`; the standalone replay gate also
failed, at `obj-086`) — and a repeat run on the byte-identical
code tree scored 173/176, the same two plus row 99's known
dead-man wall-clock flake; Phase 2 gate re-run live **passed
30/30** with its verdict feed verified; rewiring + tiers
targeted tests **24/24**. Not re-run for row 80: the live
Phase 3 gate (fuel line, row 113; Phase 3's sealed kill stands)
and the heavy Phase 5 / Phase 6 gate workloads — their status
is carried as historical receipt + suite evidence and labeled
as such in `BUILD-STATUS.md`. No fresh Tights re-verification
of the unified tree is claimed. Phase 7 remains not started.

## Merged in the 2026-11-01 train

Nothing. (The custody commit predates the train.)

## Parked PRs

None open. (SIA-Foundry #16, a different repo, is parked — its base
is another workstream's branch.)

## Where it is going

Ruled (D4): custody is complete — every Foundry claim is now
falsifiable from this repo. No further direction ruled.

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

## Evolution — one canonical `verify` command (2026-11-15)

**Capability:** `tools/verify.py` (stdlib-only Python, zero new
dependencies), wired as the repo's documented one command in
`README.md`. One run: (1) runs the canonical suite once,
(2) drift-checks every duplicated judge/test tree against the
canonical tree, (3) asserts the mechanizable falsifiable claims
below against the live tree. Per-section verdicts; nonzero exit
on any failure.
