# Savage_MoneyEngine — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-09 (Pass 2 — post-fix verification; full suites
re-run on the head below, this VM, Python 3.12.3)
**Canonical branch:** main @ `07b2f261c638050c8f6b5be6e1a4f5d011549576`
(the head this refresh was verified against; this file's own landing
commit succeeds it)

## What this repo is

An offline, evidence-grade unclaimed-property data pipeline for
California — **not a payment engine**. It acquires official California
State Controller unclaimed-property bulk ZIPs (claimit.ca.gov) under
strict URL allowlists, hash-pins them, ingests them into a local
SQLite database of property records, and then verifies, replays,
reconciles, snapshots, and attests that the ingested records match the
pinned source bytes — without ever claiming the records confer
rights, claims, or revenue.

"$0 revenue ever" is a structural invariant of the code, not just a
statement: every receipt schema hardcodes `actual_revenue_cents` /
`actual_company_revenue_cents_verified` to 0 and validators reject
nonzero values. The only outbound wiring in the pipeline is
caller-invoked HTTPS GET of the five official CA archive URLs. The
repo contains no ZIP/CSV/SQLite data files; every test runs on
synthetic fixtures labeled as such. The newest pipeline modules
(v122–v123) build print-and-mail claim packets offline and explicitly
file nothing, submit nothing, contact nobody; there is no field
capable of holding a TIN/SSN/ID number or signature, by design.

Since 2026-11-09 the tree also carries the v124 offline operator
service stack and the v125 customer-commerce release (PRs #4→#5→#6,
merged as one chain). The v125 machinery is verification-only Stripe
integration (webhook HMAC + GET-only readback, `livemode` enforced,
no charge creation, never issues refunds) behind a pinned $79 B2B
software-license offer (SKU `MONEYENGINE-79`). Its own release
document (`docs/CUSTOMER_RELEASE_V125.md`) states its status:
**"NOT YET PUBLICLY LAUNCH-ACCEPTED"**, and the offer self-reports
`publishedSaleReady: False` (`engine/customer_offer_v125.py:66`).
Landing the chain did not make anything sellable.

Tree at the verified head: 572 blobs; `engine/` = 107 Python modules;
`tests/` = 185 test modules, 2,494 tests. Open PRs: none.

## Component state

| Component | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Acquisition (`engine/acquire.py`, `acquire_set.py`, `provenance.py`, `acquisition_audit.py`) — allowlisted HTTPS download, per-hop redirect re-validation, size caps, streamed SHA-256, no-overwrite fsync publication | verified | Estate audit 2026-11 (full code read); suite green 2026-11-09 (see How to verify) |
| Ingest (`engine/forensic.py`) — ZIP→SQLite, `Decimal` money parsing rejecting negatives/non-finite/sub-cent/>$100B, ZIP/CSV guards; amounts stored as `listed_cents`, explicitly "not revenue" | verified | Audit table; `cents()` `forensic.py:73-82` |
| Verification stack (~70 modules: replay, cross-tier reconciliation, ledger snapshots, five-source deltas, full-row parity) — read-only / no-overwrite, fail-closed | verified | Audit; suite green 2026-11-09 |
| Review / blind evaluation (`blind_review.py`, `sealed_controls_v45.py`, `witnessed_blind_v57.py`, `reviewer_attestations_v58.py`, `signed_pinset_v46.py`) — sealed-label protocol, Ed25519 attestations, aggregate-only outputs | verified | Audit; the 90 attestation tests run green with `cryptography` installed and skip by name without it (D1, PR #8) |
| Rights / fee screening (`rights.py`, `ca_contract_guardrails_v76.py`, ~25 jurisdiction guardrail modules) — screening status only, never approval; return values hardcode `verified_revenue_cents: 0`, `property_rights_established: False` | verified | Audit |
| Filing layer v122–v123 (`ca_multiowner_policy_v122.py`, `filing_packet_v123.py`) — offline print-ready CA SCO claim packet, fail-closed, no TIN/SSN/signature field, mails/submits nothing | verified | Audit; `filing_packet_v123.py:288-291`, `:314`, `:527` |
| v124 offline operator service stack (`evidence_custody_v124.py`, case journal, packet vault, proof lattice, service CLI) | verified (as tested) | On main via PR #5; its 27 suite tests pass in the 2026-11-09 full runs |
| v125 customer-commerce release (offer, webhook/readback verification, entitlements, portal, revocations) | verified (as tested); **not launch-accepted** | On main via PR #6; its 30 acceptance tests pass in the 2026-11-09 full runs; release doc states NOT YET PUBLICLY LAUNCH-ACCEPTED; `publishedSaleReady: False` in code |
| Revenue recording | verified (impossible) | Receipt schemas hardcode 0 and validators reject nonzero (audit Evidence §1: `acquire_set.py:259,428`, `:361-362`; same pattern across `audit.py`, `blind_review.py`, `filing_packet_v123.py`, …) |
| Real California data ingest | absent (in-repo) / unknown (elsewhere) | No data files in the tree (file inventory, audit + 2026-11-09 tarball listing); whether the acquisition path was ever run against live CA archives from another machine is unknown — no receipts in-repo. First pinned real ingest is an operator decision (plan §9 decision 17), still open |
| Dangerous money-movement code | absent | Audit: no transfers/charges/payouts/account access; sole pipeline subprocess uses fixed argv, scrubbed env, rlimits; v125 adds no charge/refund path (its own release doc + acceptance tests) |
| Dependency manifest (`requirements.txt`) | verified (present, sufficient) | Added by PR #8 (defect D1): pins `cryptography==50.0.2`. Full-tree AST import scan: `cryptography` is the only third-party module imported anywhere in the repo. Clean-venv install from this file → full suite green (see How to verify). Every direct `cryptography` consumer fails by name when it is absent: the three attestation test modules skip naming it, the three engine verifiers raise a named `RuntimeError` at use, and — since the D1 completion pass — the three attestation benchmark scripts exit naming it (`<script> requires the \`cryptography\` dependency declared in requirements.txt`) instead of an opaque `ModuleNotFoundError` traceback |
| Canonical test command (`run_tests.sh`, `Makefile`) | verified | Added by PR #9 (defect D2). A naive `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` still refuses by layout (no `__init__.py`; sibling imports) — the canonical command is the documented path, and a bare `pytest` also passes (measured, see How to verify) |
| Regression runners' journal paths | verified (configurable) | v111: `MONEY_ENGINE_JOURNAL_DIR` env var, default `/mnt/data`, loud named refusal when the directory does not exist (PR #7, defect D4; proven in three resolution states + scratch end-to-end run). v112: `--output-dir` / `SAVAGE_MONEY_REGRESSION_DIR`, repo-local default |
| Privacy handling for owner/identity exports (`engine/identity.py`, `owner_holder_cases_v50.py`) | verified (deliberate — plan D5 INFO, no action) | 0o700/0o600 modes, no-overwrite publication, read-only DB opens, CSV formula-injection guard (audit). Residual risk is operational, not code |
| Research corpus (`research/`, `docs/`, ~25 jurisdictions) | observed | Research asserts opportunities; engine modules uniformly encode "no claim authority / no revenue" — code never upgrades research into entitlement (audit) |

## How to verify

Canonical: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, then `./run_tests.sh`
(`make test` is the same). Verifier environment note: run with a
TMPDIR on a filesystem that honors POSIX modes (the suite's custody
checks require real 0700 directories — on this VM that means the
`/tmp` tmpfs, not the group-shared workspace mount, whose forced
setgid bit fails the checks) and with several hundred MB free (the
acquisition preflight compares free space against the 400 MB
per-archive cap; a nearly-full TMPDIR fails those tests spuriously).

Runs executed 2026-11-09 on main @ `07b2f261`, Python 3.12.3:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Clean venv built from `requirements.txt` (cryptography 50.0.2), `./run_tests.sh` | **Ran 2,494 tests — OK (skipped=2)**, exit 0 |
| Stdlib-only (system Python, no `cryptography`), `./run_tests.sh` | **Ran 2,494 tests — OK (skipped=92)**, exit 0 — the 90 Ed25519 attestation tests skip explicitly, naming the missing dependency; the other 2 skips are environment-gated probes |
| Bare `pytest` 9.2.0 (provisioned venv) | **2,492 passed, 2 skipped**, exit 0 |

Baselines at the pre-fix head (`2ceceea6`, same day, same environment):
provisioned discover — 2,494 OK (skipped=2); stdlib-only discover —
**2,407 ran, FAILED (errors=3, skipped=2)**: the 3 errors were the
undeclared-`cryptography` import failures (D1), and 90 attestation
tests were silently absent from the count.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **First real ingest has never happened** (plan D6 INFO): the
  pipeline is proven against synthetic fixtures only. This is an
  operator decision (when, not whether the capability is the target),
  not a code gap.
- **v111 runner empty-run green**: `benchmarks/run_v111_regression.py`
  reports `all_passed: true` with `module_count: 0` when no test
  modules are discovered (observed 2026-11-09 during D4 verification;
  v112 explicitly refuses empty runs, v111 does not). Not yet fixed.
- **v111 default journal path is host-relative**: with
  `MONEY_ENGINE_JOURNAL_DIR` unset the runner still defaults to
  `/mnt/data` — now a documented, loudly-failing default (D4), but
  hosts without that mount must set the variable.
- Claim **preparation** machinery is real; **filing code does not
  exist**. Legal entitlement is absent (code-enforced).
- The README is a 186 KB version ledger — an index, not verification.
  Where it disagrees with this file, this file wins.

## What is NOT true

- **"MoneyEngine is a payment / revenue engine."** False. No Stripe,
  bank API, charge, payout, or transfer exists in the pipeline;
  revenue is hardcoded to 0 and nonzero revenue values are rejected
  by its own validators. The v125 code on main is verification-only
  and likewise moves no money.
- **"MoneyEngine has sold something / can recognize a sale today."**
  False. $0 revenue ever stands. The v125 offer self-reports
  `publishedSaleReady: False`, its release document states it is not
  publicly launch-accepted, and no paid order exists anywhere in
  evidence.
- **"Real California data has been ingested and the pipeline is
  proven on it."** Not established. The repo contains no data files;
  every test runs on synthetic fixtures.
- **"This engine files claims."** False. The v123 packet builder
  produces a print-ready packet for a human to mail; it files
  nothing, submits nothing, contacts nobody, and cannot hold a
  TIN/SSN/ID or signature.
- **"The test suite runs on the standard library alone at full
  coverage."** False. One declared dependency exists
  (`cryptography`, for the Ed25519 attestation machinery). Without
  it the suite completes but the 90 attestation tests skip — by
  name, since PR #8; before that they errored at import and the
  coverage loss was silent.
- **"The v125 release is unmerged / branch-only."** No longer true
  (it was, until 2026-11-09): PRs #4→#5→#6 merged to main as one
  chain. What remains true is that it is not launch-accepted.

## Landing record (2026-11-09 fix wave)

- PR #7 — D4: v111 journal dir configurable (`MONEY_ENGINE_JOURNAL_DIR`).
- PR #8 — D1: `requirements.txt` + explicit attestation skip guards.
- PR #9 — D2: `run_tests.sh` + `Makefile` + README "Running the tests".
- This refresh — D3: GROUND_TRUTH Pass 2 + README ground-truth pointer.
- Earlier: PR #1 (runner honesty — the runner always re-executes;
  historical 2,403-pass claim downgraded), PR #3 (filing layer),
  PRs #4→#5→#6 (v124/v125 chain, one landing decision).

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# murmuration-codex — GROUND TRUTH

**Repo:** sa6ag9/murmuration-codex
**Status header:** GROUND TRUTH — Pass 2, verified 2026-11-08 by Knights' build run under Savage's direct order (2026-11-08 02:31 PT). This replaces the Pass-1 statement and the repo's earlier GROUND_TRUTH.md, whose header was stale (it described a pre-merge head after the merges it narrated had landed). Default branch: `main` @ `e0da722d` at the time of the build; the build lands as a branch + PR from that head. Where any other document in this repo disagrees with this file, this file wins.

## (a) What this system is and does

Murmuration is a **proof-and-verification harness plus a working logical-agent execution layer**, built 2026-11-08 to the architecture its own plan documents declare (BUILD-PROMPT.md, docs/MURMURATION-FINAL-BUILD-PLAN.md, phases P1–P8).

The harness (pre-existing, re-verified): frozen pre-declared tasks, hash-chained traces of real local inference, fail-closed loaders, mutation checks, preserved failures, statuses computed rather than asserted — including the WO-P3-001 inference proof (a frozen 20-task corpus through a hash-pinned local 1.5B model in 2-node chains), the Pool substrate (P1/P2), and the foundation non-regression suite.

The execution layer (new, `murmuration/swarm.py`): 5,000 durable agent identities seeded per the ruled S=10 registry in the Pool's store; Contract-Net seat allocation computed from a hash-chained merit ledger whose intake re-computes every claimed outcome's artifact hash (a claim that does not recompute is recorded as a fabrication — merit zeroed, teaching rights stripped); a teaching loop that admits lessons only through executable verification it runs itself, over a frozen never-overwritten anchor, with a measured diversity/collapse alarm; an Observer federation whose observers hold no execution surface by construction; and a Universal Mandate executor that declares and hashes its spec (including its proof tests) before work, awards every node by Contract-Net, executes through the WO-P3-001 entry point with per-set board shards, checkpoints between legs with Merkle hashes, resumes without re-executing completed nodes, and returns impossible sub-goals as findings instead of relabeling them.

The foundation engine's original synthetic mandate path still exists but is **quarantined**: it is labeled `SYNTHETIC_DAG_INTEGRITY_ONLY` in its own report and cannot emit PROVEN_SUCCESS (the repo's open finding P2-01, closed by this build). Real mandates run through the entry point and earn their status over real artifacts.

Bulk note: the repo is ~2.5 GB, of which code is small; the rest is model transfer bulk — the Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GGUF held in two chunked encodings, hash-verified (§(c)). There are **no gpt-oss-20b weights in this repo**.

## (b) Declared spec

- `BUILD-PROMPT.md` / the build plan, phases **P1–P8**: P1 Pool substrate; P2 substrate integration; P3 categories + assignment (5,000 identities seeded per the ruled registry); P4 allocation + merit (Contract-Net bidding, merit ledger); P5 teaching loop; P6 Observer federation; P7 Universal Mandate end-to-end; P8 scale proof (duty cycle). Each phase ends in a demonstration with raw output filed (`evidence/P1.md` … `evidence/P8.md` + `.json` receipts).
- **The set registry is S=10, ruled** (docs/SET-REGISTRY-APPENDIX.md §2; Savage's ruling of 2026-11-05 recorded in that appendix): CodeEng 700, MathLogic 550, SecurityAudit 550, CryptoFin 550, DataAnalytics 450, SysOps 400, MediaOps 450, Research 400, Comms 350, ProofAtt 600 = 5,000. The §2 counts are Lens 1 §4's [PROPOSED] allocation — the only S=10 allocation in the record — implemented as the allocation of record; the appendix's Open Choices OC-1…OC-5 remain Savage's.
- The Sentinel's declared purpose, in code: **generated-data only** — `murmuration/sentinel_runtime.py` raises unless `data_scope == "generated-debate-benchmark-only"`, and every output carries `operational_decision_authorized: False`. Refusing real data is the declaration being honored, not a defect. Extending it to real data would be a new declaration for Savage, not an existing capability.
- Merit law (BUILD-PROMPT.md): merit = verified outcomes × diversity contribution × integrity; fabrication = merit zero + teaching rights stripped; merit decays (7-day half-life as implemented) and is capped (100 as implemented). Teaching is verified-only with provenance; the anchor is never overwritten.
- The engine header's five "candidate plan" items (5,000 rank-16 LoRAs, 189 GB VRAM, Wasm tokenization, 1.14 s MTTR circuit breakers) are labeled in the file itself as **design targets — not implemented in this module**.

## (c) Component state

| Component | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| WO-P3-001 proof harness (`p3_proof_run.py`, `p3_engine_entry.py`, `p3_engine_adapter.py`, `p3_inference_dag.py`, `pool.py`) | verified | Full re-execution reproduced the filed record exactly, before and after this build: acceptance PASSED, all 7 gates true, T01 20/20, T02 18/20 with the same two genuine failures (P3TASK-12, P3TASK-13), both mutation checks detected, dependencies unchanged, $0. After-run on the modified tree: acceptance PASSED again, all 7 gates true, T01 20/20, T02 18/20 with the same two failures, both mutation checks detected, dependencies unchanged (elapsed 124.6 s on a quiet box vs 2,629 s for the baseline run under heavy VM contention; results identical). |
| Swarm execution layer (`murmuration/swarm.py`, `swarm_demo.py`) | verified — at stand-in scale | Phase demonstrations P3–P8 executed 2026-11-08 on this VM with the in-repo 1.5B backend; receipts in `evidence/P3–P8.json`. P3: 5,000 identities seeded, per-set counts = registry, assignment spread max 1 (declared bound ≤ 1), wake-verified sample across all sets. P4: merit accrued only through hash-recomputing intake; Contract-Net winner independently recomputed from raw ledger events — match; fabrication injection zeroed the agent's merit (2.0 → 0.0) and stripped teaching rights on a valid hash chain. P5: valid lesson admitted, poisoned lesson rejected, author's later fabrication expelled its admitted lesson, collapse probe fired the alarm and throttled teaching. P6: fabrication rulings upheld; SQL-tampered and byte-flipped ledger copies both detected by the hash chain; observers expose no execute/generate surface. |
| Universal Mandate UM-001 (P7) | verified | `evidence/P7.json`: spec hashed before work; two legs, both entry-point PROVEN_SUCCESS, Merkle checkpoints verified; halt after leg 0, resume executed exactly the 2 remaining calls (no re-execution); all 4 real nodes passed their predeclared oracles with the real model (Paris / 46 / echo 46 / `add` passing 3 restricted asserts); the impossible sub-goal (one word simultaneously "yes" and "no") returned as a FINDING — mandate status `COMPLETED_WITH_FINDINGS`, never PROVEN_SUCCESS; merit recorded for all 4 verified nodes; a verified lesson harvested into population memory. Debate gates: untrained Sentinel ABSTAINED; trained Sentinel UPHOLD (panel unanimous 5/5 "46"; probability 0.306 recorded) — the FLIP-installs-minority branch is implemented and rule-declared but has not fired in a live run (see §(e)). |
| Scale proof (P8) | verified — cohort-bounded | `evidence/P8.json`: one full duty cycle of all 5,000 identities in 420.6 s. Inference cohort: 40 identities through the full path (wake → state-fed generation → predeclared oracle → sleep), 40/40 verified, mean generation latency 10.4 s/call (p50 2.6 s, p95 50.8 s — contention variance on a shared VM, distribution reported, not hidden). Deterministic cohort: 4,960 identities doing sha256 cross-check work; 4,950 intact + 10 planted corruptions all detected; 0 failures. Verified work products total 4,990. Projection (basis stated in the receipt): an all-inference cycle at the measured mean latency ≈ 51,808 s ≈ 14.4 h sequential on this hardware — a projection, not a run. |
| Pool (`pool.py`) | verified | Wake/sleep hash-verified store; `run()` now feeds the verified state into generation (deterministic state-context preamble: identity, set, experience digests) and records the transition back into state (defect D6 closed). P1 demo: 10/10 save/wake cycles hash-identical, SIGKILL-mid-write recovery to the exact prior hash — before and after. |
| Foundation engine (`grand_hybrid_engine.py`) | verified — with quarantine | domain_map = S=10 (sum 5,000). `execute_mandate` dispatches: dict nodes → REAL mode via the entry point (PROVEN_SUCCESS earnable; declared `sentinel_review` governs: a trained FLIP demotes the mandate and withholds the node's acceptance; untrained abstains); string nodes → quarantined synthetic (statuses `SYNTHETIC_INTEGRITY_*`); mixed → refused. Scenarios A–G all behave (`run_engine_scenarios.py`, incl. F: real mode earns PROVEN_SUCCESS over real artifacts with a labeled deterministic backend; G: real mode without a backend raises). |
| Sentinel (`minority_sentinel.py`, bundle, runtime) | verified | Untrained `evaluate_debate` abstains fail-closed — `(None, None, "[SENTINEL ABSTAIN] …")`, no fabricated probability (D3 closed; before: `(1, 0.85, "…OVERTURN MAJORITY")`). Trained path and the 22-feature contract unchanged; seed-42 numbers reproduce exactly (90.50% / 96.62% / +16.50%). Bundle re-issued as `intake/sentinel-bundle-v1.0.1` (model/dataset/evaluation/threshold byte-identical; extractor re-pinned to the D3 edit; the stale "loader does NOT exist" line corrected — D13); runtime re-pinned; v1.0.0 preserved with a SUPERSEDED pointer. Runtime tests 6/6. |
| ToolGen (`toolgen_registry.py`) | verified | Registration validates the artifact hash (the empty-string placeholder is refused by name), enters tools `REGISTERED_UNVERIFIED`; `verify_tool` promotes to VERIFIED_ACTIVE only after hash recomputation from real bytes + an execution check. Wasm tools cannot complete verification (no Wasm runtime exists here) and stay UNVERIFIED with the reason recorded (D5 closed). The live-mandate demo's tool reaches VERIFIED_ACTIVE through this path. `predict_tool_token` is labeled a simulation over seeded-random embeddings — no model head is involved. |
| Foundation suite + CFN + Merkle (substrate gates) | verified | `master_benchmark_suite.py` 5/5 before and after, identical measured values (max write 2,482 B / 0 breaches in 500; Merkle rollback 50/50 + 50/50; K* exact). Foundation zip rebuilt from the current directory incl. `merkle_vault.py` and fresh `raw_outputs/`, with a per-file SHA-256 manifest inside (D11 closed). |
| Entry point board routing (D8/D9) | verified | Board writes route to per-set shards (spec/mandate set, else CodeEng — the frozen proof corpus routes exactly as before, which is why the proof still reproduces); unknown shard fails closed. With an artifact store attached, oversized payloads are stored content-addressed and carried by reference; roundtrip verification resolves and recomputes them. The swarm mandate exercised multi-shard writes; the by-reference branch is covered by construction + the store's own hash checks (a >2.5 KB live deliverable has not yet occurred in a run — see §(e)). |
| Model bulk (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct GGUF Q4_K_M, 1,117,320,736 B) | verified | Both chunked encodings reassemble to the pinned SHA-256 `6a1a2eb6d15622bf3c96857206351ba97e1af16c30d7a74ee38970e434e9407e`. This 1.5B model is the build plan's declared stand-in backend, not the trained swarm. |
| gpt-oss-20b | absent | No weights, no code references in this repo. The weights are a separate ~13 GB transfer item outside the repo. |

## (d) How to verify

Environment: a venv at the bundle's pinned versions (numpy 2.5.4, lightgbm 4.7.0, scikit-learn 1.9.1, scipy 1.18.1, pytest, llama-cpp-python 0.3.16); TMPDIR on real disk.

1. `python foundation/codex-archive-fixed/master_benchmark_suite.py` → **ALL TESTS PASSED (5/5)**; max write 2,482 B; seed-42 Sentinel 90.50% / 96.62% / +16.50% (synthetic overlapping generator — labels mandatory).
2. `python foundation/codex-archive-fixed/run_engine_scenarios.py` → "ALL ENGINE SCENARIOS BEHAVED AS REQUIRED" (A–E quarantined synthetic vocabulary; F real-mode PROVEN_SUCCESS with a labeled fake backend; G fail-closed without a backend).
3. `python foundation/codex-archive-fixed/run_cfn_adversarial.py` → all within cap (worst case measured 2,481–2,482 B across runs — jitter on a run-dependent payload; the gated suite value is 2,482 B).
4. `python foundation/codex-archive-fixed/live_mandate_runner.py` → scripted demo completes; its tool ends VERIFIED_ACTIVE via verify_tool. Caller mode: `--candidate FILE --verifier FILE`.
5. `pytest murmuration/test_sentinel_runtime.py murmuration/test_p3_wiring.py` → **15 passed** (6 runtime + 9 wiring, main tree).
6. Untrained probe: `MinoritySentinelClassifier().evaluate_debate({...})` → `(None, None, "[SENTINEL ABSTAIN] …")`.
7. `python murmuration/p1_demo.py --model <GGUF>` → P1_PASS. `python murmuration/p2_demo.py <GGUF>` → P2_CHECKS_COMPLETE (its synthetic-path assertion expects the quarantined label).
8. **P3 proof:** `python murmuration/p3_proof_run.py --model <GGUF> --evidence <dir>` → acceptance PASSED, T01 20/20, T02 18/20 (failures P3TASK-12/13), both mutations detected, $0.
9. **Phase demos:** `python murmuration/swarm_demo.py --model <GGUF> --workdir <dir> --out <dir>` → P3–P8 receipts; compare against `evidence/P3–P8.json` (model answers may vary run to run under contention timing, statuses are earned per run).

## (e) What is NOT true

- **"5,000 agents" does not mean 5,000 resident models or 5,000 parallel workers.** It means 5,000 seeded, durable, individually-stated identities that wake, work, and sleep time-shared over ONE local 1.5B stand-in backend — demonstrated in one full duty cycle (P8). The inference cohort was 40 of 5,000 by hardware/time budget; the rest did real deterministic verification work, reported as such, never blended. An all-inference cycle is a stated projection (≈14.4 h at the measured mean latency on this VM), not a run.
- **The trained swarm is not in this repo.** The backend is the Qwen2.5-1.5B stand-in the plan declares. Savage's trained model connects behind the same Pool interface when its weights arrive; nothing here is that model, and no gpt-oss-20b weights exist in this repo.
- **The Sentinel has no evidenced accuracy on real debates.** All training/eval data is generated; the honest numbers (90.50% / 96.62% / +16.50%) belong to the synthetic overlapping generator, seed 42. The separable pipeline now labels itself SYNTHETIC-SEPARABLE in its own output (D10). Operational use remains unauthorized by design (`operational_decision_authorized: False`).
- **The debate gate's FLIP branch has not fired in a live run.** Both live panels (P7) produced an UPHOLD and an ABSTAIN. The gate rule — a FLIP installs the minority answer only if it passes the objective oracle, else the node fails as a finding — is implemented and declared, and the engine-level override (demotion) is implemented; neither has been observed firing, because no live panel has yet produced a trained FLIP. Claiming otherwise would be fabrication.
- **The by-reference board path (D9) has not carried a live >2.5 KB deliverable.** It is implemented, and the artifact store's resolve-recompute checks run in the P8 duty cycle; the frozen proof corpus produces small payloads by design, so no run yet has crossed the cap through the entry point.
- **D15 stands, deliberately:** `p2_demo.py`'s non-regression gate string-matches exact measured values. It can flip on environment drift with no code regression. Converting it to numeric parsing was judged a gate-weakening risk mid-build and left for a separate, deliberate change.
- **Cold provisioning remains unproven** (preserved from the prior GT): GitHub Actions acceptance failed at provisioning on the self-hosted box (1.04 GiB model vs ~954 MB RAM); acceptance was executed locally instead. Sustained serving under load is likewise unproven — the P8 duty cycle is one pass, not a soak test.
- **The synthetic engine path's statuses certify bookkeeping only.** `SYNTHETIC_INTEGRITY_VERIFIED` means the constant payloads were internally consistent under the four bookkeeping verifiers — by design it can never be PROVEN_SUCCESS, and any older document or receipt showing PROVEN_SUCCESS from bare-string `dag_nodes` predates the quarantine and should be read as the synthetic claim it was (finding P2-01).

## (f) Evidence basis

Pass 2, written 2026-11-08 from the build run itself: baseline reproduction of every runnable layer on the unmodified tree (suite 5/5 with identical values; scenarios/CFN/live green; sentinel pytest 6/6; wiring 9/9; P1_PASS; full WO-P3-001 proof acceptance with the filed failures reproduced exactly — the first baseline attempt was killed at task 13/20 by the 2026-11-08 11:34 UTC VM reboot and re-run clean), then the same battery after the changes, plus the P3–P8 phase demonstrations with the real model. Audit basis: `murmuration-codex.md` (estate audit, defects D1–D17) and fix plan v2 §5.8. Default-branch head at build start: `main` @ `e0da722d4627eacfdab989b946038124e9952c2f`.

# proofcrew — Ground Truth

**Last verified:** 2026-11-09 (Pass 2 + D1 fix pass — full re-verification against the tree below: every component read in code, suite executed on the merged tree, PR state read from the GitHub API; the D1 sections were re-verified against the fixed tree and live server runs the same night)
**Canonical branch:** main @ b082236d3688bb4d9c0384ac3be75a1416fe4583 (post-PR #12 merge; this file's own commit sits on top)

## What this repo is

ProofCrew: a multi-model verification pipeline — a planner model
drafts, two worker models execute in parallel (one web-grounded),
a screener model cross-checks, and an adjudicator resolves only
disagreements — emitting a SHA-256 hash-chained receipt file that
anyone can re-verify, plus an optional Ed25519 attestation over the
chain and deliverable, verified against a caller-pinned public key.
Built for the Nebius × NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon (Devpost), entered
by Savage individually. Public, MIT licensed. Covered by the
2026-11-08 estate audit (`ops-web-cluster.md`): core verified
fail-closed at 44/44 tests; the audit's defects were all on the
demo surface (D1, D2 below).

## Verified current state

- **Head:** `b082236d3688bb4d9c0384ac3be75a1416fe4583` — merge of
  PR #12 (D3 GROUND_TRUTH Pass 2); the D1 fix lands on top of it via
  its own PR. Lineage since the previous GT: `f39bde74` (PR #5) →
  `33f1c67e` (PR #8, optional attestations wired into CLI and web
  runs) → `b5314311` (PR #9, model defaults pinned to live IDs) →
  `a6099ac2` (PR #11, D2 guard) → `b082236d` (PR #12).
- **Open PRs:** exactly one — **PR #10**, "Evolution: Independent
  multi-operator Ed25519 attestation quorum" (branch
  `evolution/proof-bound-20261105`). Unlanded. Its tests prove the
  rejection paths; no positive multi-operator acceptance test exists
  yet, which is the recorded condition for calling the quorum
  verified (fix plan §6.3).
- **Tests (executed 2026-11-09 on this exact tree, post-D1-fix):**
  `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` → **71 passed**;
  `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → **70 tests, OK**.
  (The counts differ by one because pytest and unittest count one
  subtest-bearing test differently; both runners are fully green.
  Pre-D2 baseline on `b5314311` measured the same way: 44 passed;
  pre-D1-fix baseline on `b082236d`: 51 pytest / 50 unittest. The
  D1 fix added 20 tests in `tests/test_app_run_auth.py` and modified
  no existing test.)

## Component-by-component state

- **`proofcrew/crew.py`** — VERIFIED. Planner → two parallel
  workers → screener → cross-verification → adjudicator. A review
  counts as agreement only if it explicitly says "agree"; anything
  else, including an unparseable review, escalates
  (`verdict_of`/`needs_adjudication`). The screener's
  `evidence_sufficient` gates worker B's citations only on an
  explicit `false`. All model calls go through the
  `ChatTransport` protocol — no direct network code here.
- **`proofcrew/receipts.py`** — VERIFIED. SHA-256 hash chain over
  canonical JSON; `verify_receipts` returns the list of problems
  (empty = valid); `load_receipts` parses strictly.
- **`proofcrew/attestation.py`** — VERIFIED, fail-closed.
  Domain-separated Ed25519 signature over the receipt chain, the
  deliverable digest, and the signing key's id. Verification
  recomputes the expected statement from the **caller-pinned**
  public key — a key embedded in the package is never trusted —
  and rejects unexpected fields, bad signature length, and any
  statement mismatch. `load_attestation` rejects duplicate JSON
  keys and nonfinite values.
- **`proofcrew/signed_run.py`** — VERIFIED. Runs the crew, signs,
  then self-verifies the attestation before returning; a failed
  self-check raises. With no signing key configured the run is
  returned unsigned with `attestation=None` — labeled, never
  silently presented as signed (the web UI prints "Package is
  UNSIGNED" in that state).
- **`proofcrew/config.py`** — VERIFIED. Environment-only secrets;
  no key material in code (full-tree grep: no private keys). The
  default model IDs are the exact-case live IDs — planner
  `nvidia/Nemotron-3-Ultra-550b-a55b`, worker
  `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b`, screener
  `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B` — and `tests/test_config.py`
  pins the defaults to the IDs documented in `.env.example`.
  Environment variables can still override every model ID.
- **`proofcrew/transport.py`** — VERIFIED. `TokenFactoryTransport`
  is the only model-call path (OpenAI-compatible Nebius Token
  Factory endpoint).
- **`proofcrew/tavily.py`** — VERIFIED. Optional grounding: with
  `TAVILY_API_KEY` unset, worker B runs ungrounded and the run
  reports `grounded_worker_b` accordingly — degradation is
  recorded, not hidden.
- **`run.py`** (CLI) — VERIFIED. Exit 2 with a named error when
  `TOKENFACTORY_API_KEY` is unset or the signing key is bad —
  fail-closed at both entry points. Writes `deliverable.md` +
  `receipts.jsonl` and self-checks the chain before exiting.
- **`verify_receipts.py` / `attest_receipts.py`** — VERIFIED
  standalone checkers. `verify_receipts.py` is standard-library
  only (imports `proofcrew.receipts` only); `attest_receipts.py`
  additionally needs `cryptography` for Ed25519.
- **`app.py`** (demo web UI) — VERIFIED. Single in-memory
  last-run state behind a lock. **D2 FIXED by PR #11:**
  `POST /run` validates `Content-Length` before reading any body
  byte — non-numeric or negative → 400, over 64 KiB
  (`MAX_RUN_BODY_BYTES`) → 413 — where previously a bad value
  crashed the handler, a negative one hung it under the run lock,
  and an oversized one was buffered without bound. **D1 FIXED
  (this pass):** the server now binds loopback by default
  (`HOST` overrides), and `POST /run` is authorized by
  `authorize_run` before any state change or run work. With
  `PROOFCREW_RUN_TOKEN` configured, a valid token (the
  `X-ProofCrew-Token` header or the form's token field,
  constant-time compared) is required from every client. With
  no token configured, only a direct local request — loopback
  bind, loopback client, no proxy/tunnel forwarding headers —
  is accepted; forwarded, remote, and wide-bind requests are
  refused 403 with a named reason, because a tunnel makes a
  remote visitor indistinguishable from a local client at the
  address level. The viewing endpoints (page, deliverable,
  receipts, attestation of the last run) remain public by
  design — D1 was the spend surface, and the spend surface is
  what is gated. Exposure and closure were both proven against
  live servers (before: `0.0.0.0` listen + unauthenticated POST
  drove a real provider API call with the server's key; after:
  loopback listen, forwarded and wide-bind POSTs refused,
  token POSTs accepted, on three configurations).

## Reported, not re-verified this pass

- **Live runs:** two full runs against the Nebius Token Factory
  API (2026-10-30), each producing 8 receipts with a VALID hash
  chain; run #2 was web-grounded (Tavily) and adjudicated, with
  real citations. — REPORTED (2026-10-30 record; not re-executed
  2026-11-09; no spend was authorized for this pass).
- **Demo and video:** a public demo (recorded run #2) and an
  88-second demo video, verified live on 2026-10-30. — REPORTED;
  not re-checked this pass. The demo dies if the Oracle box or
  the tunnel dies.
- **The one live signed run** remains STAGED-ONLY per the PR #5
  filer's disclosure: execution needs an operator key + Nebius
  key + spend authorization. — REPORTED, carried forward.

## Known defects / honest gaps

- **D1 FIXED** — the demo bound `0.0.0.0` with `POST /run`
  unauthenticated (an open spend surface whenever reachable,
  including via the public demo's Cloudflare quick tunnel).
  Closed per the queue target (row 77): localhost bind by
  default + `/run` authenticated by the operator token
  whenever a request is not a direct local one. See the
  `app.py` component entry for the exact policy and proof.
  Operator note: exposing the demo through any tunnel or
  proxy without setting `PROOFCREW_RUN_TOKEN` leaves `/run`
  refusing forwarded requests — deliberately; set the token.
- **ProofCrew was never submitted to the hackathon** — verified
  first-hand 2026-10-30 (Devpost portfolio shows 0 projects; no
  confirmation mail exists). The submission task failed silently.
  A late-entry request was emailed to the hackathon manager on
  2026-10-31; no reply is recorded. The deadline (2026-10-30
  10:00 AM PT) has passed. (Historical record, carried from the
  previous GT; not re-checked this pass.)
- **No production signing key exists** or is claimed anywhere in
  this repo; fixtures are test-only.
- **PR #10's quorum is not verified** — rejection paths only
  (see Open PRs above).

## What is NOT true

- The head is **not** `3db2fc19` (PR #4) and **not** `f39bde74`
  (PR #5). The previous version of this file asserted both in
  different sections — that internal contradiction was defect
  D3. The only head claim is the one at the top of this file.
- Open PRs are **not** none: PR #10 is open.
- Model IDs do **not** have to be passed via environment to be
  correct: the code defaults are the exact-case live IDs (the
  pre-PR #5 gap is closed; overrides remain available). The old
  "casing must be passed via environment" line is retired.
- The suite is **not** 40 tests (previous GT) and not 15: it is
  51 by pytest / 50 by unittest on this tree, both green.
- ProofCrew was **not** submitted to the hackathon (see gaps).
- A valid receipt chain does **not** prove the models' claims
  are true — it proves the recorded bytes were not altered
  afterwards. The attestation authenticates the designated key
  and the exact bytes: not model claims, not source truth, not
  settlement. `docs/SIGNED_EVIDENCE_EXPORT.md` states the same
  scope.
- The demo's spend endpoint is **not** open anymore: the
  pre-fix claim "the demo is not authenticated and not
  localhost-only" described D1 and is retired. What remains
  true: the tunnel URL is **not** a private surface for
  *viewing* (the page and the last run's artifacts are public
  by design), and a tunnel without `PROOFCREW_RUN_TOKEN` set
  cannot run the crew at all — runs are refused, not exposed.

## How to verify

- `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` (with `requirements.txt`
  installed) → expect 71 passed at this head;
  `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → expect OK (70 tests).
- `python3 verify_receipts.py <receipts.jsonl>` → chain check,
  standard library only.
- Head check: `GET /repos/Savages-studios/proofcrew/git/ref/heads/main`.

## Estate rule

Update this file after any significant repo change. No claims without verification.

# savage-hunter — GROUND TRUTH — Pass 2 (code-verified refresh)

**Status header:** Repo `Savages-studios/savage-hunter`, default branch `main` @ `9d62646337344941d1f24729019fb2af136b3f01` (Merge PR #39, 2026-11-10). **Pass 2 verified first-hand 2026-11-11 by Knights (fix #124)** in a clean extraction of the current tree (86 files): full suite **274 tests OK, 0 skipped** (Python 3.12.3), loopback smoke passing, `python -m hunter doctor` clean, all probes below re-run at this baseline. This Pass 2 **supersedes** the prior in-repo GROUND_TRUTH.md, whose headline verification was the PR #22 baseline of 2026-11-05 (suite 198) — the staleness recorded as audit Defect 3. Every claim below was re-verified against the current tree's source, tests, data, CI, and **all 33 branches** — not carried over from Pass 1.

**The one-sentence truth:** Hunter is a finished, heavily tested **local build** — and it is **not deployed, not connected to any live channel, and has never sold or sent anything.** Both halves are proven below; the repo's own README says the same.

## (a) What this system is and does

A proof-bound commercial opportunity engine that runs entirely locally: it compiles evidence-bound offers from a capability-truth registry, stores prospect consent and inbound conversations under fail-closed eligibility rules, plans human-dialed call operations, maintains a transaction-bound HMAC audit trail, and verifies Stripe webhooks — while deliberately containing **no outbound adapter of any kind**. Nothing in the repository dials, sends, messages, or charges. The server hard-refuses non-loopback binds (`hunter/server.py:296-298`). Payment reconciliation is read-only.

The audit splits the "Hunter is finished" question in two, and the repo itself draws the line:

- **Finished as a build — verified, and stronger than at Pass 1.** Feature-complete against its own declarations, stdlib-only (one Windows-only `tzdata` dependency), with a strong fail-closed test discipline: **274 tests passing at head with 0 skips**, loopback HTTP smoke passing, `python -m hunter doctor` clean, and **CI green at the exact head commit on both workflows** — core regression (run `42897780523`, success) and native cross-OS acceptance (run `42897780525`, success, Ubuntu + Windows legs). Every defect the Pass 1 audit recorded against the build (Defects 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) has since been repaired on main and is re-verified fixed in §c — including the HIGH callops price-tamper hole (Defect 1). Org CI additionally caught a real Windows portability defect after Pass 1 (CRLF checkouts changed the registry bytes the pinned loader hashes; a locale-decoding defect in data-file I/O) — fixed in PR #39 with regression tests and real-Windows runs.
- **Finished as a deployed / operating commercial engine — contradicted, unchanged.** The shipped catalog can never compile an executable offer (all 48 offers fail their gates, all Stripe IDs null), and Hunter's own ledgers record 0 journeys, 0 dispatches, 0 fulfillments, 0 sales. The README says the same in plain words: "This pilot is not a production sales service." The import runbook (`IMPORT-STATUS.md`) records steps 1–3 done (import + verification) and steps 4–8 — one genuinely sellable SKU end-to-end, one connected inbound channel, a consent-verified outbound adapter, a supervised customer path — **not done**.

End to end: FIND is real but the harvest lives outside the repo (leads are canonicalized with mandatory provenance; 226 shipped leads per dataset file all validate, 0 with `contact_authorized` true). VERIFY is the strongest part (consent ordering, SHA-256-pinned registry on **every** load path since PR #33, claims gate with 0 violations over all 28 shipped packages). ACT is deliberately absent; REPORT is real and honest (metrics hard-code `actual_dispatches: 0, actual_fulfillments: 0`). Hunter's proofs verify internal consistency and gate compliance rigorously — an HMAC hash chain and code-pinned registry digests — but the HMAC trust root is a device-local operator key, consent/inbound records are labelled `operator_asserted` in code, and nothing claims to prove a real buyer, payment, or delivery exists in the outside world.

## (b) Declared spec

What this repo claims to be, per its governing documents:

- `README.md` — "An executable, proof-bound commercial opportunity engine for Savage AI Studios / Everything Savage LLC," with status in capitals: "LOCAL PILOT IMPLEMENTED AND TESTED. NOT DEPLOYED, NOT CONNECTED TO A LIVE CALLING OR MESSAGING PROVIDER, NOT GENERATING VERIFIED REVENUE." It declares there is "currently no actual message dispatcher and no live voice adapter," lists the still-required work to reach live operations, and states: "This pilot is **not** a production sales service."
- `docs/SAVAGE-HUNTER-BLUEPRINT.md` — the launch specification (2026-10-30), self-labelled "Research-backed proposal. Not implemented or deployed by this report." It specifies the ProofBound Opportunity Compiler, which emits exactly one of `ExecutableOffer` (complete, priced, with independently verified fulfillment and payment route), `NeedsApproval`, `UnserviceableNeed`, or `ForbiddenAction`. Measured against that spec, the shipped catalog can currently emit only the non-executable outcomes — by design, because the verification evidence does not exist yet.
- `IMPORT-STATUS.md` — the release runbook: import and first-hand verification (steps 1–3) completed 2026-11-02; steps 4–8 (sellable SKU end-to-end, connected inbound channel, outbound adapter, supervised customer path, field experiment) remain the gates to live operation and are **not recorded as done anywhere in the repo**.
- Charter fences (preserved from the prior GT, still in force): claims proof-bound to the capability-truth registry; consent integrity is code; first-send of any new campaign gets Savage's sign-off; Profit Brain placeholder until 25 completed journeys (count ZERO); evidence boundary — "All test buyers, payments and consent in this validation are fixtures… commercial operation remains unproven."

The declared spec and the code agree unusually well. The "not true" items in §e are one recurring evidence-file staleness (test-results.txt) and any reading of "finished" that means "operating."

## (c) Component state

| Component | State | Evidence (Pass 2, at `9d626463…`) |
|---|---|---|
| Lead finder (`hunter/leadfinder.py`) — canonicalizes harvested records with mandatory source-URL + observation-date provenance and own-domain contact citation | verified | Re-validated first-hand: `data/leadfinder-pilot-2026-11-05.json` and `data/leadfinder-vnext-2026-11-05.json` each hold 226 leads; all 226 in each file pass `validate_lead_record`; 0 leads `contact_authorized` true; 28 leads per file carry packages. Harvest itself happened outside the repo; pilot report discloses all 7 vertical harvests hit HTTP 429 caps (`docs/LEADFINDER-PILOT-2026-11-05.md`) |
| Discovery actors inventory (`hunter/actors.py`) | reported / observed (honestly labelled) | Runnability is **computed**, not a static table: `runnable_today()` (`actors.py:282-290`) marks the 3 gateway-local actors (`echo`, `qr-code-generator`, `tooldiff`) runnable via the local actor gateway and the generic public-web fallback runnable; every fleet discovery actor returns `False` with reason. It remains a preference table (`preferred_sources`) — Hunter invokes none of these actors to harvest; the harvest lives outside the repo. (Corrects Pass 1's "every actor False" — the mechanism changed.) |
| Consent engine (`hunter/core.py` `eligible()`) — suppression → permission → destination binding → expiry → channel window → quiet hours → human-review, fail-closed, in that order; every permission write invalidates queued actions; `plan_action` re-checks inside the transaction | verified | Full suite at head (consent, atomic admission/revocation, queue revalidation, quiet-hours suites all green — §d) |
| Capability-truth registry, core path (`hunter/registry.py`) — fail-closed load with SHA-256 pin in code | verified | Digits recomputed first-hand at this baseline: v1 `f8c66bf36b9c…` and v2 `662c5191f72d…` — both match the pins at `registry.py:24-26`. v2 is the registry of record (60 entries: 48 offers + 12 parked, rebound by SKU to the gen-2 Stripe account's doors) |
| Call-ops registry loader (`hunter/callops.py` `load_registry_data`) | **verified (Defect 1 FIXED)** | Was Pass 1's HIGH contradiction. Since PR #33 (merged 2026-11-09) the loader **delegates to `hunter.registry.load_registry`** — one pinned loader for the whole repo (module docstring corrected: PR #20 "is on main"). Pass 2 tamper probe, first-hand: a v2 copy with `amountTotal` 19900 → 100 is **REFUSED by both** `registry.load_registry` (`RegistryError: registry bytes do not match the pinned version digest`) and `callops.load_registry_data` (`RegistryDataError`, same refusal). Suite adds `CallOpsLoaderPinTests` (4 tests: tamper / version-swap / missing-file refused, pristine v1 loads) — all pass |
| Claims gate (`check_message_claims`) + package verification | verified | Re-ran `verify_package` over all 28 shipped packages under registry v2 — 0 violations (first-hand, this baseline) |

Independent re-checks in this pass:

- Recomputed both registry SHA-256 digests — match the code pins (`registry.py:24-26`) exactly.
- **Tamper probe (the Defect 1 test):** a copy of registry v2 with `amountTotal` edited 19900 → 100 is refused by `hunter.registry.load_registry` **and** by `hunter.callops.load_registry_data`. At Pass 1 the callops path accepted it; it no longer does.

- **"Hunter is finished" — if "finished" means deployed, operating, or selling.** Contradicted by the repo's own code and data: no outbound adapter exists, the server refuses non-loopback binds (`hunter/server.py:296-298`), all 48 shipped offers fail their gates with null Stripe IDs so no offer can be executable and `receive_stripe` can never accept a payment against the shipped catalog, and the ledgers record 0 journeys / 0 dispatches / 0 fulfillments / 0 sales. - **"A webhook-verified payment is a settled, fulfilled sale."** — The code itself refuses this reading: reconciliation returns `provider_readback: required_not_observed` and `release_allowed: False` for every row; the webhook never calls back to Stripe, so a receipt is never dressed up as settlement or readback.
- **"Hunter's proofs independently prove real buyers, payments, or deliveries."** — They prove internal consistency only. The HMAC key is a device-local file the operator controls; consent and inbound records are labelled `operator_asserted` in code; signed web ingress authenticates the relay and returns `visitor_verified: False, marketing_permission_granted: False`.
- **"The version is 0.1.0 / 0.2.0 / 0.3, depending where you look."** — No longer true: since PR #36 there is exactly one version source, `hunter.__version__ = "0.3.0"`, and the other surfaces derive from it under test.
- **"Windows-native support is not continuously verified; CI status at head is unknown."** — No longer true: the acceptance workflow triggers on `main` (PR #38) and is green at the exact head alongside the core regression (runs `42897780525`, `42897780523`). The Windows legs have already earned their keep — they caught the CRLF digest defect that PR #39 fixed.
- **"The commerce stack (PRs #25–#32) is part of the shipped Hunter."** — Not true: all eight are unmerged **drafts** on `commerce/*` branches. Main contains no outbound dispatch queue, outcome ingestion, or suppression-dispatch machinery; what those drafts propose is a decision that has not been taken.
- **"The callops real-registry contract test always skips in CI."** — No longer true (PR #34): it reads the in-repo registry and passes in CI and locally; the suite at head reports 0 skips.

# GROUND_TRUTH — glitch-books-private

Private fulfillment repo for the five $9 Glitch coloring books sold from the
Savage AI Studios storefront (`sa6ag9/savageaistudios-site`, `coloring-books/`).
Written from code and file evidence, 2026-11-09. Claim-state labels:
*verified* (proven by a run or read this session), *declared* (stated by a
repo document, not independently proven), *not established*.

## What is here, component by component

| Component | State |
| --- | --- |
| The five PDFs (`glitch-{rain,honey,moon,bridge,bird}-book.pdf`) | *verified* — byte counts and SHA-256 match `SHA256-MANIFEST.json` exactly (verifier run, 2026-11-09: 5/5 PASS). They are the fulfillment copies, moved out of the public site repo on 2026-11-02 so the paid books are not publicly downloadable (README). |
| `SHA256-MANIFEST.json` | *verified* — lists exactly the five PDFs, each with `bytes`, `sha256`, and `git_blob_sha`. It is the integrity reference for fulfillment; the runbook's stop conditions halt a send on mismatch. |
| `FULFILLMENT-RUNBOOK.md` | *declared* — the fulfillment model of record: manual email delivery to the checkout address, usually within one business day; payment proven from the Stripe dashboard, never from a thank-you page or redirect; no public download URL is ever sent. Knights does not independently prove orders are fulfilled this way — that is an operations fact, not a repo fact. |
| `tools/verify_fulfillment.py` | *verified* — one-command verifier (stdlib-only Python). Recomputes every PDF against the manifest, fails on unlisted PDFs, and scans supplied storefront copy for delivery-model drift: any "download" wording in a page's meta description or visible text fails, and the email-delivery promise must be present in both. Exit 0 only on a full pass; `--json` for machine consumption. Built 2026-11-09 as an evolution item under the estate fix program. |
| `tests/test_verify_fulfillment.py` | *verified* — 11 fixture-based tests, all passing 2026-11-09. They prove the verifier fails on a tampered PDF, on manifest hash and byte-count mismatches, on download wording in meta or body, on a missing email promise, on a missing thanks page, on an unlisted PDF, and when no storefront is supplied. Fixtures only — the tests never touch the real goods or the live site. |
| Storefront agreement | *verified* — verifier run 2026-11-09 against the site repo's `coloring-books/` tree at site main `7357864e`: 26/26 checks PASS (goods 7/7, storefront presence 7/7, copy rules 12/12). The pages promise email delivery and contain no "download" wording. |
| EVO-4 measurement evidence (`evidence/measure_evo4.py`, `tests/fixtures/storefront/`) | *verified* — the evolution's before/after measurement is reproducible from this repo: the harness measures the pre-change tree (base `c6ffbfb8`: no `tools/`, no `tests/` — 0 automated checks) against this tree (26/26 verifier checks over the repo goods + the pinned storefront snapshot, site main `4efd6486`, provenance in the fixture's `PROVENANCE.json`; fixture suite 11/11). Recorded run: `evidence/evo4-measurement.json` (re-run 2026-11-10: reproduced). |

## How to verify

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v          # the verifier's own proof
python3 tools/verify_fulfillment.py \
  --storefront /path/to/savageaistudios-site/coloring-books
python3 evidence/measure_evo4.py                  # EVO-4 before/after proof
sha256sum glitch-*-book.pdf                       # spot-check vs the manifest
```

## What is NOT true

- Fulfillment is NOT automated. The runbook is a manual procedure; the
  site's webhook records a paid order as a pending human work item and does
  not email anything (runbook, "Automation boundary").
- The verifier does NOT prove that any order was paid or any email was
  sent, and it does NOT fetch the live deployed site — it checks the
  storefront directory you hand it. Point it at a fresh export of the live
  site if you need the deployed copy proven.
- The verifier does NOT cover other sales channels (e.g. Gumroad drafts);
  their product files are attached and checked elsewhere.
- The PDFs carry no watermarking or per-buyer tracking (*not established*
  either way from repo contents — nothing in the tree implements it).
- Nothing in this repo authorizes a deployment, a payment-provider call, or
  sending any file to any buyer. Those stay behind their own gates.

# Ground Truth — savage-relay

Code-proven state of this repository and its deployments: Slice 1,
2026-11-09; Slice 2 (Sol bridge), 2026-11-10; Slice 3 (Tara bridge),
2026-11-10; RELAY-E1 live carry (Tara), 2026-11-10; RELAY-E2
interoperability surface, 2026-11-15.
Every claim below is checkable against the code in this repo or the running
service's `/health` and `/admin/verify` endpoints. Labels follow house
practice: **verified** = demonstrated by a run recorded in this repo;
**observed** = read from the code or the live state; **not established** =
nobody has proven it yet.

## What this system is

A seat-to-seat message bus for the Savage AI Studios assistant seats,
written from zero in this repo (Savage-original, Python standard library
only — there are no third-party dependencies to audit). Design record:
`docs/DESIGN.md`, including Savage's 2026-11-09 amendments, which govern
where the original spec and the amendments differ.

## Component-by-component state

| Component | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Bus core (`relay/server.py`) | **Built.** Per-seat bearer-token auth (SHA-256 hashes stored, never tokens), per-seat queues, send/poll/ack, presence heartbeat, unknown-recipient rejection | Code; acceptance run below |
| Hash-chained event log | **Built.** Append-only JSONL; every record carries the previous record's hash; transitions chained: `MESSAGE_QUEUED`, `MESSAGE_DELIVERED`, `MESSAGE_ACKED`, plus `SEAT_REGISTERED`, `SEAT_TOKEN_MINTED`, `AUTH_REJECTED`, `FORGED_PICKUP`, `INGEST_REJECTED`, `SEND_REJECTED`, `ID_CONFLICT`, `BUS_BOOT` | Code; independent chain recompute inside the acceptance test |
| Secret-shape ingest filter | **Built and verified.** Bodies matching credential shapes (GitHub tokens, private-key blocks, AWS/OpenAI/Slack/Google keys, JWTs, bearer blobs, relay tokens) are refused with HTTP 422; the refusal is logged by pattern name; the body is never stored or logged | Probe run 2026-11-09: two secret-shaped bodies rejected (`github_token_classic`, `private_key_block`), clean body accepted, rejected text absent from the log |
| Idempotent send | **Built and verified.** Client message-id + request-hash fingerprint (pattern adapted from savage-router's console): a retry returns the original receipt; id reuse with different content is a 409 and is logged | Acceptance check (f) |
| Seat client (`relay/client.py`) | **Built.** Library + CLI: heartbeat, send, poll, ack, seats, message, health | Code; used by the acceptance test and by Knights' poller |
| Acceptance gate (`tests/test_acceptance.py`) | **PASS — all six checks**, recorded in `evidence/acceptance-slice1.json`: (a) exact delivery + receipt quoting nonce and body hash; (b) zero leakage to other seats; (c) exactly one `DELIVERED` transition per message across repeated polls, chain verifies; (d) forged pickup rejected (401 unknown token, 403 non-recipient ack) and logged; (e) offline store-and-forward delivered byte-identical on the seat's return; (f) idempotent resend | `evidence/acceptance-slice1.json` |
| Bridge (`relay/bridge.py`, `run_bridge.py`) | **Built and verified against the fake thread adapter.** Carries one non-polling seat in both directions, byte-identical: poll-with-reconciliation inbound (carry log + `include_delivered`), deterministic-client-id sends outbound, watermark advanced only past carried or bus-refused replies, over-long replies chunked with `part n/m` markers, adapter failure marks the seat unreachable in the bridge's status record (and optionally posts an operator notice) *without polling* — the seat's messages stay `QUEUED` on the bus | `tests/test_bridge.py`; `evidence/acceptance-slice2.json`; live-bus probe pair on the local instance's chain (seq 10–15, bodies marked as probes) |
| Fake thread adapter (`FakeThreadAdapter` in `relay/bridge.py`) | **Built.** Deterministic, file-backed stand-in for a ChatGPT thread (counter ids, injectable replies, simulated session death). It is a test/demo double behind the `ThreadAdapter` interface — it is not connected to any real thread | Code; used by both Slice 2 test harnesses |
| Bridge acceptance gate (`tests/test_bridge.py`) | **PASS — all five checks**: (a) exact carry in, hash matching receipt and chained event; (b) exact carry out, one `QUEUED` in the chain; (c) adapter down → status marks the seat unreachable, notice sent, message held `QUEUED`, carried exactly once on recovery; (d) restart resumes with zero duplicates across both crash windows (post-before-ack, poll-before-post), chain verifies; (e) a 9,658-char reply chunked into 2 marked parts reassembles byte-identical | `evidence/acceptance-slice2.json` |
| Bridge metrics (`tests/measure_bridge.py`) | **Measured.** 24 round trips, fake adapter, passes back-to-back: one-way-in median 0.578 s (p95 0.724), one-way-out median 0.479 s, round-trip median 1.049 s (p95 1.214); **fidelity 48/48 legs byte-exact (100%)**, hash-compared. Baseline: the measured 2026-11-09 mail leg (chase 17:22 PT → reply delivered 21:15 PT) = 13,980 s one-way with no byte-exactness mechanism. Ratios: ≈24,000× (machine loop), ≈46.5× even at the production Shape-A worst case (300 s cadence + machine median) | `evidence/bridge-metrics-slice2.json` |
| Tara bridge (Slice 3) | **Built and verified against the fake thread adapter, and its first live carry is complete (below).** The same `Bridge` machinery as Slice 2, second seat: `tara` registered on the local instance, token minted into the local run dir only (mode 0600, never in this repo), bridge configured for thread `6ad9ba71` (Forge Tights Handshake, sa6ag9), replies carried to `knights`. The bridge code itself is seat-generic; Slice 3 added no bridge-code change — the seat's own acceptance gate and metrics harness are the new artifacts | `tests/test_bridge_tara.py`; `evidence/acceptance-slice3.json`; local instance chain seq 17–18 (`SEAT_REGISTERED`, `SEAT_TOKEN_MINTED` for `tara`) |
| RELAY-E1 live carry — Tara (2026-11-10) | **First live carry COMPLETE, byte-exact both legs — RELAY-E1's live-carry claim is PROVEN for this carry.** Knights posted the staged probe `KNIGHTS-2026-11-10-02` (bus message `f0ebbe78b659468a807e0008b93d26ef`, 456 chars, body SHA-256 `789f897b…`, verified against the bus store before posting) byte-identical into Tara's real ChatGPT thread (`6ad9ba71-d4f4-83e8-b5c8-5e298d2ef791`, "Forge Tights Handshake", sa6ag9) at 2026-11-10T16:32Z via the signed-in browser session. Tara's reply, captured verbatim after generation completed (169 chars, SHA-256 `8718f9ac…`), was carried back on the bus as `tara` → `knights` (message `d1e4a04cf35a463db35da083ca5427f6`, queued 2026-11-10T16:34:25Z); Knights polled it, the carried body was byte-identical to the thread text (direct string comparison true; bus `body_sha256` == thread-text SHA-256), and both messages end `ACKED`. The live adapter here is browser-mediated Shape A operated by Knights — not an automated daemon. Register metric (§8): live cross-vendor carries with byte-exact receipts 0 → 1; chain-verification of carried messages 100% (24/24 events). The register's "first 100 carries" scale target and continuous operation (box deployment, transfer Phase 4) remain open | `evidence/relay-e1-live-carry-2026-11-10.json`; chain verified two independent ways: `/admin/verify` → ok, 24 events, tip `1c17aa0c…`; Knights' independent recompute of `events.jsonl` (server's canonical algorithm) → 24 events, intact, same tip |

End state: probe delivered + `ACKED` as tara; reply `ACKED`; chain length 24, verified two ways — see the RELAY-E1 live-carry row above | Local instance chain seq 17–19 (registration, token mint, probe queued; seq 16 is an `AUTH_REJECTED` for an unauthenticated `/seats` probe by the same crew); `/health` at staging time (seats 4, queued 1); `/admin/verify` ok, chain length 19 at staging, 24 after the carry; `evidence/relay-e1-live-carry-2026-11-10.json` |

Card fields: name, description, url, provider (Savage AI Studios), version, capabilities `{streaming: false, pushNotifications: false, stateTransitionHistory: true}`, default input/output modes `["text/plain"]`, skills `send-message` / `poll-inbox` / `acknowledge`. Cards contain no credentials and only public discovery data | Code; interop gate checks (a)–(b) in `evidence/acceptance-interop.json` |

Notifications (no `id`) → HTTP 204, no body; malformed JSON-RPC → `-32700`/`-32600`; unknown method → `-32601`; unknown tool → `-32602`; `GET /mcp` → 405. The client side speaks only the two public specs (raw `http.client` + JSON; no `relay.client` import, no direct Relay calls): bus + seat card discovery, MCP initialize and tools/list, **12 protocol-native round trips (relay_send → relay_poll → relay_ack) with fidelity 12/12 byte-exact** (delivered body identical, `body_sha256` == sha256(body), every ack `ACKED`), the `relay_seats`/`relay_health` tools, negative controls (forged ack, unknown recipient, secret-shaped body, unknown tool, missing/unknown MCP token → 401, unknown seat card → 404, `GET /mcp` → 405, notification/parse/invalid/unknown-method protocol edges), and a final `/admin/verify` chain check | `evidence/acceptance-interop.json` |
| Deployment (first instance) | **Running** on Knights' VM, bound to `127.0.0.1:8799` (see "What is NOT true" for why not the tailnet), state in a directory outside this repo, supervised by a restart wrapper, `/health` answering | Deploy record in the build report to Knights, 2026-11-09 |
| Seats | `knights`: **registered, token minted, client configured, inbox polled by a local poller**. `tights`: **reserved slot** (name registered, no token — see below). `sol`: **registered on the local instance, token minted into the local run dir only** (mode 0600, never in this repo), bridge client configured for thread `6aee18e6`. `tara`: **registered on the local instance (2026-11-10), token minted into the local run dir only** (mode 0600, never in this repo), bridge client configured for thread `6ad9ba71` | Live state via `GET /seats`; chain seq 8–9 (`SEAT_REGISTERED`, `SEAT_TOKEN_MINTED` for `sol`), seq 17–18 (same for `tara`) |

## Interoperability surface (RELAY-E2)

RELAY-E2 exposes the same bus to external agents through two public
specs, both hand-rolled in stdlib Python with zero new dependencies
(server version 0.2.0):

- **Agent Card discovery** (`relay/agentcard.py`): the bus card at
  `/.well-known/agent-card.json` and one card per seat at
  `/agent-cards/<seat>`, in the A2A Agent Card shape. Discovery is
  public; the cards name the bus and its seats, give each seat's card
  URL, and advertise the three skills (send-message, poll-inbox,
  acknowledge). They carry no credentials and grant no access.
- **MCP tools** (`POST /mcp` in `relay/server.py`): a JSON-RPC 2.0
  subset (`initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`) whose five
  `relay_*` tools are the native send/poll/ack/seats/health operations
  under MCP framing — same per-seat bearer auth, same refusals (as
  `isError` tool results), same hash-chained events. There is no
  second delivery path and no second semantics to drift.

The proof is `tests/test_interop.py`: an external client that speaks
only those two specs completes 12 round trips byte-exact (12/12) and
passes every negative control, recorded in
`evidence/acceptance-interop.json`.

## How to verify

1. `python3 tests/test_acceptance.py` — boots a throwaway bus and re-runs
   the whole founding gate. Exit 0 means all six checks passed again.
2. Against the running instance: `GET /health` (counts + chain tip) and
   `GET /admin/verify` with the operator admin token (full chain recompute).
3. Read `relay/server.py`: the delivery path is `Relay.poll` — a seat's
   poll can only ever select messages whose `to` equals that seat, under
   one lock, with the `DELIVERED` transition chained before the response.
4. `python3 tests/test_bridge.py` — boots a throwaway bus and re-runs
   the whole Slice 2 bridge gate (carry in/out, adapter failure,
   restart safety, chunking) against the fake thread adapter.
5. `python3 tests/measure_bridge.py` — re-measures the bridge round
   trip and hash-compared fidelity; compare against
   `evidence/bridge-metrics-slice2.json`.
6. `python3 tests/test_bridge_tara.py` — the Slice 3 gate: same five
   checks for seat `tara` / thread `6ad9ba71`.
   `python3 tests/measure_bridge_tara.py` — the Tara bridge metrics;
   compare against `evidence/bridge-metrics-slice3.json`.
7. The RELAY-E1 live carry is an operational record, not a re-runnable
   test: read `evidence/relay-e1-live-carry-2026-11-10.json`, then
   recompute the running instance's chain (`GET /admin/verify`) — at
   carry time it held 24 events, tip `1c17aa0c…`, the length and tip
   the evidence file records.
8. `python3 tests/test_interop.py` — boots a throwaway bus and re-runs
   the whole RELAY-E2 interop gate as an external client (Agent Card
   discovery + MCP tools only); on success it writes
   `evidence/acceptance-interop.json`. Exit 0 means all fifteen checks
   passed again, including 12/12 byte-exact round trips.

## What is NOT true

- **Tights is NOT connected.** Her seat is a reserved slot: the name is
  registered, but no token exists for it and nothing has been sent to or
  received from her side. Her token is minted when she connects (see
  ONBOARDING.md) and is never minted, held, or recorded by Knights or by
  this repo in advance.
- **Sol is NOT yet talking on the bus.** The Slice 2 bridge machinery is
  built and acceptance-proven against a deterministic fake thread
  adapter and the local bus — but no message has been carried into or
  out of any real ChatGPT thread. The live adapter (design Shape A:
  agent-mediated browser passes against Sol's designated thread
  `6aee18e6`) is a separate operational step, not part of this code; the
  bridge CLI's `chatgpt` adapter kind fails closed as not-built. The
  only `sol` traffic on the local instance's chain is the clearly
  marked Slice 2 acceptance probe pair (seq 10–15) — its "reply" was
  injected into the fake adapter, not written by Sol.
- **Tara's live path is proven for ONE carry — not for continuous
  operation.** Slice 3 built her leg to exactly the Slice 2 standard
  (seat registered, bridge configured for thread `6ad9ba71`,
  acceptance gate and metrics proven against the fake thread adapter),
  and on 2026-11-10 the first live carry completed end to end: the
  staged probe `KNIGHTS-2026-11-10-02` was posted into her real
  ChatGPT thread and her reply was carried back onto the bus,
  byte-exact on both legs (`evidence/relay-e1-live-carry-2026-11-10.json`).
  What is NOT true: there is no automated live adapter or daemon for
  Tara — the carry was browser-mediated Shape A operated by Knights,
  executed once; the bridge CLI has no live ChatGPT adapter (it fails
  closed as not-built). Continuous operation still rides on the box
  deployment (transfer Phase 4, stalled), and the register's "first
  100 carries" scale target remains open. Vance is NOT connected — no
  adapter exists for him; he is Slice 4 of the design
  (`docs/DESIGN.md` §8). The second Tara account (design open
  question) remains unverified and untouched.
- **`docs/bridge-design-slice2.md` describes a different instance state**
  (a bus on the Oracle box at `100.123.181.18:8799`, Tights connected
  there, Knights' token unminted). That state is **not verified from
  Knights' side** and does not match the local instance this file's
  claims are proven against, where Tights is still a reserved slot.
  The design's rulings (Sol's thread `6aee18e6`, Shape A, traffic
  classes) are followed; its instance claims are not adopted.
- **The bus is NOT reachable from other machines yet.** The first
  deployment binds `127.0.0.1` on Knights' VM because this VM has no
  directly bindable tailnet interface (its Tailscale access runs through
  a proxy). Cross-machine reachability, and the permanent bus host
  (design Open Question 4 — Knights' VM suffered two external process
  kills on 2026-11-09), are **undecided and not established**.
- **A delivery receipt does NOT mean a seat read or accepted anything.**
  `DELIVERED` = the addressed seat's client picked the message up.
  `ACKED` = the seat's client explicitly acknowledged it. Neither means
  a commission was agreed to; the team's ACK-first filing discipline is
  unchanged, and filings remain the system of record until Tights rules
  a class of traffic bus-native.
- **Message bodies are NOT encrypted at rest in Slice 1.** State files
  sit under operator filesystem permissions (state dir 0700, token files
  0600). Bodies are coordination text only — the ingest filter refuses
  credential-shaped content — but anyone with read access to the host's
  state directory can read queued bodies.
- **There is NO uptime guarantee.** One stdlib process on one VM, with a
  restart wrapper and on-disk queues: crashes and host churn cost
  downtime, not messages. Nothing already queued is lost across a
  restart (state is fsync'd JSON + the append-only chain), but "the
  seats can talk at all times" is the requirement the design serves —
  it is not yet a measured availability claim.
- **Presence is soft state.** `online` means "heartbeat within 120 s"
  in a JSON file; heartbeats are deliberately not part of the hash
  chain. Presence can lag; the message log cannot be edited silently.
- **The MCP surface is a subset only.** `POST /mcp` implements
  `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` and `tools/call` for the five
  `relay_*` tools — nothing else. There is NO streaming, NO
  resources/prompts surface, and NO push notifications (the Agent
  Cards say so: `streaming: false`, `pushNotifications: false`).
- **Agent Cards are discovery documents, nothing more.** They carry
  no credentials and grant no access: reading a card does not mint,
  reveal, or substitute for a seat token, and every MCP or native
  call still requires the calling seat's own bearer token.
- **The A2A task lifecycle is NOT implemented.** There are no
  `tasks/send`, `tasks/get` or sibling A2A task endpoints; the A2A
  side of the surface is Agent Card discovery only. Message exchange
  itself runs over MCP tools (or the native API) with the bus's own
  QUEUED / DELIVERED / ACKED states, not A2A task states.
