# GROUND_TRUTH — savage-api-atlas

What this repository actually does, component by component, with claim
states. Written 2026-11-10 from the code and from runs executed that day.

## Components

| Component | State |
|---|---|
| `ingest.py` — fetch + parse | **verified** — run 2026-11-10 against the live catalog README: 2,338 entries, 51 categories, 0 rows skipped as unparseable. Parses only `### Category` sections carrying the five-column API/Description/Auth/HTTPS/CORS header; handles both header spellings (leading pipe or not), backticked values, trailing junk cells, and pipes inside descriptions. Sponsor tables (APILayer, MCP Servers) are not parsed as catalog entries — covered by a test. |
| `data/catalog.json` | **verified** — 6,867 entries after Phase 2: the founding 2,338 (count and per-category counts match `data/ingest-receipt.json`; largest founding categories: Development 235, Government 137, Geocoding 117) plus 4,529 federated entries that each carry a `provenance` block (2,529 APIs.guru + 2,000 Socrata). 351 categories total. |
| `federate.py` + `data/federation-receipt.json` | **verified** — run live 2026-11-10: APIs.guru parsed 2,529 / added 2,529; Socrata parsed 2,000 / added 2,000 (a declared slice: first 2,000 datasets in the source catalog's default order — the network's resultSetSize saturates at 10,000, recorded in the receipt as ">=10000"); duplicates dropped 0, URL-only collisions 0 — the two federated sources genuinely did not collide with the founding catalog on the joint (normalized URL, normalized name) key in this run. The receipt pins each payload's SHA-256 and byte count. Descriptions are normalized by a declared rule (HTML stripped, entities unescaped, whitespace collapsed, ≤500 chars) — see NOT-true below. |
| `data/sources.json` + `sources.py` + `atlas.py sources` | **verified** — registry of the 14 sources from the research Savage shared 2026-11-10 (4 directories/discovery feeds measured directly, 2 platforms, 4 government portals, 4 supporting services). Every research figure sits under `claims` with provenance + a verification state; every Atlas figure sits under `measured` with method + timestamp. First pass results: APIs.guru's 2,529 headline CONFIRMED exactly; its 108,837-endpoint figure NOT_MEASURED (reason recorded); Socrata 'api'-type assets measured at 0; data.gov organizations measured at 109 while its '450+ APIs / 25 agencies' claims are NOT_MEASURED (unit mismatch, reasons recorded); OpenAlex's works count NOT_MEASURED (free shared-IP budget exhausted — the API's own 429 said so); World Bank 29,544 indicators / 71 sources, NCBI 38 databases, Google Discovery 543 APIs — all counted from the services' own endpoints. `sources.py validate_sources` enforces the separation, and tests prove a claim figure copied into a measured field is caught. |
| `atlas.py probe` over federated entries | **verified** — the probe layer works over federated entries unchanged: 2026-11-10 spot probes of one APIs.guru entry (1Forge Finance APIs → its OpenAPI document) and one Socrata entry (Dallas Police Active Calls → its SODA endpoint) both returned alive/200 and were appended to the chain (58 entries, re-verified). |
| `data/ingest-receipt.json` | **verified** — records source URL, fetch timestamp (UTC), SHA-256 `baefd1738848a9dbbbf2b373501212cbbfb726daff24e895547d3f12c4c148c7` of the exact bytes parsed, byte count 351,859, and upstream HEAD pin `88706670ac0ffaad7bf3c6307747e2515f638bed`. |
| `atlas.py search / show / categories` | **verified** — exercised against the real catalog 2026-11-10. Ranking: exact-name > name-contains > description-contains; within a tier, no-auth then HTTPS first; deterministic regardless of input order (tested). |
| `atlas.py recommend` | **verified** — ranks matches for immediate usability: relevance tier, then HTTPS, then no-auth < apiKey < OAuth, then probed-alive ahead of unprobed. Probe state comes only from the probe log. Its known defect is measured, not hidden: on the 30-need benchmark (`benchmarks/needs-benchmark.json`) its top pick is topically usable for **0 of 30 needs** — for nearly every plain-words need it falls to its weakest relevance tier and the same no-auth/HTTPS entries (0x, 17NAS, administrative-divisons-db) win regardless of the need. `recommend` is a list-maker; the calling layer below is the reflex. |
| `call.py` + `atlas.py call` / `atlas.py benchmark` (Phase 3, the calling Atlas) | **verified** — a plain-words need goes in and a live call comes out, receipted. Retrieval: BM25F over the catalog's own name (×3) / category (×2) / description (×1) fields with need-coverage-first ordering, unioned with an independent specificity scan (matched-terms ÷ entry topical vocabulary); different needs provably return different top routes (tested). A route is callable ONLY when a probe receipt proves BOTH that it answered a keyless GET and that the stored URL is a live endpoint — catalog auth claims alone never establish callability, and repo/doc-host URLs (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, app-hosting domains) are never endpoints. Execution is stdlib HTTP with a 10 s timeout and manual redirect handling; failures are named (`http 401`, `url: <reason>`, exception names), never laundered. Failover: on a failed attempt, next route in the SAME catalog category sharing a matched need term with the failed route (the semantic-equivalence rule adopted from the registry-ZIP audit), ≤3 attempts, every failure recorded in the receipt's `failover_chain`. Every call — success, failed, or refused — returns an SRE-1 receipt envelope (`schema savage/receipt-envelope/1`): the envelope layer IS savage-standard's implementation — its `canonical.py` (RFC 8785 JCS) and `envelope.py` are vendored byte-identically under `vendor/savage_standard/`, SHA-256-pinned against savage-standard main `f551ec40` by `tests/test_envelope_convergence.py`, and `call.py`'s former local JCS/digest/wrap implementations are deleted (fix #82 convergence; savage-standard's verifier natively verifies these receipts through its `atlas-call` dialect adapter, and `verify_envelope` here runs the same envelope legs plus the dialect legs locally): need, route chosen, attempts, failover chain, status, latency, SHA-256 response-body digest; `verify_envelope` re-verifies native + envelope digests and gate consistency from the envelope's own contents; `--log` appends envelopes to the hash-chained `data/call-log.jsonl`. Benchmark (run live 2026-11-10, artifact `benchmarks/needs-benchmark.json`): BEFORE recommend = **0 usable across 0 of 30 needs**; AFTER calling Atlas = **24 usable across 24 of 30 needs** (relevance-gated: a live 200 from a route matching <1/3 of the need's terms counts as served-but-off-topic, not usable; 3 more needs were served live but excluded by that gate; 2 needs refused — no callable route; 1 need failed with every attempt named). All 30 benchmark envelopes re-verify from their own contents. |
| `atlas.py probe` + `data/probe-log.jsonl` | **verified** — day-one batch of 56 no-auth + HTTPS entries (Finance, Cryptocurrency, Weather, Geocoding, Machine Learning, News; ≤10 per category): **46 alive (HTTP 200–399), 4 HTTP-error (403, 403, 404, 503), 6 unreachable (timeouts / connection closed)**. Phase 3 grew the log through the same mechanism: +1 spot probe (OpenWeatherMap, alive/200) and +62 needs-targeted candidates (the top-ranked no-auth, non-repo-host routes per benchmark need): 53 alive / 1 HTTP-error / 8 unreachable. **121 receipts total; `atlas.py verifylog` re-verified the full chain 2026-11-10.** Each result is a hash-chained receipt (prev-hash + entry hash). Tamper control is covered by a test: editing a logged status breaks verification at that entry. |
| `freshness.py` + `atlas.py freshness` + freshness blocks in `benchmarks/needs-benchmark.json` (ATLAS-E2, 2026-11-15) | **verified** — temporal proof for needs: every benchmark need now carries `observed_at` (read from its own ATLAS-E1 receipt envelope's `recorded_at`, cross-checked against the native receipt's `recorded_at`; disagreement → UNKNOWN), a computed verification age, and a verdict against a declared 7-day window (CURRENT ≤ window, STALE older, UNKNOWN where no honest timestamp exists). Metric, measured exactly as pre-declared: BEFORE (pre-E2 landed artifact) needs carrying a computed freshness verdict = **0 of 30 (0%)**; AFTER = **30 of 30 (100%)** — distribution at annotation time (evaluated 2026-11-16T03:01:31Z): AFTER rows CURRENT 30 / STALE 0 / UNKNOWN 0 (receipts recorded 2026-11-10T20:39–20:40Z, age ≈5.3 days); BEFORE (recommend) rows UNKNOWN 30 / 30 — a recommendation verifies nothing, so no timestamp is claimed for it. Planted-stale control (scratch copy only, receipt timestamps aged 30 days): recomputed STALE **30 of 30 (100%)**; a planted lying stored verdict ("CURRENT" on aged receipts) is ignored by the recompute path; a timestamp-stripped legacy copy recomputes UNKNOWN 30 of 30. Verdicts are recomputable from the artifacts alone: `atlas.py freshness` ignores stored blocks and recomputes from the embedded receipts against an explicit `--now`; the same artifact honestly recomputes STALE 30/30 when evaluated 2026-12-10. `run_benchmark` annotates fresh reports (a just-run verification is stamped at verification time — `perform_call`'s `recorded_at` — and annotates CURRENT at age ~0); `atlas.py call` prints the fresh receipt's freshness; `atlas.py benchmark` prints the distribution. Freshness blocks live OUTSIDE the receipt envelopes: all 30 envelope digests and the convergence pins are unchanged (suite-proven). 16 new tests in `tests/test_freshness.py`; suite 69 → 85, zero regressions. |
| `vendor/savage_standard/` — vendored savage-standard envelope layer (`canonical.py`, `envelope.py`), byte-identical to savage-standard main `f551ec40` | **verified** (fix #82) — SHA-256 pins asserted by `tests/test_envelope_convergence.py` on every run; the files carry a DO-NOT-EDIT header naming savage-standard as the source of truth. Only the producer-side twin is vendored; the verifier, dialect adapters and signing stack are NOT copied — they live canonically in savage-standard. |
| `tests/` | **verified** — 85 stdlib unittest tests (69 pre-ATLAS-E2, + 16 in `tests/test_freshness.py`: the pure CURRENT/STALE/UNKNOWN computation incl. the exact window boundary and future-timestamp rejection, receipt timestamp cross-checking, the landed-artifact 0%→100% metric, the planted-stale and legacy-UNKNOWN scratch controls, stored-verdict distrust, and run_benchmark annotation; 58 pre-convergence, + 11 in `tests/test_envelope_convergence.py`: vendored-byte pins, fresh-receipt verification under the converged path, wrap parity against the canonical wrap, digest-core signature exclusion, Knights' two tamper controls, and all 30 landed benchmark receipts re-verifying standalone and as a chain), all passing 2026-11-10, no live network (probe and executor tests use a local fixture HTTP server on 127.0.0.1; parser tests use an excerpt of real README lines and fixtures cut from the real APIs.guru / Socrata payloads, committed under `tests/fixtures/`; registry tests validate the real `data/sources.json` plus synthetic registries that attempt claim→measured leaks; call tests cover retrieval variance across needs, the probe-evidence allowlist, failover recording, receipt verification + tamper rejection, and refusal when nothing is callable). |
| `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (CI gate) | **verified** — added 2026-11-10 (PR #4, branch `ci/atlas-tests-gate`): the repo's first Actions workflow. On `pull_request`, `push` to `main`, and `workflow_dispatch` it runs the full suite (`python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, Python 3.12 on `ubuntu-latest` — 3.12 is the version every module header and the README declare). Before this file the repo had **zero** workflows (Actions API: `total_count: 0`) and the suite ran only locally. Green run: PR #4's check, Actions run **42900973373**, job 130126518350 `unittest (Python 3.12)` — **success**, all 58 tests. The gate is proven able to fail, not decorative: negative-control run **42901157460** (throwaway branch `ci-gate-negative-control`, PR #5, closed unmerged and branch deleted after the run) carried the identical workflow plus ONE deliberately broken assertion (`tests/test_call.py` `TestNeedsFixture.test_fixture_shape`: unique fixture-id count asserted equal to `-1`) — the run's conclusion was **failure**, with the failure isolated to exactly that test (locally reproduced against the identical tree: `FAILED (failures=1)`, the other 57 passing). One platform limit found while gathering this evidence: Actions registers workflows only from the default branch, so `workflow_dispatch` returns 404 for a branch-only workflow — the negative control therefore ran as a throwaway PR's check, which exercises the same job end-to-end. Honest limit: this workflow makes the gate RUN; branch protection requiring the `unittest (Python 3.12)` check before merge is a repository-settings (operator/governance) act and is **NOT done** — see NOT-true. |

## How to verify

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests     # all green, offline
python3 ingest.py --federate               # re-ingest + federate; receipts refresh
python3 atlas.py categories                # 6,867 total, 351 categories
python3 atlas.py verifylog                 # probe chain: 121 entries, hashes verified
python3 atlas.py call "current weather forecast for a city"   # live call + SRE-1 receipt
python3 atlas.py benchmark                 # re-run the 30-need BEFORE/AFTER (live; overwrites benchmarks/needs-benchmark.json)
python3 atlas.py freshness                 # ATLAS-E2: recompute every need's freshness verdict from its receipt alone (offline)
python3 atlas.py freshness --now 2026-11-11T20:40:00Z   # replay verdicts at an explicit reference time
python3 atlas.py sources                   # sources layer: claims vs measurements
python3 atlas.py probe --category Weather --noauth --https --limit 3
```

## What is NOT true

- **Freshness is a statement about a receipt, not about an API (ATLAS-E2).**
  CURRENT means only: this need's verification call was recorded at
  `observed_at`, and that moment is inside the declared 7-day window
  relative to the recorded `evaluated_at_utc`. It does NOT mean the
  route still answers now, still serves the same data, or was ever
  fit for the need (the relevance gate is a separate audit). Verdicts
  are time-relative: recomputing the identical artifact after the
  window passes honestly flips CURRENT → STALE, and that flip is the
  feature, not drift. Stored freshness blocks are a display cache
  OUTSIDE the receipt envelopes — they are not digest-bound and are
  never trusted; `atlas.py freshness` recomputes from the receipts
  alone. Legacy needs get no borrowed time: the founding catalog's
  ingest/federation receipts (2026-11-10) timestamp the CATALOG's
  claims, not any need's verification, so they are never used as a
  need's `observed_at` — a need with no call receipt, or a receipt
  with no `recorded_at`, is UNKNOWN. The only stamping path is a
  verification that actually runs.
- **Envelope convergence is pinned-vendored, not imported (fix #82).**
  savage-standard is not published as an installable package anywhere
  in the estate, so this repo vendors its `canonical.py` +
  `envelope.py` byte-identically (SHA-256-pinned in the suite) instead
  of depending on it — Atlas keeps its zero-third-party-dependency,
  stdlib-only posture. If savage-standard's envelope source changes
  and this repo does not re-vendor, the pin test fails loudly; it does
  not silently drift. The dialect-leg logic exists in two maintained
  places by design — savage-standard's `atlas-call` adapter (canonical)
  and `call.py`'s local twin (so the Atlas verifies standalone) — with
  verdict parity pinned on the 30 landed benchmark receipts; the
  envelope layer itself exists in exactly one implementation.
- **Atlas envelopes are issued unsigned.** The custody stack exists
  (fix #78) and an Atlas envelope CAN be wrapped and signed at the
  canonical layer — proven in savage-standard's suite under a throwaway
  key — but no production Atlas envelope is signed, because no real
  estate key has been minted (operator act, unchanged by this fix).
  Fresh envelopes state this in their boundary text; the 30 landed
  benchmark envelopes still carry the pre-#78 boundary text ("custody
  still owed") — they are historical artifacts and verify exactly as
  issued.
- **The standard's verifier does not check Atlas chain sequence.**
  `chain.prev_digest` is bound by the envelope digest on both paths,
  but sequence agreement (each envelope's pointer equals the previous
  envelope's digest) is checked only by this repo's chain-aware paths
  (`verify_call_log`, the benchmark chain test), because a
  single-envelope verifier is not shown a sequence. A bare atlas-call
  native receipt (no envelope) is NOT verifiable by savage-standard —
  the native is not self-describing; convergence is envelope-level.
- **Catalog claims are unverified until probed.** Auth / HTTPS / CORS in
  `catalog.json` are what the public-apis contributors published. The
  catalog even contradicts itself in places (e.g. an entry whose link is
  `http://` while its HTTPS column says Yes). Ingest preserves claims
  as-is; only a probe receipt says anything about reality.
- **A probe proves one thing only:** the entry URL answered (or did not)
  once, at the recorded time, with the recorded status, to a bare GET —
  often the URL is a documentation page, not an API endpoint. A probe does
  NOT prove the API works, is fit for any purpose, honors its claimed
  auth/CORS behavior, or will answer tomorrow.
- **Unprobed means unprobed.** 2,282 of 2,338 entries have no probe
  receipt yet. `recommend` ranks them below probed-alive entries but still
  surfaces them — their claims are all anyone knows about them so far.
- **Dead links are left in, on purpose.** The 10 sampled entries that did
  not answer successfully are findings, recorded in the probe log; the
  index does not silently delete or "fix" catalog entries.
- **No API keys are stored, requested, or handled anywhere in this tool.**
  Probe targets that require auth are never probed with credentials.
- **Probing is a sample, not coverage.** The day-one batch is capped at 56
  entries in 6 categories chosen for Savage project relevance; it is not
  evidence about the other 45 categories.
- Nothing here calls any listed API on behalf of a project, manages
  accounts, or wraps the listed APIs — it is a registry and a checker.
- **The Socrata federation is a slice, not the network.** 2,000 datasets
  in the source catalog's default order, out of ≥10,000 (its counter
  saturates at 10,000 — the true total is not known to this tool). The
  slice rule is declared in `federate.py` and the receipt.
- **Federated fields are claims with weaker provenance than they look.**
  APIs.guru entries record auth/CORS as "unknown" because the directory
  does not state them per-API; Socrata entries record auth "none" on the
  platform's keyless-read design. Neither is a probe result. Federated
  descriptions are normalized (HTML stripped, truncated at 500 chars) —
  they are NOT the sources' verbatim text; the founding ingest's entries
  remain verbatim.
- **The calling layer calls exactly one thing, one way.** A call is a
  bare keyless GET of the single URL stored in the catalog entry — no
  query parameters, no POST bodies, no auth headers, ever. Nothing
  constructs endpoints: Socrata dataset URLs and APIs.guru spec-document
  URLs are called as stored or not at all. Growing what can be called
  means growing the probe log (`atlas.py probe`), never guessing URLs.
- **A success receipt proves less than it looks like.** It proves the
  stored URL answered HTTP 2xx–3xx at call time and that the response
  body hashed to the recorded digest. It does NOT prove the response is
  the data the need wanted — topical relevance is the retrieval layer's
  claim, and the benchmark audits it separately (its relevance gate
  excluded 3 live 200s as off-topic). Response bodies are digested, not
  stored, so body content is NOT re-verifiable from a receipt: the
  verification ceiling for a success receipt is VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL,
  and the envelope says so in its boundary statements.
- **Per-route license is unknown.** The catalog carries no license
  field, so the semantic-equivalence failover rule's "under a permitting
  license" leg cannot be verified per route. Failover enforces the
  semantic leg (same category + shared matched need term) and receipts
  record license state as not-verified rather than asserting permission.
- **Probe coverage bounds the calling surface.** 121 of 6,867 entries
  carry probe receipts; only probe-proven routes can ever be called.
  Routes without receipts are refused even when the catalog claims
  no-auth — in the benchmark, the movies and translation needs were
  refused for exactly this reason, and one probed route answered 401 at
  call time despite its earlier alive probe (recorded as a named
  failure, not retried into a fake success).
- **The research's registry ZIP has not been retrieved.** The ChatGPT
  thread names a "SAVAGE Free API Source Registry" ZIP deliverable; it
  has not been downloaded or integrated. The sources layer here was
  built from the research's text claims plus the Atlas's own calls.
- **Platform sources are not integrations.** Composio and Activepieces
  are registered as sources with their claims labeled; the Atlas does
  not execute tools through either, holds no account with either, and
  their free-tier figures are unverified marketing claims.
- **The CI check is not yet a required merge gate.** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs the full suite on every PR and every push to `main`, and a red run is visible on the PR — but nothing in this repository's settings blocks merging on a red (or missing) check. Making the `unittest (Python 3.12)` check required is a branch-protection change under Settings → Branches — an operator/governance act that no file in this repo can perform. Until that act happens, the gate is enforced by convention, not by GitHub.
- **Two headline counts are honestly absent.** OpenAlex's works count
  and data.gov's catalog total appear nowhere as Atlas figures, because
  they could not be measured from this host on 2026-11-10 (reasons in
  `data/sources.json`). The research's versions of those numbers exist
  only under `claims`, labeled — dataset-scale counts (data.europa.eu,
  data.gov) are never cited as API supply.

# GROUND_TRUTH — savage-api-compass

What this repository actually does, component by component, with claim
states. Written 2026-11-10 from the code and from runs executed that day.

## Components

| Component | State |
|---|---|
| `ingest.py` — fetch + parse | **verified** — run 2026-11-10 against the live catalog README: 2,338 entries, 51 categories, 0 rows skipped, 0 HTTPS anomalies. Reproduces the savage-api-atlas catalog exactly (same upstream SHA-256 `baefd173…4c148c7`, same 2,338 keys, zero field diffs). Parses only `### Category` sections carrying the five-column API/Description/Auth/HTTPS/CORS header; handles both header spellings (leading pipe or not), backticked values, trailing empty/badge/junk cells, and pipes inside descriptions (validated against a known auth-token set). Sponsor tables (APILayer, MCP Servers) are not parsed as catalog entries — covered by a test. |
| `data/catalog/chunk-*.json` | **verified** — generated by that run; count and per-category counts match `data/ingest-receipt.json`. Largest categories: Development 235, Government 137, Geocoding 117, Games & Comics 114, Finance 109, Cryptocurrency 106. Chunks reassemble to the receipt's `assembled_sha256`. |
| `data/ingest-receipt.json` | **verified** — records source URL, fetch timestamp (UTC), SHA-256 of the exact bytes parsed, byte count 351,859, and upstream HEAD pin `88706670ac0ffaad7bf3c6307747e2515f638bed` (operator-supplied, verified to exist via the GitHub API; the unauthenticated branches API is rate-limited from this VM, so the script never invents a pin). |
| `compass.py search / recommend / show / categories` | **verified** — exercised against the real catalog. Ranking: relevance tier (exact name > all terms in name > all terms in name+description > any term), then probed-alive first, then HTTPS, then auth ease (none < apiKey < OAuth < other), then name/URL for determinism. Every result line prints claim state AND probe state separately. |
| `compass.py probe` + `data/probe-log/part-*.jsonl` | **verified** — full-catalog run 2026-11-10 (see run record in the PR body / probe summary). Each result is a hash-chained receipt (prev-hash + entry hash); `compass.py verifylog` re-verifies the chain. Tamper control is covered by a test: editing a logged status breaks verification at that entry. |
| `compass.py diff` | **verified** — compares two catalogs by (category, name, URL): added / removed / changed with field-level detail. Against the savage-api-atlas catalog the first diff is zero-change (same upstream SHA), which verifies reproducibility. |
| `compass.py contradictions` | **verified** — claim-vs-reality audit over probed entries: (a) claims HTTPS yes but URL is http://, (b) claims HTTPS no but URL is https://, (c) claims no-auth but probe got 401/403, (d) probe redirected to a different host (informational). CORS is NOT checked: a bare GET without an Origin header cannot observe CORS behavior, so the claim stays a claim. |
| `tests/` | **verified** — 20 stdlib unittest tests, all passing 2026-11-10, no live network (probe tests use a local fixture HTTP server on 127.0.0.1; parser tests use crafted rows in the shape of real README lines). |

## How to verify

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests     # all green, offline
python3 ingest.py                          # re-ingest; receipt + counts refresh
python3 compass.py categories              # 2,338 total, 51 categories
python3 compass.py verifylog               # probe chain: N entries, hashes verified
python3 compass.py diff --other <other-catalog.json>
python3 compass.py contradictions
python3 compass.py recommend "free weather data"
```

## What is NOT true

- **Catalog claims are unverified until probed.** Auth / HTTPS / CORS in
  `catalog.json` are what the public-apis contributors published. Ingest
  preserves claims as-is; only a probe receipt says anything about reality.
- **A probe proves one thing only:** the entry URL answered (or did not)
  once, at the recorded time, with the recorded status, to a bare HEAD
  (GET fallback on 405/501) — often the URL is a documentation page, not
  an API endpoint. A probe does NOT prove the API works, is fit for any
  purpose, honors its claimed auth/CORS behavior, or will answer tomorrow.
- **Probes run through this VM's egress proxy.** A connection reset or
  timeout may reflect the proxy, not the target host. The recorded error
  string is the observation; `unreachable` means "did not answer us from
  here, this time", nothing stronger.
- **Dead links are left in, on purpose.** Entries that did not answer
  successfully are findings, recorded in the probe log; the index does not
  silently delete or "fix" catalog entries.
- **No API keys are stored, requested, or handled anywhere in this tool.**
  Probe targets that require auth are never probed with credentials; a
  401/403 on a no-auth claim is recorded as a contradiction finding.
- Nothing here calls any listed API on behalf of a project, manages
  accounts, or wraps the listed APIs — it is a registry and a checker.

## Live layer (added 2026-11-10)

- **Registry:** 14 sources from the Savage Free API Source Registry
  (research snapshot 2026-11-10), ingested as reference data
  (`data/live-sources.json`, source SHA-256
  `2d0b591485c234d12e2b257f24b7b33848bd1213a675e1d910a09c408d6df1df`).
  Registry counts (1,722 toolkits, 12,210 APIs, 1.8M datasets) are
  CLAIMS from that snapshot, never verified numbers.
- **Keyless callable (7):** apis-guru, socrata, data-europa, openalex,
  world-bank, ncbi, google-discovery. **Key-required (4, never
  called):** composio, korea-data-go-kr, us-api-data-gov, india-ogd.
  **Mixed (1, page only):** embl-ebi. **Runtime (1):** activepieces.
  **Catalog (1):** public-apis.
- **Live probe:** the 8 keyless/mixed endpoints probed through the
  router; receipts in `data/live-probe-log.jsonl`. The package's own
  smoke test (run first-hand before building) gave 5/6 alive with
  OpenAlex 429 — the rate-limit is real on this egress; a 429 is
  recorded as rate-limited, honored via Retry-After, and re-probed
  once. A live 200 proves the endpoint answered once, not that it
  will answer tomorrow or within quota.
- **Calls:** every `compass.py call` / POST /call leaves a receipt in
  `data/call-log.jsonl` (need, capability, routes tried in order,
  result summary). Keyed estate routes (Stripe, Brev, PolyAI, Quo,
  OpenAI) are registered with `callable: false` — the Atlas names
  them and the key holder, never calls them.
- **Ranking fixes (2026-11-10, disclosed):** the head-to-head run
  showed sentence queries returning the same three entries for every
  need (no stopwords: "a" matched almost every description) and tier-3
  ranking going alphabetical (one stray term beat five matched terms).
  Fixed need-independently: a stopword list in `tokenize`, and a
  within-tier term-count tie-break. Tier ORDER is unchanged. Both
  fixes are covered by regression tests. Knights' `recommend` has the
  same stopword behavior (same top-3 for all 25 sentence needs,
  verified first-hand); that is their finding, not ours to fix.
- **Full-catalog probe (2026-11-10):** 2,335/2,338 entries probed
  (3 entries have no usable URL — trailing-space link residue, same in
  Knights' catalog). alive 1,929, http-error 177, unreachable 229.
  Re-probe agreement vs Knights' 56: 54/56. Contradictions: 293
  (a=28, b=31, c=28, d=206). Diff vs Knights' catalog: 0/0/0.

# GROUND_TRUTH.md — savage-standard

Code-proven state of this repository, component by component. Verify any
line of it by reading the named file and running the named command.

## What this repo is

The SIA-E2 "One Promotion Standard" build: a common receipt envelope
(SRE-1) plus a universal verifier for the seven receipt dialects minted
across the Savage estate, plus the claims-gate inventory that baselines
SIA-E2's second metric. Python 3 standard library only; zero third-party
dependencies (`pyproject.toml` declares `dependencies = []`).

SIA-E1 "The Recomputable Benchmark" (this build) adds the first
EXTERNAL dialect: `helm-benchmark`, a recompute adapter for a published
benchmark result from a system Savage does not own — Stanford CRFM's
HELM classic v0.4.0 — with the recompute minter in
`savage_standard/helm.py`. See the SIA-E1 lines in the component table
and Metrics below.

The key-custody build (this build) closes the envelope-signature
defect named in earlier revisions of this file: SRE-1 envelopes can
now carry a real issuer signature, checked by the universal verifier
against a public key registry committed in this repo
(`savage_standard/signing.py`, `savage_standard/rsa.py`,
`savage_standard/key_registry.json`). Private keys are generated and
held by the operator OUTSIDE any repository; only public entries are
committed. See the custody lines in the component table, Metrics, and
"What is NOT true" — in particular: no real estate key has been minted
yet, so no production envelope is signed today.

## Component state

| Component | State | How to verify |
|---|---|---|
| `savage_standard/canonical.py` — JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalizer with ECMAScript number serialization; Python sorted-compact; Starr canonicalJson; fixed-order JS stringify | VERIFIED against producer-minted artifacts | Test suite recomputes real marketplace entry hashes / receipt digests, the sia-v6-core chain hash, Breakthrough record digests, and the Starr receipt hash from fixture bytes and matches them exactly. |
| `savage_standard/envelope.py` — SRE-1 envelope: wrap, digest, structural checks | VERIFIED | `tests/test_savage_standard.py::TestEnvelope` (wrap→verify VERIFIED; tampered native → REJECTED; tampered envelope field → REJECTED). The digest core now also excludes the `signatures` member (the signature is computed over the digest); envelopes without one digest byte-identically to before, which the fixture suite proves on every run. |
| `savage_standard/rsa.py` — RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256 (RFC 8017): Miller-Rabin key generation, EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 encoding, sign/verify — Savage-original, stdlib only | VERIFIED, incl. against the reference implementation | `tests/test_signing.py::TestRsa` (EMSA block asserted byte-exact against the RFC 8017 construction; sign/verify round-trip; garbage rejected). Cross-checked against OpenSSL during development in BOTH directions: OpenSSL verified this code's signature, and this code verified OpenSSL's. Classical scheme — NOT post-quantum, not constant-time (see "What is NOT true"). |
| `savage_standard/signing.py` + `savage_standard/key_registry.json` — estate key custody: public registry (committed), operator-side key generation (private key written mode-0600 to an operator-chosen path outside any repo, never copied by this code), envelope signing, and the verifier's signature legs | VERIFIED as a mechanism; NO real estate key exists yet | `tests/test_signing.py` (17 tests: signed envelope VERIFIED end to end; the pre-custody re-digest forgery REJECTED; tampered signature REJECTED; wrong public key REJECTED; unknown/revoked key caps at VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL; unsigned envelopes unchanged; a signed marketplace-delivery envelope verifies with its pair passed as a side input — the pair itself travels under the signature only via the `marketplace-delivery-pair` dialect, fix #81). The shipped registry holds exactly ONE entry — a throwaway DEMO key (usage `demo`) whose private half was destroyed at build time after signing `fixtures/signed-envelope-demo.json`; its leg passes with a detail stating it attests nothing. |
| `savage_standard/dialects.py` — seven estate adapters: marketplace-delivery, siav6core-benchmark, relay-event-log, breakthrough-evidence, siav6-benchmark-manifest, ceros-promotion, starr-bounce | VERIFIED per the coverage table in the PR body | `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → genuine PASS + tamper FAIL per dialect. |
| `savage_standard/dialects.py::verify_marketplace_pair` + `verify.py` detection — the `marketplace-delivery-pair` dialect: a marketplace delivery-ledger receipt PAIR (payment + delivery) is a first-class native of the verifier, detected by its `savage/delivery-receipt-pair/1` marker or by the ledger's unmarked `receiptsFor()` shape | VERIFIED (fix #81, 2026-11-10) | `tests/test_delivery_pair.py` (12 tests): both committed fixture pairs verify with every binding leg passing (the minted pair reaches VERIFIED with its artifact bytes supplied); a signed envelope over a real pair verifies VERIFIED with the signature leg passing; an edited amount, an honestly-re-digested payment, a member swap, and a malformed member are all REJECTED; an unsigned pair envelope adds no signature leg. See Metrics below. |
| `savage_standard/dialects.py::verify_atlas_call` + `verify.py` envelope routing — the `atlas-call` dialect: savage-api-atlas call receipts verify natively. Envelope-embedded only: detection requires issuer dialect `atlas-call` AND subject native_schema `savage/atlas-call/1`; the adapter recomputes the producer's four dialect legs (gate-verdict-vs-native, body-digest-pointer, body-content, result-consistency) | VERIFIED (fix #82, 2026-11-10) | `tests/test_atlas_call.py` (12 tests) against three genuine landed benchmark receipts (`tests/fixtures/atlas-call-envelopes.json`, copied verbatim from savage-api-atlas `benchmarks/needs-benchmark.json` at atlas main `d9c24a21`): success/refused/failed envelopes verify VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL with the dialect legs passing (body-content unverifiable by the producer's design); claim-flip and native-digest-zeroed REJECTED (Knights' 2026-11-10 controls); honest-redigest status/body/http-status tampers fail their dialect legs; a signed atlas envelope verifies with the signature leg passing and its re-digest forgery REJECTED. The pre-convergence producer source travels at `vendor/atlas_call_v1.py`, pinned by `dialects.ATLAS_CALL_SOURCE_SHA256`. See Metrics below. |
| `savage_standard/helm.py` — SIA-E1 recompute minter: HELM per-instance Stat merge + native receipt (`savage/external-benchmark-recompute/1`) | VERIFIED on a real external artifact | `gunzip -dc fixtures/helm-boolq-per-instance-stats.json.gz > /tmp/per_instance_stats.json`, then `savage-verify recompute /tmp/per_instance_stats.json …` reproduces `fixtures/helm-boolq-receipt.json`: 874.0/1000.0 = 0.874. (The fixture is committed gzip-compressed — GitHub's git-blobs API refuses the raw 64.7 MB blob; the decompressed bytes are exactly the SHA-256 pin in the receipt.) |
| `savage_standard/dialects.py::verify_helm` — the eighth dialect, `helm-benchmark`: re-derives the external claim from supplied public artifact bytes | VERIFIED | Suite `TestHelm` (6 tests): genuine VERIFIED native + envelope; no-artifact VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL; edited recomputed value, edited published value, and swapped artifact all REJECTED. |
| `savage_standard/verify.py` — dialect detection + verdict assembly (VERIFIED / VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL / REJECTED / UNVERIFIABLE) | VERIFIED | Same suite; garbage input returns UNVERIFIABLE, never a pass. Envelope path additionally emits an `envelope-signature` leg when a `signatures` member is present (pass / fail / unverifiable per the registry); unsigned envelopes produce no such leg and keep their exact pre-custody verdicts. |
| `savage_standard/cli.py` — `savage-verify` CLI (verify / wrap / recompute / claims / keygen / sign; `--keys` registry override on verify) | VERIFIED | Smoke-run in the PR body; exit codes 0/1/2 by verdict. `tests/test_signing.py::TestDemoAndCustody::test_cli_keygen_sign_verify` drives keygen→sign→verify end to end. |
| `savage_standard/claims.py` — claims-gate inventory | VERIFIED as an enumeration | Rows cite their sources (site repo main `4efd6486`, marketplace `catalog.json`, Stripe registry, fix-program results). The BEFORE number is definitional — the definition is printed in the module docstring so it can be argued with. |
| `fixtures/` — real artifacts from the fix program (and, for SIA-E1, one real external artifact) | VERIFIED | `fixtures/PROVENANCE.md` names each artifact's origin. |
| `pyproject.toml` + `MANIFEST.in` — packaging: setuptools backend, `savage-verify` console script, `key_registry.json` package-data; the sdist grafts the full evidence tree (`fixtures/`, `tests/`, `vendor/`) plus this file | VERIFIED (fix #85, 2026-11-10) | From a clean venv: `pip install .` in a checkout succeeds; `savage-verify fixtures/signed-envelope-demo.json` from an unrelated cwd prints the same verdict + legs as the from-source run (byte-identical output, measured); the suite passes 74/74 against the INSTALLED package and 74/74 from an extracted sdist. BEFORE fix #85 the sdist shipped the test modules without any of their data (extracted-sdist suite: 56 tests ran, 52 FileNotFoundError errors). The wheel remains runtime-only; the package is installable but NOT published to any index, and no consumer imports it yet (see "What is NOT true"). |

## Metrics (Evolution Rule v2)

- Fix #85 packaging (2026-11-10; BEFORE measured on the pristine tree
  @ `b12cb607`, version 0.4.0): the wheel path already worked — a clean
  venv `pip install .` succeeded, the `savage-verify` console script
  verified both committed fixtures with output byte-identical to the
  from-source run, a keygen→sign→verify round-trip under a throwaway
  key returned VERIFIED with the signature leg passing, and the suite
  passed 74/74 against the installed package. What was broken was the
  SOURCE distribution: the sdist shipped the four test modules but
  none of their data — no `fixtures/` tree, no
  `tests/fixtures/atlas-call-envelopes.json`, no
  `vendor/atlas_call_v1.py`, not even this file — so the published
  source artifact could not reproduce the repo's own verification:
  extracted-sdist suite **"Ran 56 tests … FAILED (errors=52)"**, every
  error a FileNotFoundError for a missing fixture. AFTER (version
  0.5.0): `MANIFEST.in` grafts the evidence tree into the sdist;
  extracted-sdist suite **74/74 OK**; clean-venv install of the fixed
  tree reproduces the byte-identical fixture verdicts and the 74/74
  against-installed suite; from-source suite unchanged at 74/74. No
  module, digest, or verdict changed — packaging metadata, this file,
  and the README only. Build backend unchanged (setuptools); runtime
  dependencies still `[]`.
- Fix #82 Atlas envelope convergence (2026-11-10; BEFORE measured on
  the pristine trees — savage-standard @ `f551ec40`, savage-api-atlas @
  `d9c24a21`): atlas-call dialect legs executed by this verifier on a
  genuine Atlas receipt **0 → 4** (gate-verdict-vs-native,
  body-digest-pointer, body-content, result-consistency; before, the
  envelope shell verified with dialect None and a single unverifiable
  dialect-detection leg); the 30 landed benchmark receipts keep their
  VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL verdicts, now WITH the dialect legs passing;
  Atlas envelopes signable under the custody stack **no → yes**
  (mechanism proven under a throwaway key; the producer's own digest
  core could not exclude a signatures member, so its verifier could
  never have accepted one); suite **62 → 74** tests, all passing. The
  producer side converged in the same fix: Atlas vendors this package's
  `canonical.py` + `envelope.py` byte-identically under
  `vendor/savage_standard/` (SHA-256-pinned in its suite) and its local
  JCS/digest/wrap implementations are deleted — one envelope
  implementation. What convergence does NOT yet mean: savage-standard
  is not published as an installable package anywhere, so the vendored
  copy is pinned-and-proven rather than imported (packaging state
  since updated by fix #85 — see its Metrics entry above; consumers
  still do not import it); and no production
  Atlas envelope is signed (no real estate key exists — see "What is
  NOT true").
- Fix #81 delivery-pair bridge (2026-11-10; BEFORE measured on the
  pre-bridge tree against a real pair minted by the ledger's own code
  from savage-marketplace main `bfaa3a18`; repro
  `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` → `tests/test_delivery_pair.py`):
  marketplace receipt pairs natively understood **0 → 1 dialect**
  (`marketplace-delivery-pair`); pair legs executed on a real pair
  **0 → 10**; signed envelopes whose signature covers the
  payment↔delivery binding **0 → mechanism proven** (VERIFIED with the
  signature leg PASS under a throwaway key; the re-digest claim forgery
  REJECTED by the signature leg); suite **50 → 62** tests, all passing.
- BEFORE: receipt dialects verifiable by a single independent tool =
  **0 of 7 (0%)** — measured from the pre-build tree (`BEFORE-MEASUREMENT.md`).
- AFTER: **7 of 7 dialects** covered by the one verifier, each with a
  genuine artifact passing and tamper controls failing loudly in the
  suite. Two dialects return VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL rather than VERIFIED
  for the reasons below — that distinction is the product working as
  designed, not a gap in the build.
- Claims gate: BEFORE **1 of 12 claim groups (8.3%)** gate-issued with
  outsider-recomputable receipts. This build does not move that number —
  it builds the instrument the number is measured with. Adoption
  (routing each line's public claims through the standard) is the
  follow-on work program.
- SIA-E1 (external recompute) BEFORE: the chosen external claim —
  HELM classic v0.4.0, BoolQ, Mistral v0.1 (7B), EM = 0.874 — had **0**
  independent recompute paths through the standard: no SRE-1 receipt
  existed for any external claim and `savage-verify` recognized no
  external dialect; an outsider's only options were trusting HELM's
  published tables or re-implementing HELM's aggregation from scratch.
- SIA-E1 AFTER: the claim is recomputed from HELM's own public
  per-instance statistics (pinned by SHA-256 in the receipt) under
  HELM's own Stat-merge rule, read from HELM's source: **recomputed
  0.874 (sum 874.0 / count 1000.0 over the run's 1,000 unperturbed
  valid instances) vs published 0.874 — MATCH, delta 0.0**; the receipt
  verifies **VERIFIED** through `savage-verify` (native and
  envelope-wrapped) with the artifact supplied, and the external-claim
  recomputability for this claim goes **0 → 1**. Suite 27 → 33 tests.
- Key custody BEFORE: envelopes carrying a verifiable signature =
  **0** — the verifier emitted no signature leg at all, and the defect
  was worse than absence: because the envelope digest is an unkeyed
  hash, an attacker who forged an envelope's claim statement, gate
  verdict, and issuer line and then honestly RE-COMPUTED the digest
  still received **VERIFIED** from the pre-custody verifier (measured
  on the pristine tree; the attack is reproduced in
  `tests/test_signing.py` as a regression test). Hash-binding alone
  cannot stop a re-digesting forger.
- Key custody AFTER: the same forgery against a signed envelope is
  **REJECTED** on the signature leg; a genuine signed envelope
  verifies end to end (signature leg pass) through the universal
  verifier; unknown or revoked keys cap the verdict at
  VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL; unsigned envelopes are byte-for-byte and
  verdict-for-verdict unchanged. Verifiable-signature envelopes go
  **0 → 1** (the committed demo fixture, signed by the destroyed demo
  key — mechanism proof, not an attestation) plus every envelope an
  operator signs after minting a real key. Suite 33 → 50 tests.

## What is NOT true

- **The package is installable but not published, and consumers still
  do not import it (fix #85).** As of 0.5.0 the package installs
  cleanly from a checkout or sdist of this repo and its sdist can
  reproduce the full suite — but it is on no package index (PyPI or
  otherwise), savage-api-atlas still vendors its pinned byte-identical
  copies of `canonical.py`/`envelope.py` rather than importing, and
  the marketplace's issuance path still resolves the verifier by path
  rather than importing the installed package. Import-based
  convergence in consumers is a separate step, gated on each
  consumer's CI being able to fetch the package.
- **SIA-E1 covers exactly ONE external claim, not external benchmarks
  in general.** The adapter speaks one published format (HELM classic
  per-instance statistics) and has been exercised on one claim (BoolQ /
  Mistral v0.1 (7B) / exact_match / valid split, HELM classic v0.4.0).
  The merge code is metric- and scenario-generic *within that format*,
  but no other HELM scenario, release, or leaderboard — and no other
  benchmark family (lm-eval, SWE-bench, WMT, …) — is covered, and no
  other external claim has a receipt. The claims-gate inventory
  (`claims.py`) is unchanged: it enumerates the estate's OWN claims,
  and this external claim is not one of them (the 1/12 number does not
  move).
- **The SIA-E1 recompute verifies HELM's aggregation, not HELM's
  measurements.** It proves the published 0.874 is the correct merge of
  HELM's published per-instance statistics under HELM's published rule.
  Whether those per-instance statistics faithfully record the model's
  raw outputs is HELM's own attestation — the receipt's publisher field
  says so, and the raw request/response artifacts (scenario_state /
  display_predictions) were not independently re-scored in this build.

- **CEROS signatures are NOT cryptographically verified here.** ML-DSA-87
  (FIPS 204) has no verifier in the Python standard library and the
  zero-dependency law forbids adding one. The adapter recomputes the
  receipt's shape, dimension total, and the exact signed-core byte form,
  and reports the signature leg UNVERIFIABLE (verdict
  VERIFIED-STRUCTURAL). The fixture receipt was confirmed genuine by the
  producer's own `verifyReceipt` at mint time; an outsider who needs the
  cryptographic leg today must run the producer's Node verifier. A
  Savage-original ML-DSA verifier is a named future build.
- **SIA-v6 per-record HMACs are NOT verifiable from artifacts.** The
  producer verifies each record's MAC in-process and persists only the
  `hmac_valid` boolean; the MAC itself is never stored. The adapter
  verifies everything that IS persisted (manifest artifact hashes, the
  certification arithmetic from the suite summary) and reports the
  record-MAC leg UNVERIFIABLE.
- **No production envelope is signed yet, and no real estate key
  exists.** The custody mechanism is built and proven, but the shipped
  registry's only entry is the throwaway demo key (private half
  destroyed). Minting the real estate key is the operator's remaining
  act: run `savage-verify keygen --key-id <id> --out <path OUTSIDE any
  repo>` on their own machine and commit ONLY the printed public entry
  to `savage_standard/key_registry.json`. Until that entry lands,
  EVO-9 marketplace receipts and all other envelopes remain hash-bound
  exactly as before — this build removes the "custody is owed" defect,
  it does not backdate signatures onto existing receipts.
- **The signature is classical RSA, NOT post-quantum, and the
  implementation is not constant-time.** RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5/SHA-256 was
  chosen because it is exactly implementable and provable with stdlib
  integer math (and cross-checks against OpenSSL); it does not advance
  the ML-DSA-87 leg named in CEROS receipts, which remains not-built
  for the same stdlib reason as before. Signing runs locally on the
  operator's machine; the private-exponent timing exposure of a local
  offline tool is accepted and stated, not hidden.
- **There is still no trusted timestamp.** A signature binds
  `recorded_at` (it can no longer be edited after signing) but the
  value remains issuer-reported — the signature proves the issuer
  attested that time, nothing more.
- **Atlas-call chain sequence is not checked here (fix #82).** An
  Atlas envelope's `chain.prev_digest` is bound by the recomputed
  envelope digest, so a rewritten pointer fails `envelope-digest`; but
  whether the pointer equals the PREVIOUS envelope's digest is a
  sequence claim this single-envelope verifier is not shown the inputs
  for — the producer's chain-aware paths (`verify_call_log`, the
  benchmark chain test) own that check. A bare atlas-call native (no
  envelope) is NOT detected as a dialect: the native is not
  self-describing, and convergence is envelope-level by design.
- **Producers do not sign at mint time yet — with one path now built,
  at this layer.** Signing is an envelope-level step (`savage-verify
  sign`, or `signing.sign_envelope`) applied after wrapping. As of fix
  #81 (2026-11-10) the EVO-9 delivery ledger's pair is the first
  issuing path the format fully covers: the pair is a native dialect
  (`marketplace-delivery-pair`), so a fulfillment-side issuance path
  exists end to end — mint the pair, form the pair native
  (`dialects.marketplace_pair_native`), wrap, sign — and is proven with
  throwaway keys in `tests/test_delivery_pair.py`. What does NOT yet
  exist: (a) any PRODUCTION signing key — the registry still holds only
  the destroyed demo key, so no production envelope can be signed until
  the operator mints the real estate key (the named operator act
  above); (b) producer-side wiring — savage-marketplace's deployed
  fulfillment code does not itself call wrap+sign at issuance; the
  marketplace side of fix #81 updates its boundary text only, and the
  ledger's bare receipts remain hash-bound exactly as before (the
  signature lives on the envelope, never on the receipt). A
  `signatures` member can also be stripped by an attacker — the result
  is an unsigned envelope whose missing signature leg is visible in the
  verifier output; whether a given surface REQUIRES signed envelopes
  is a policy for its operator, not something this format can enforce
  on a bare file.
- **No producer was modified.** Every dialect adapter re-implements its
  dialect's checks from the producer's source; producers keep minting
  exactly as before. Convergence of the *gate* (Foundry's arbiter +
  CEROS's engine + Breakthrough's checker as one issuing path) is not
  built here; this repo is the format + verifier foundation the register
  sequences first.
- **The claims BEFORE % is an inventory judgment, not a crawl of the
  whole web.** It enumerates the estate's own public surfaces (site,
  catalogs, registry, published program results) under the stated
  definition. Claims on surfaces not enumerated (e.g. the five
  off-GitHub websites whose domains are not yet recorded) are not
  counted in either direction.
- **The marketplace genuine pair is a measurement-run pair, not a real
  customer sale.** Estate revenue is $0; no production delivery receipt
  exists yet. A scratch pair harvested earlier from a verify-CLI temp
  dir fails the producer's own verifier and was excluded — see
  `fixtures/PROVENANCE.md`.
